vir: Vadbena pola Učilnica.com. Zgradba, vrsta nalog in točkovanje sledijo uradni poli splošne mature (spomladanski rok 2026, osnovna raven, izpitna pola 1), besedila, naloge in rešitve pa so naši. Uradne pole izdaja Državni izpitni center (RIC), ki ima nanje vse avtorske pravice.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter

When my mother left, my father took the only job he could find that would keep us together: keeper of the lighthouse on Carrick Point. I was eleven and furious. The nearest shop was an hour's walk away, the nearest girl my age lived on the mainland, and the school sent my lessons by post, in a brown envelope that arrived every second Tuesday with the supply boat.

My father was not a talkative man. He believed that most things could be explained with a pencil and the back of an envelope, and he drew diagrams of everything – the tides, the lamp, the reason the wind always seemed to blow straight through my bedroom wall. At first I refused to look at them. Later, when there was nothing else to look at, I began to keep them in a shoebox under my bed.

The light itself was his whole world. Every evening at sunset he climbed the hundred and twelve steps to the lamp room, polished the great glass lens until it shone, and wound the clockwork that turned it. If the clockwork stopped, he had to turn the lens by hand, all night, so that the ships could still recognise our signal: two long flashes and one short. "Every lighthouse speaks its own language," he told me. "If ours goes silent, a captain could think he is somewhere else."

That winter the clockwork broke during the worst storm in forty years. The radio was dead, the boat could not come, and my father had a fever so high that he could hardly stand. So I climbed the stairs myself. I had watched him often enough. For nine hours I pushed the heavy handle round and round, counting the flashes aloud – long, long, short – until my arms shook and my voice disappeared.

At dawn a fishing boat came into the bay, and its captain walked up to the house with a bag of oranges. He had seen our light all night, he said, and it had brought him home. He never knew who had been turning it.

My father recovered. He did not say much, but the next brown envelope from school contained, along with my maths, a diagram in his handwriting: a girl, a handle and a ship, connected by a long, careful line.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.Where did the narrator's family live?
    In a lighthouse (on Carrick Point).
  2. 1.Why did the father accept the job at the lighthouse?
  3. 2.How did the narrator receive her school lessons?
  4. 3.What did the father use to explain things?
  5. 4.Where did the narrator keep her father's drawings?
  6. 5.What did the father do to the lens every evening?
  7. 6.What was the lighthouse's signal?
  8. 7.Why was it important that the light did not go silent?
  9. 8.Why couldn't the father turn the lens himself during the storm?
  10. 9.How long did the narrator turn the handle?
  11. 10.What did the captain bring to the house?
  12. 11.How did the father show his gratitude?
naloge.rezultat:
1. To keep the family together. / So they could stay together.
2. By post. / In an envelope (by post).
3. (Pencil-drawn) diagrams. / A pencil and an envelope.
4. In a shoebox (under her bed).
5. He polished it.
6. Two long flashes and one short (flash).
7. A captain could get lost. / Captains could think they were elsewhere.
8. He had a (high) fever. / He was ill.
9. (For) nine hours.
10. A bag of oranges.
11. With a diagram (in the envelope). / He drew her a diagram.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. To keep the family together. / So they could stay together.
»the only job he could find that would keep us together« – namen, zato odgovor z to + nedoločnik ali so (that). Vprašanje »Why …?« zahteva namen ali razlog. Zveza »that would keep us together« pomeni »ki bi nas obdržala skupaj«, zato je odgovor namen: to keep the family together.
2. By post. / In an envelope (by post).
»the school sent my lessons by post« – dovolj je način: by post. »How …?« tu sprašuje po načinu. V besedilu je naveden način pošiljanja (by post), ne vsebina pošiljke.
3. (Pencil-drawn) diagrams. / A pencil and an envelope.
»most things could be explained with a pencil and the back of an envelope« in »drew diagrams of everything«. Sprejmeta se oba dela navedka, saj oče stvari razlaga s svinčnikom na hrbtni strani kuverte in z risbami (diagrams).
4. In a shoebox (under her bed).
Neposredno iz besedila: »keep them in a shoebox under my bed«. »Where« = kraj. Odgovor je kraj s predlogom (in a shoebox); »under my bed« je dodatna podrobnost, ki ni nujna.
5. He polished it.
»polished the great glass lens until it shone« – vprašanje sprašuje le po leči, ne po urnem mehanizmu. Vprašanje se nanaša na lečo (the lens); urni mehanizem (clockwork) je drugo opravilo, zato ga ne pišeš.
6. Two long flashes and one short (flash).
»two long flashes and one short« – zapiši celoten vzorec. Signal je vzorec bliskov. Če napišeš le »flashes«, odgovor ni popoln, ker ne pove, kakšen je vzorec.
7. A captain could get lost. / Captains could think they were elsewhere.
»a captain could think he is somewhere else« – odgovor parafraziraš v 1–5 besedah. »Why was it important …?« zahteva posledico, ki bi nastala: kapitan bi mislil, da je drugje, in bi zašel.
8. He had a (high) fever. / He was ill.
»a fever so high that he could hardly stand«. Razlog je bolezen: »a fever so high that he could hardly stand« = vročina tako visoka, da je komaj stal.
9. (For) nine hours.
»For nine hours I pushed the heavy handle round«. »How long« = koliko časa; odgovor je časovni podatek (nine hours), lahko s predlogom for.
10. A bag of oranges.
»walked up to the house with a bag of oranges«. Neposreden podatek iz besedila. Pazi na celoto: »a bag of oranges«, ne le »oranges«.
11. With a diagram (in the envelope). / He drew her a diagram.
Oče ne govori veliko, hvaležnost pokaže z risbo: »a diagram in his handwriting: a girl, a handle and a ship«. Oče hvaležnosti ne izrazi z besedami (»He did not say much«), ampak z risbo v kuverti. Odgovor mora povedati to dejanje.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentence parts below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence part can be used only once. There are two extra sentence parts which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (J).

Why we queue: a short history of standing in line

Few habits are as British as waiting your turn – but the queue is younger than you might think.

Visitors to Britain are often amazed by the patience of people at bus stops, [0]. The orderly queue has become part of the national image, yet historians say that for most of history people simply pushed.

The modern queue appeared in the early nineteenth century, when industrial towns grew rapidly and large crowds began to gather at shops, ticket offices and factory gates. Before that time, most people bought what they needed at markets, [1].

The habit really took root during the Second World War. Food was rationed, and every family received a book of coupons [2]. Waiting in line became a patriotic duty, and government posters encouraged people to "take your turn". Anyone who pushed in front risked the anger of the whole street.

Psychologists say that queues work because they feel fair. We are willing to wait for a long time as long as we believe that everybody is treated equally. What makes us furious is not the waiting itself [3]. Experiments show that people in a slow line become more stressed when a second, faster line opens next to them, even if their own wait does not get any longer.

Shops and theme parks have learned to use this knowledge. Some put mirrors near lifts, [4]. Others display a waiting time that is a little longer than the real one, so that customers are pleasantly surprised [5]. Disney even hires designers to plan queues that bend around corners, which prevents visitors from seeing how many people are still in front of them.

Technology is now changing the queue once again. Many restaurants send a text message when a table is ready, [6]. Online, we wait in "virtual queues" to buy concert tickets, watching a little figure walk slowly across the screen.

Some experts believe that the traditional line will soon disappear. Others are not so sure. Standing in a queue, they argue, is a small social ritual [7]. It is one of the few moments when strangers agree on a rule without anyone telling them to.

Whatever happens, the British are unlikely to give up their reputation without a fight. A recent survey found that nine out of ten adults still feel embarrassed [8]. Perhaps the queue will survive simply because nobody wants to be the first [9].

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. Awhich allowed them to buy a fixed amount of sugar, butter and meat
  2. Bbut the feeling that someone else is getting an advantage
  3. Cwhen they see somebody ignoring the line
  4. Dbecause watching your own reflection makes the wait seem shorter
  5. Ewhere bargaining and shouting were part of the fun
  6. Fso that customers can go for a walk instead of standing at the door
  7. Gto break this unwritten rule
  8. Hthat reminds us we are part of a community
  9. Iwhen the doors finally open
  10. Jwho wait calmly in the rain
  11. Kalthough nobody has ever measured it
  12. Lwhen the line moves faster than they expected
naloge.rezultat:
1. E
2. A
3. B
4. D
5. L
6. F
7. H
8. C
9. G
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. E
Pred vrzeljo so »markets«; oziralni »where« uvaja opis tržnic, kjer so barantali – nasprotje urejenega čakanja. Pred vrzeljo je samostalnik kraja (markets), zato se nadaljuje z oziralnim prislovom where. Pomen: na tržnicah je bilo barantanje del zabave, kar je nasprotje mirnega čakanja.
2. A
»a book of coupons [2]« – kuponi so omogočali nakup določene količine živil (which allowed them …). »coupons« so stvar, zato se nadaljuje z which. Kuponi so v vojni določali, koliko sladkorja, masla in mesa lahko kupiš, kar je ljudi naučilo čakati v vrsti.
3. B
»not the waiting itself [3]« zahteva drugi del zveze not … but …: but the feeling … Zveza »not X but Y« (ne X, ampak Y) se mora dokončati z but. Jezi nas občutek, da ima nekdo drug prednost, ne samo čakanje.
4. D
Ogledala ob dvigalih: razlog z because – odsev skrajša občutek čakanja. Del z because pove razlog, zakaj ogledala pomagajo: ko gledaš svoj odsev, se ti zdi čakanje krajše.
5. L
»pleasantly surprised [5]« – presenečeni so, ko se vrsta premika hitreje, kot so pričakovali. »pleasantly surprised« = prijetno presenečeni; presenetijo se, ko se vrsta premika hitreje, kot so pričakovali (prikazan čas je daljši od resničnega).
6. F
SMS, ko je miza prosta – gostje zato ne čakajo pred vrati (so that …). Zveza so that izraža namen: restavracija pošlje SMS, da se gostje lahko sprehodijo, namesto da bi stali pred vrati.
7. H
»a small social ritual [7]« + oziralni stavek that reminds us … community. »ritual« je samostalnik, zato sledi oziralni stavek s that. Pomen: obred, ki nas spomni, da smo del skupnosti.
8. C
»feel embarrassed [8]« – zadrega, ko vidijo nekoga, ki ne spoštuje vrste. »feel embarrassed« = jih je sram; del z when pove, kdaj: ko vidijo nekoga, ki ne upošteva vrste.
9. G
»the first [9]« + to + nedoločnik: the first to break this unwritten rule. »the first« se veže z nedoločnikom (the first to do something). Nihče noče biti prvi, ki bi kršil to nenapisano pravilo.

Schools ban glitter to protect the oceans

Hundreds of nurseries and primary schools across the UK have decided to stop using glitter, (0) tiny pieces of plastic end up in rivers and the sea. Teachers say the decision was not an easy one, because children love decorating cards and costumes with something (1) sparkles.

Most glitter is made from a type of plastic called PET, covered with a thin layer of aluminium. Because the pieces are so small, they pass straight through water treatment plants and are swallowed by fish, shellfish and even birds. Scientists warn that microplastics (2) been found in almost every ocean on the planet, from the surface (3) the deepest trenches.

"We used (4) buy several kilograms every year," says Sarah Holt, head teacher of a nursery in Bristol. "When we realised where it was going, we couldn't justify it any (5)." Instead, her staff now give children dried leaves, seeds and coloured paper. "At first the children were disappointed, but they soon became just (6) excited about collecting their own materials."

Not everyone agrees (7) a ban is the right answer. Some experts point out that glitter represents only a tiny fraction of the plastic pollution (8) reaches the sea every year. Car tyres and synthetic clothes, they say, are a far bigger problem. "Banning glitter makes people feel good, (9) it is mostly a symbol," says one researcher.

Supporters of the campaign reply that symbols matter. Children who learn about pollution at the age of four are more likely (10) think about it as adults. Several manufacturers have already started to produce "eco-glitter" made from plant cellulose, (11) breaks down naturally in soil and water.

The new products are more expensive, and some teachers complain that they do not shine as brightly. (12), demand is growing quickly. One British company says it sold (13) as much biodegradable glitter last year as in the year before.

For Sarah Holt, the debate is about more than craft materials. "If we can't give up something as small as glitter," she asks, "how (14) we ever give up the bigger things?" The question, she adds, is one that every school (15) to ask.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. because / as / since
naloge.rezultat:
1. that / which
2. have
3. to
4. to
5. longer / more
6. as
7. that
8. that / which
9. but
10. to
11. which
12. However / Nevertheless / Still
13. twice
14. can / will / could / would
15. needs / has / ought
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvar (something that sparkles); pri something je pogostejši that. Za something, anything, everything se kot oziralni zaimek uporablja that (something that sparkles = nekaj, kar se sveti). Which je sprejemljiv, a manj naraven.
2. have
Present perfect v trpniku: microplastics have been found (osebek v množini). Ker je osebek množina (microplastics) in gre za izkušnjo do zdaj, je čas present perfect; v trpniku: have been found.
3. to
Zveza from … to …: from the surface to the deepest trenches. Zveza from … to … izraža razpon (od površja do najglobljih jarkov).
4. to
used to + nedoločnik za preteklo navado: We used to buy. »used to« + nedoločnik pomeni nekdanjo navado (nekoč smo kupovali). Za used vedno stoji to.
5. longer / more
not … any longer = ne več (tudi any more). »not … any longer« = ne več. Ker je v vrzeli ena beseda, napišeš longer ali more.
6. as
Primerjava enakosti as … as: just as excited (as before). »just as excited as before« = prav tako navdušeni kot prej; primerjava enakosti se začne z as.
7. that
agree that + stavek; that lahko uvede odvisnik po agree. Za glagoli mišljenja in govorjenja (agree, say, think) odvisnik začnemo z that.
8. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za pollution: the plastic pollution that reaches the sea. Oziralni stavek opisuje samostalnik pollution (stvar), zato that ali which; brez vejice sta pravilna oba.
9. but
Nasprotje dveh trditev: makes people feel good, but it is mostly a symbol. Prvi del (makes people feel good) in drugi (it is mostly a symbol) si nasprotujeta, zato veznik but.
10. to
be likely to + nedoločnik. »be likely to do something« = verjetno bo kaj storil. Za likely stoji to + nedoločnik.
11. which
Nedoločni oziralni stavek po vejici se nanaša na stvar: which breaks down (that za vejico ni pravilen). Za vejico (nedoločni oziralni stavek) za stvar uporabimo samo which; that za vejico ni pravilen.
12. However / Nevertheless / Still
Povezovalec, ki uvaja nasprotje prejšnji povedi, na začetku povedi z vejico. Prejšnja poved navaja slabosti (dražje, manj se svetijo), naslednja pa, da povpraševanje raste – nasprotje, zato However ali Nevertheless.
13. twice
twice as much as = dvakrat toliko kot; ena beseda. »twice as much as« = dvakrat toliko kot. Pred as … as stoji števnik: twice, three times.
14. can / will / could / would
Modalni glagol v vprašanju: how can we ever give up …? V vprašanju z how manjka modalni glagol; smisel je »kako se bomo/bi se lahko odpovedali«: can, will, could, would.
15. needs / has / ought
needs to ask, has to ask ali ought to ask: osebek every school je ednina, zato glagol s -s. »every school« je ednina, zato needs/has (s -s). Ought to je brez -s, a je prav tako pravilen.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

How the bicycle changed women's lives

In the 1890s, Europe and America were gripped by a cycling craze. For the first time, the bicycle was cheap, safe and (0) (COMFORT) enough to be used by ordinary people – and women were among its most (1) (ENTHUSIASM) riders.

Before the bicycle, a woman's freedom of movement was (2) (SEVERE) limited. She usually needed a carriage, a horse or a male companion to travel any distance. Cycling offered a new kind of (3) (DEPEND): with a machine that cost about as much as a month's wages, a young woman could visit friends, go to work or explore the countryside alone.

Not everyone welcomed this change. Doctors warned of a mysterious illness called "bicycle face", supposedly caused by the (4) (EXHAUST) of keeping one's balance. Newspapers printed cartoons that showed female cyclists as (5) (RESPONSIBLE) mothers who neglected their homes. Some critics even claimed that cycling would make women (6) (ABLE) to have children.

The bicycle also caused a (7) (REVOLVE) in fashion. Long skirts and tight corsets made pedalling almost impossible, so many riders adopted loose trousers called "bloomers". To many observers they looked shockingly (8) (APPROPRIATE), and women who wore them were sometimes insulted in the street.

Despite the (9) (OPPOSE), the number of female cyclists continued to grow. Cycling clubs organised long-distance rides, and in 1895 the American (10) (CAMPAIGN) Susan B. Anthony said that the bicycle had done more to free women than anything else in the world. In Britain, a young woman named Annie Londonderry became an international (11) (CELEBRATE) after cycling around the world in fifteen months.

Historians now see the bicycle as an important step towards political (12) (EQUAL). It gave women physical confidence, helped them meet and organise, and made the idea of a woman travelling alone seem (13) (ORDINARILY) rather than scandalous. As one suffragist wrote, a woman on a bicycle was a picture of (14) (FREE) that nobody could forget. More than a century later, the image has lost none of its (15) (SIGNIFY).

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. comfortable
naloge.rezultat:
1. enthusiastic
2. severely
3. independence
4. exhaustion
5. irresponsible
6. unable
7. revolution
8. inappropriate
9. opposition
10. campaigner
11. celebrity
12. equality
13. ordinary
14. freedom
15. significance
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. enthusiastic
Pred samostalnikom riders je pridevnik: enthusiasm → enthusiastic (most enthusiastic). Pridevnik stoji pred samostalnikom (riders); iz samostalnika enthusiasm tvorimo pridevnik s pripono -astic.
2. severely
Prislov ob pridevniku/deležniku limited: severe → severely. Ob deležniku limited (omejen) stoji prislov, ki pove, kako zelo: pripona -ly (severely = močno).
3. independence
Samostalnik za a new kind of; pomen svobode zahteva nikalno predpono in-: independence. Za »a new kind of« sledi samostalnik. Ker gre za svobodo, je pomen nasproten odvisnosti: in- + depend + -ence.
4. exhaustion
Za določnim členom the je samostalnik: exhaust → exhaustion. Za the stoji samostalnik; glagol exhaust (izčrpati) dobi pripono -ion: exhaustion (izčrpanost).
5. irresponsible
Kritika: matere, ki zanemarjajo dom, so neodgovorne – predpona ir-. Pridevnik pred samostalnikom mothers; kritiki jih prikazujejo negativno, zato nikalna predpona ir- (pred r).
6. unable
make somebody unable to … – nikalna oblika able → unable. Za make somebody stoji pridevnik; pomen je »nezmožen«, zato un- + able.
7. revolution
a … in fashion: samostalnik revolve → revolution. Za a stoji samostalnik; revolve (vrteti se) → revolution (sprememba, prevrat).
8. inappropriate
»shockingly« in užaljenost kažeta negativen pomen: in- + appropriate. »shockingly« (šokantno) in to, da so ženske žalili, kažeta na negativen pomen: in- + appropriate = neprimeren.
9. opposition
Za the (Despite the …) je samostalnik: oppose → opposition. Za »Despite the« stoji samostalnik: oppose → opposition (nasprotovanje).
10. campaigner
Oseba (Susan B. Anthony): campaign → campaigner. Pred imenom osebe (Susan B. Anthony) je samostalnik za osebo: campaign + -er = borka, aktivistka.
11. celebrity
an international … = slavna oseba: celebrate → celebrity. »an international …« zahteva samostalnik za osebo, ki je slavna: celebrity. Pazi, celebration pomeni praznovanje.
12. equality
political + samostalnik: equal → equality. Za pridevnikom political stoji samostalnik: equal → equality (enakopravnost).
13. ordinary
seem + pridevnik (ne prislov): ordinarily → ordinary. Za glagolom seem stoji pridevnik, ne prislov (seem ordinary = zdeti se običajno), zato -ly odstraniš.
14. freedom
a picture of + samostalnik: free → freedom. Za »a picture of« stoji samostalnik: free → freedom (svoboda).
15. significance
its + samostalnik: signify → significance. Za svojilnim zaimkom its stoji samostalnik: signify (pomeniti) → significance (pomen).

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a recording about Mary Anning, a fossil hunter from the south coast of England. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Today we remember a woman whose name was almost forgotten for more than a century: Mary Anning, who was born in 1799 in Lyme Regis, a small town on the Dorset coast. Her family was poor. Her father, Richard, was a carpenter who earned a little extra money by selling curiosities – shells and strange stones – to tourists who came to the seaside in summer.

The cliffs around Lyme Regis are made of soft rock that slips into the sea after every storm, and with each landslide new fossils appear. Richard took Mary and her brother Joseph along the beach to collect them. When he died in 1810, he left the family in debt, and fossil hunting turned from a hobby into the family's main income.

In 1811, Joseph found a strange skull. Over the next months, Mary, who was only twelve, uncovered the rest of the skeleton. It was an ichthyosaur, a marine reptile, and it was the first complete one ever identified. Later she discovered the first plesiosaur skeleton, an animal with a tiny head and an extremely long neck. When the French scientist Georges Cuvier saw the drawings, he thought it must be a fake. A meeting of experts was called, and only after they had examined the bones did Cuvier admit that he had been wrong.

Mary had almost no formal education, but she taught herself geology and anatomy. She even dissected modern fish and cuttlefish to understand the animals she was digging up. Gentlemen scientists visited her shop to ask for her opinion, yet when they published papers about her finds, her name was usually missing. As a woman, she could not join the Geological Society of London, and she was not allowed to attend its meetings.

The work was dangerous. In 1833, a landslide killed her dog, Tray, only a few metres away from her. Mary carried on working until she died of breast cancer in 1847, at the age of forty-seven.

Today, her story is told in museums, in children's books and even in a feature film. In 2010, the Royal Society named her one of the ten British women who have most influenced the history of science, and in 2022 a statue of her was finally unveiled in Lyme Regis.

Mary Anning

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Mary Anning grew up in a poor family. (T)
  2. 1.Mary Anning's father sold fossils to visitors. T / F
  3. 2.New fossils appear in Lyme Regis mainly in summer. T / F
  4. 3.After her father's death, collecting fossils became a way of earning a living. T / F
  5. 4.Mary found the ichthyosaur skull herself. T / F
  6. 5.Georges Cuvier at first doubted that the plesiosaur was real. T / F
  7. 6.Mary studied living animals to understand fossils better. T / F
  8. 7.Scientists always mentioned Mary's name in their publications. T / F
  9. 8.Mary was a member of the Geological Society of London. T / F
  10. 9.A statue of Mary Anning was put up in her home town more than 150 years after her death. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. T
6. T
7. F
8. F
9. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
»selling curiosities – shells and strange stones – to tourists« – fosili so te »čudne kamnine«. Trditev je T, ker »curiosities – shells and strange stones« so prav fosili. Pozor na parafrazo: v posnetku ni besede fossils, a pomen je isti.
2. F
Fosili se pokažejo po neurjih in plazovih (»after every storm«), poleti pa pridejo turisti. Trditev je F, ker govorec poveže nove fosile z neurji in plazovi; poletje omeni le zaradi turistov.
3. T
»fossil hunting turned from a hobby into the family's main income«. T: »turned from a hobby into the family's main income« = iz konjička je postal glavni vir dohodka (way of earning a living).
4. F
Lobanjo je našel brat Joseph, Mary je odkrila preostanek okostja. F: podrobnost se razlikuje v osebi – lobanjo je našel Joseph, ne Mary. Taka razlika vedno pomeni F.
5. T
»he thought it must be a fake«. T: »he thought it must be a fake« = mislil je, da je ponaredek, torej je dvomil.
6. T
»dissected modern fish and cuttlefish to understand the animals she was digging up«. T: secirala je sodobne ribe in sipe (living animals), da bi razumela fosile.
7. F
»her name was usually missing«. F: »always« v trditvi je v nasprotju z »usually missing« v posnetku. Besede always/never so pogosto znak napačne trditve.
8. F
Kot ženska se društvu ni mogla pridružiti. F: kot ženska ni smela postati članica društva.
9. T
Umrla je leta 1847, kip so odkrili leta 2022 – 175 let pozneje. T: izračun 2022 − 1847 = 175 let, kar je več kot 150.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear an interview with Tom Blake, who keeps bees on the roofs of London. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, you look after bees in the middle of London. How did that start?

Tom: By accident, really. I was working in an office in the City, and one day a swarm landed on the window of our meeting room. Nobody knew what to do, so I phoned a beekeeper, and I was fascinated by how calmly she collected them. Within a year I had done a course and had two hives on my own balcony.

Interviewer: And now?

Tom: Now I manage about sixty hives on the roofs of hotels, banks and a hospital. Companies pay me to keep the bees, and in return they get honey with their own label. Many of them use it as a present for clients.

Interviewer: Isn't a city a strange place for bees?

Tom: People think so, but London is full of parks, private gardens and railway embankments. There is a greater variety of flowers than in the countryside, where you often have huge fields of just one crop. That's why city honey usually tastes more complex – every jar is a mixture of hundreds of plants.

Interviewer: Is there a downside?

Tom: Yes, and it's an important one. There are now so many hives in central London that there isn't enough food for all the bees, especially in late summer. Honeybees then compete with wild bees, and wild bees lose. So I tell companies that are thinking of getting hives: plant flowers first. A roof garden helps more than another hive.

Interviewer: What does a typical day look like for you?

Tom: In spring I open every hive once a week to check that the queen is laying eggs and that the colony isn't preparing to swarm. A strong colony can have fifty thousand bees, and if they swarm from a hotel roof onto a busy street, you get calls from the police. The hardest part of the job is carrying equipment up the stairs – most of these buildings don't let you use the lifts.

Interviewer: Do you get stung?

Tom: All the time! About once a day in summer. You stop reacting after a while, although I always carry medicine in case a visitor is allergic.

Interviewer: Finally, what is the most important thing your bees have taught you?

Tom: Patience. You can't hurry bees. If you move fast, they get nervous. So I've learned to slow down, which, for someone who used to work in finance, is quite a change.

An interview with a beekeeper

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Tom Blake keep his bees?
    On (the) roofs in London.
  2. 1.Where did the swarm that changed Tom's life land?
  3. 2.Where did Tom keep his first two hives?
  4. 3.What do companies get in return for paying Tom?
  5. 4.Why do the countryside fields offer bees less variety?
  6. 5.Which bees lose when there are too many hives?
  7. 6.What does Tom advise companies to do first?
  8. 7.What does Tom check every week in spring?
  9. 8.What is the hardest part of Tom's job?
  10. 9.What has working with bees taught Tom?
naloge.rezultat:
1. On the window of a meeting room (at his office).
2. On his (own) balcony.
3. Honey with their own label.
4. They have just one crop.
5. Wild bees.
6. (To) plant flowers.
7. That the queen is laying eggs. / Whether the colony is preparing to swarm.
8. Carrying equipment up the stairs.
9. Patience. / To slow down.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. On the window of a meeting room (at his office).
»a swarm landed on the window of our meeting room«. Vprašanje »Where … land?« sprašuje po kraju, zato odgovor začneš s predlogom (On the window …). Dodatek »at his office« ni nujen.
2. On his (own) balcony.
»two hives on my own balcony«. Ključna beseda »first two hives« te pripelje do začetka zgodbe; odgovor je kraj: balkon.
3. Honey with their own label.
»they get honey with their own label«. »In return for paying« = kaj dobijo v zameno za plačilo. Tom reče, da dobijo med z lastno nalepko (label).
4. They have just one crop.
»huge fields of just one crop«. Vprašanje »Why …?« zahteva razlog: polja imajo eno samo kulturo (just one crop), zato je hrane za čebele malo različne.
5. Wild bees.
»Honeybees then compete with wild bees, and wild bees lose«. Govorec primerja medonosne in divje čebele; izgubijo divje (wild bees). Pazi, da ne napišeš honeybees.
6. (To) plant flowers.
»plant flowers first. A roof garden helps more than another hive«. »First« v vprašanju ustreza »plant flowers first« v posnetku. Odgovor je dejanje, zato je dovolj glagol z dopolnilom.
7. That the queen is laying eggs. / Whether the colony is preparing to swarm.
Dovolj je eden od dveh podatkov, ki ju omeni. »Every week in spring« – Tom omeni dve stvari; dovolj je ena, saj vprašanje sprašuje »what«, ne »what two things«.
8. Carrying equipment up the stairs.
»The hardest part of the job is carrying equipment up the stairs«. »Hardest part« je v posnetku skoraj dobesedno ponovljen; odgovor je glagolnik (carrying …), ki opiše dejanje.
9. Patience. / To slow down.
»Patience. You can't hurry bees.« Zadnje vprašanje sprašuje po spoznanju; Tom ga pove z eno besedo: Patience. Sprejme se tudi parafraza »to slow down«.

naloge.besedilo:
Report

You recently took part in a week-long project at your school in which students organised a repair café, a place where people from the town could bring broken objects to be fixed for free.

Write a report of 120–150 words to the head teacher, in which you:

  • describe what people brought to the repair café and what was repaired,
  • explain which part of the project was the most successful and why,
  • suggest how the project could be improved next year.
To: Head Teacher
From: Dominik(a) Novak
Subject: Repair café
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo in naslovom, uvodom z namenom, tremi odstavki s podnaslovi (kaj so prinesli in popravili, najuspešnejši del z razlogom, predlog za izboljšavo) in kratkim sklepom; 120–150 besed, formalni jezik.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (120–150 words), formal style
  2. describe what people brought to the repair café and what was repaired
  3. explain which part of the project was the most successful and why
  4. suggest how the project could be improved next year
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: the Head Teacher / From: Dominik(a) Novak / Subject: Repair café project
Poročilo ima glavo (komu, od koga, zadeva) in naslov. Ni nagovora »Dear …« kot pri pismu.
Introduction – The aim of this report is to summarise the repair café organised by our class last week.
Uvod v eni povedi pove namen poročila.
Odstavek 1: kaj so prinesli
Over 60 visitors brought items such as lamps, toasters, bicycles and torn jackets. Our volunteers managed to repair around 40 of them.
Prva iztočnica: konkretne stvari in številke. Vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek s podnaslovom.
Odstavek 2: najuspešnejši del
The most successful part was the bicycle corner, because it attracted families and many visitors learned to fix punctures themselves.
Druga iztočnica zahteva dva dela: kaj in zakaj (because, as a result).
Odstavek 3: predlogi
I would recommend advertising the event earlier and inviting local craftspeople, as we had to turn away people with broken electronics.
Predlog: I would recommend + -ing / It would be a good idea to …
Conclusion – Overall, the project was a success and should definitely be repeated.
Kratek sklep. Formalen jezik, brez skrajšanih oblik (don't → do not).
Točke se podelijo za vsebino (vse tri iztočnice), zgradbo in obliko (glava, odstavki), besedišče in slovnico. Preštej besede: 120–150.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Head Teacher
From: Dominika Novak, 3.B
Subject: Repair café project

Introduction

The aim of this report is to summarise the repair café that our class organised in the school hall last week.

What was brought and repaired

About sixty visitors brought lamps, toasters, radios, bicycles and torn jackets. Our volunteers repaired about forty items.

The most successful part

The bicycle corner was the most popular part of the project. Not only were punctures and brakes fixed, but many children also learned to repair their own bikes.

Suggestions for next year

I would recommend advertising the event earlier. It would also be a good idea to invite more craftspeople, because we had to send away several broken laptops.

Conclusion

Overall, the repair café was a great success and should definitely be repeated.

Dominika Novak

Število besed: 135 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Young people should spend a year volunteering before university.
  2. Cities should be designed for pedestrians, not cars.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem v uvodu, dvema ali tremi argumenti s primeri, upoštevanim protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en sam izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in jasno povej svoje stališče (I largely agree that …).
Ocenjevalci iščejo jasno tezo že v uvodu. Ne prepiši naslova dobesedno.
Jedro 1: prvi argument + primer (A gap year of volunteering teaches responsibility …).
Vsak odstavek ima temeljno poved, razlago in konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
Jedro 2: drugi argument + primer (… it also helps students choose the right course).
Povezovalci: Furthermore, What is more, In addition.
Jedro 3: protiargument in zavrnitev (Critics argue that … However, …).
Upoštevanje nasprotnega mnenja pokaže zrelost argumentacije in prinese točke za vsebino.
Sklep: povzemi stališče brez novih argumentov (All things considered, …).
Sklep naj odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: cleaner air, safer streets, more local shops, healthier citizens. Against: older people and deliveries depend on cars, public transport is not always available.
Izberi le en naslov in ga podčrtaj. Nevtralen, formalen slog, brez skrajšanih oblik.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Young people should spend a year volunteering before university.

Many students go straight from secondary school to university without knowing what they really want to study. Some people therefore suggest that young people should spend a year volunteering first. I largely agree with this idea, although I do not think it should be compulsory.

Firstly, volunteering teaches responsibility. A young person who helps in a children's home or an animal shelter has to arrive on time, work in a team and deal with real problems. These are skills that cannot be learned from textbooks.

Secondly, a year of volunteering can help students choose the right course. My cousin worked with refugees in Greece for ten months. Before that, she wanted to study economics, but the experience showed her that she wanted to become a social worker. Without that year, she might have wasted several years at the wrong faculty.

Critics argue that a year away from school makes students forget what they have learned and delays their careers. However, most students return more motivated, and employers often value practical experience more than an extra year of studying.

All things considered, I believe that a volunteering year is a valuable opportunity. Schools and the state should support students who choose it, for example with grants, but the decision should always remain personal, because a year that is forced on someone loses much of its value.

Število besed: 234 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Last Bookshop

Every town has a place where time behaves differently. In ours it was Maddox & Daughter, a bookshop squeezed between a bakery and a shoe repairer on Castle Street. The sign said "Est. 1923", although Mrs Maddox liked to tell customers that the date had been painted by her grandfather after a particularly good lunch and might not be entirely accurate.

I started working there at sixteen, on Saturdays, for a wage so small that Mrs Maddox paid it partly in books. She explained the arrangement as if it were a great privilege. "Money," she said, "goes into your pocket and disappears. A book goes into your head and stays." I did not argue. I was too busy being amazed that someone would pay me – even in paperbacks – to spend the day in a room that smelt of paper and dust and the cinnamon rolls from next door.

The shop had no computer. Mrs Maddox kept the stock in her memory and in a series of school exercise books, one for each letter of the alphabet, filled with her tiny, slanting handwriting. When a customer asked for a title, she would close her eyes for a moment, as though listening to a distant radio, and then walk directly to the right shelf. She was wrong so rarely that the regulars treated her mistakes as small public holidays.

It was not a profitable business. Most weeks, the shop earned just enough to pay the rent, and in bad months Mrs Maddox sold her own furniture, piece by piece. Her daughter, who lived in London and worked for an insurance company, phoned every Sunday to beg her to close. "Nobody buys books in shops any more, Mum," I once heard her say through the receiver, so loudly that I could hear every word from the back room.

Then, one February, a developer bought the whole row of buildings. The bakery accepted his offer at once. The shoe repairer held out for a month. Mrs Maddox simply ignored his letters, using the envelopes as bookmarks.

What happened next surprised everyone, including her. A girl from my school posted a photograph of the shop online with the words "Save the last bookshop". Within a week, there were queues on Castle Street. People who had not bought a book in years came to buy three. A retired lawyer offered to fight the developer for free.

The shop is still there. It has a computer now, which Mrs Maddox refuses to touch. "It keeps telling me what I already know," she complains, and goes on writing in her exercise books.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.Where was the bookshop?
    On Castle Street.
  2. 1.Why might the date on the sign not be reliable?
  3. 2.Apart from money, how was the narrator paid?
  4. 3.According to Mrs Maddox, what is the advantage of a book over money?
  5. 4.What smell came from the neighbouring shop?
  6. 5.Where did Mrs Maddox record the stock?
  7. 6.How did the regular customers react to her rare mistakes?
  8. 7.What did Mrs Maddox do when the shop lost money?
  9. 8.What did her daughter want her to do?
  10. 9.How did Mrs Maddox treat the developer's letters?
  11. 10.What did the retired lawyer offer?
naloge.rezultat:
1. It was painted after a (good) lunch.
2. (Partly) in books.
3. It stays in your head.
4. Cinnamon rolls.
5. In (school) exercise books. / In her memory.
6. Like small public holidays. / They celebrated them.
7. She sold her (own) furniture.
8. (To) close the shop.
9. She ignored them. / She used the envelopes as bookmarks.
10. To fight the developer for free.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. It was painted after a (good) lunch.
Mrs Maddox šaljivo pove, da je datum napisal ded »after a particularly good lunch«. Vprašanje »Why might … not be reliable?« zahteva razlog za dvom. Šala o »dobrem kosilu« namiguje, da ded morda ni bil čisto zbran.
2. (Partly) in books.
»paid it partly in books«. »Apart from money« = poleg denarja; odgovor je druga oblika plačila: knjige.
3. It stays in your head.
»A book goes into your head and stays.« Mrs Maddox primerja knjigo in denar: denar porabiš, knjiga pa »ostane v glavi«.
4. Cinnamon rolls.
»the cinnamon rolls from next door« – sosednja trgovina je pekarna. Sosednja trgovina je pekarna; vonj so cimetovi zvitki. Odgovor je samostalniška zveza.
5. In (school) exercise books. / In her memory.
Dva vira: spomin in zvezki, po en za vsako črko. »Where« = kraj zapisa; zvezki (exercise books). Spomin je sprejemljiv, ker besedilo pove, da je zaloga tudi v njeni glavi.
6. Like small public holidays. / They celebrated them.
»treated her mistakes as small public holidays« – izjemno redki dogodki. Stranke so njene redke napake slavile kot »majhne praznike«; dovolj je parafraza »They celebrated them«.
7. She sold her (own) furniture.
»in bad months Mrs Maddox sold her own furniture«. V slabih mesecih je prodala svoje pohištvo, da je pokrila izgubo trgovine.
8. (To) close the shop.
»phoned every Sunday to beg her to close«. »beg her to close« = rotila jo je, naj zapre; odgovor je dejanje: to close the shop.
9. She ignored them. / She used the envelopes as bookmarks.
»ignored his letters, using the envelopes as bookmarks«. Dve sprejemljivi rešitvi: pisma je ignorirala in kuverte uporabljala kot kazalke.
10. To fight the developer for free.
»offered to fight the developer for free«. »for free« je ključni del ponudbe; brez njega odgovor ni popoln.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There are examples at the beginning: Example 0, Example 00.

Accidental inventions that changed everyday life

Not every great invention was planned. Some of the most useful objects we own were discovered by mistake.

A The microwave oven

In 1945, the American engineer Percy Spencer was testing equipment for military radar when he noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted. Curious, he placed some popcorn kernels near the machine and watched them burst. The first commercial microwave oven was nearly two metres tall and weighed more than 300 kilograms, so it was sold only to restaurants and ships. It took another twenty years before a version small and cheap enough for ordinary kitchens appeared.

B Sticky notes

The scientist Spencer Silver was trying to create a super-strong glue in 1968, but he produced the opposite: an adhesive so weak that it could be removed without leaving a mark. For years nobody knew what to do with it. The solution came from his colleague Art Fry, who was tired of the paper bookmarks falling out of his hymn book at church. The company was not convinced at first, and early tests in shops failed because customers did not understand the product until they were given free samples.

C The pacemaker

In 1956, Wilson Greatbatch, an engineer working on a device to record heart sounds, reached into a box for a resistor and took the wrong one. When he switched the circuit on, it produced a regular electrical pulse that reminded him of a heartbeat. He immediately understood what it could mean for patients with heart problems. He spent two years in a barn behind his house developing a small device, and today millions of people live longer thanks to his mistake.

D Safety glass

One day in 1903, the French chemist Édouard Bénédictus knocked a glass flask off a shelf in his laboratory. To his surprise, it cracked but did not break into pieces. The flask had contained a plastic solution that had dried and formed a thin film on the inside. He did not think about it again until he read about drivers injured by broken windscreens. He then patented laminated glass, but car manufacturers showed little interest at first because it was expensive, and the material was first used widely in gas masks during the First World War.

E Super glue

During the Second World War, Harry Coover was trying to make clear plastic gun sights. One of the materials he tested stuck to everything it touched, and he rejected it as useless. Nine years later he came across the same substance again and realised that its stickiness was its value. Since then it has been used for everything from mending toys to closing wounds; during the Vietnam War medics used a spray version to stop bleeding on the battlefield.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Which discovery began with food being affected in an unexpected way? (A)
  2. 00.Which inventor saw his product as worthless at first? (E)
  3. 1.Which inventor's discovery was the opposite of what he had wanted to produce?
  4. 2.Which invention was at first too large for ordinary homes?
  5. 3.Whose idea was inspired by a problem outside work?
  6. 4.Which inventor developed his product in a building on his own property?
  7. 5.Which material was first used for a purpose different from the one its inventor intended?
  8. 6.Which discovery started with a mistake in choosing a component?
  9. 7.Which product only became popular after people were allowed to try it?
  10. 8.Which inventor ignored his discovery for several years?
  11. 9.Which invention has a medical use that is not the one it is best known for?
  12. 10.Which inventor was reminded of his discovery by news of accidents?
naloge.rezultat:
1. B
2. A
3. B
4. C
5. D
6. C
7. B
8. E
9. E
10. D
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Silver je hotel izdelati zelo močno lepilo, nastalo pa je zelo šibko. »the opposite of what he had wanted« = nasprotje tega, kar je želel: hotel je močno lepilo, dobil pa šibko (Post-it).
2. A
Prva mikrovalovka je bila skoraj dva metra visoka in je tehtala več kot 300 kg. »too large for ordinary homes« ustreza podatku o višini skoraj dveh metrov in teži 300 kg.
3. B
Art Fry: kazalke, ki so padale iz pesmarice v cerkvi. »a problem outside work« = težava zunaj službe: kazalke, ki so padale iz pesmarice v cerkvi.
4. C
Greatbatch: »two years in a barn behind his house«. »a building on his own property« = poslopje na lastnem zemljišču: skedenj za hišo (barn behind his house).
5. D
Varnostno steklo je bilo namenjeno avtomobilom, najprej pa so ga uporabili v plinskih maskah. Steklo je bilo namenjeno avtomobilom, najprej pa so ga uporabili za plinske maske – drugačen namen, kot ga je imel izumitelj.
6. C
»took the wrong one« – napačen upor. »a mistake in choosing a component« = napaka pri izbiri sestavnega dela: vzel je napačen upor.
7. B
Kupci so ga razumeli šele, ko so dobili brezplačne vzorce. »only became popular after people were allowed to try it« = šele po brezplačnih vzorcih.
8. E
Coover snov zavrže in jo spet najde čez devet let. »ignored for several years« = devet let ga ni uporabil in ga je šele nato znova našel.
9. E
Lepilo, znano za popravila, so uporabljali tudi za zapiranje ran. »a medical use that is not the one it is best known for«: lepilo je znano za popravila, uporabljali pa so ga tudi za rane.
10. D
Bénédictus se spomni bučke, ko bere o voznikih, ranjenih zaradi razbitih vetrobranskih stekel. »reminded by news of accidents«: ob poročilih o nesrečah z razbitimi stekli se je spomnil na bučko.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Beavers return to Britain after 400 years

Four centuries after they were hunted to extinction, beavers are back in British rivers – and scientists say the results (0) been remarkable. In 2025 the government gave official permission (1) wild beavers to be released in England, ending years of debate.

Beavers were once common across the country, but they (2) killed in huge numbers for their fur, meat and a substance used in medicine. By the sixteenth century they (3) disappeared completely. Their return began quietly in the early 2000s, (4) a small number escaped from private farms and started living in rivers in Devon.

Instead of removing them, the authorities decided to study (5) the animals affected the landscape. The findings surprised even the researchers. Beaver dams slow down the flow of water, (6) means that towns downstream are less likely to be flooded after heavy rain. During dry summers, (7) other hand, the ponds behind the dams keep rivers from drying out.

The animals also create habitats for (8) wide range of other species. Ponds built by beavers attract frogs, insects, birds and bats, and fish numbers often increase (9) than fall. "A beaver does in a few weeks what would cost us thousands of pounds and a team of engineers," says one ecologist.

Not (10) is happy about the return, however. Some farmers complain that beavers dig into riverbanks, cut down valuable trees and flood fields (11) crops are growing. They want compensation, and the right to move animals that cause serious damage.

To reduce conflict, the new rules allow beavers (12) be relocated if they become a problem, and farmers can apply (13) financial support. Experts say the key is patience. "We have lived without beavers for so long (14) we have forgotten how to live with them," says the ecologist. "We will have to learn again." (15) the challenges, most people seem to agree that the return of the beaver is a rare piece of good news for British nature.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. have
naloge.rezultat:
1. for
2. were
3. had
4. when / after
5. how
6. which
7. on
8. a
9. rather
10. everyone / everybody
11. where
12. to
13. for
14. that
15. Despite
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. for
permission for somebody to do something. »permission« se veže s for (permission for somebody to do something = dovoljenje za koga).
2. were
Trpnik v preteklem času, množina: they were killed. Pretekli dogodek (lov v preteklosti), osebek množina, trpnik: were + 3. oblika (killed).
3. had
Predpreteklik: do 16. stoletja so že izginili – had disappeared. Dogodek je bil končan pred drugim preteklim trenutkom (do 16. stoletja), zato past perfect: had disappeared.
4. when / after
Časovni odvisnik: when a small number escaped. Časovni odvisnik: ko/potem ko je nekaj živali pobegnilo. Ena beseda: when ali after.
5. how
Odvisno vprašanje: study how the animals affected the landscape. Za study stoji odvisno vprašanje: how (kako so živali vplivale na pokrajino).
6. which
Oziralni zaimek, ki se nanaša na celoten prejšnji stavek: which means that … Za vejico se which lahko nanaša na ves prejšnji stavek (which means that = kar pomeni, da).
7. on
Stalna zveza on the other hand. Ustaljena zveza on the other hand = po drugi strani.
8. a
a wide range of – nedoločni člen. »a wide range of« = širok izbor; pred pridevnikom wide stoji nedoločni člen a.
9. rather
rather than = namesto da bi. »rather than« = namesto da bi; za rather stoji than.
10. everyone / everybody
Not everyone is happy – osebek v ednini. Osebek »everyone/everybody« je ednina (Not everyone is happy). Nobody ne ustreza, ker že stoji not.
11. where
Oziralni prislov za kraj: fields where crops are growing. Za samostalnikom kraja (fields) stoji where (kjer).
12. to
allow somebody to do something. »allow somebody to do something« = dovoliti komu, da kaj stori.
13. for
apply for (financial) support. »apply for something« = zaprositi za kaj.
14. that
Zveza so … that: so long that we have forgotten. Zveza so + pridevnik/prislov + that izraža posledico (tako dolgo, da smo pozabili).
15. Despite
Despite + samostalnik (the challenges); In spite of bi zahteval dve besedi. Despite + samostalnik (Despite the challenges = kljub izzivom); in spite of so tri besede.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Our robot vacuum ran away from home

It was supposed to make our lives easier. When my partner (0) (BUY) a robot vacuum cleaner last spring, she promised it would end our arguments about whose turn it was to clean the floor. "It (1) (DO) everything while we're at work," she said. "We'll come home to a perfect flat."

For the first week, it was a dream. Every morning at nine the little machine (2) (LEAVE) its charging station and set off on its route, and every evening the floors (3) (SHINE). Our cat, who (4) (NEVER / SEE) anything like it before, spent hours watching it from the top of the sofa.

The trouble began when we (5) (DECIDE) to give it a name. Once it was called Rupert, it seemed to develop a personality. It refused to clean the bathroom. It got stuck under the bed at least twice a day, beeping until someone rescued it. One evening we came home to find that it (6) (DRAG) a sock all the way from the bedroom to the front door.

Then, one Tuesday in June, Rupert disappeared. The charging station was empty, the front door was locked, and there was no sign of him anywhere. We searched for an hour before my partner noticed that the balcony door (7) (LEAVE) open. Rupert was sitting in the neighbours' garden, one floor below, surrounded by fallen leaves. He must (8) (FALL) over the edge while he was chasing dust.

Our neighbour, Mr Price, was not amused. "If that thing (9) (LAND) on my tomatoes," he said, "you would be buying me new ones." We apologised, promised to keep the door shut, and carried Rupert home like a lost dog.

These days Rupert is watched more carefully. Before we go out, we check that all the doors (10) (CLOSE). The cat has stopped being interested, although she still likes (11) (RIDE) on top of him when she thinks nobody is looking.

Was buying him a mistake? Not exactly. The floors are cleaner than they (12) (BE) for years. But if I (13) (KNOW) how much attention a robot needs, I might have chosen a simple broom instead. At least a broom (14) (NOT / RUN) away. And by next summer, I suspect, we (15) (SPEND) more money on repairs than the machine itself cost.

naloge.rezultat:
1. will do / 'll do
2. left
3. shone
4. had never seen
5. decided
6. had dragged
7. had been left
8. have fallen
9. had landed
10. are closed
11. riding / to ride
12. have been
13. had known
14. doesn't run / does not run / wouldn't run / would not run
15. will have spent
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. will do / 'll do
Napoved v poročanem govoru: »It will do everything« (premi govor v narekovajih). Proizvajalec obljublja prihodnost (it will do everything), zato will + nedoločnik.
2. left
Pretekla ponavljajoča se dejanja v pripovedi: past simple. Pripoved v preteklosti, dejanje se je ponavljalo: past simple (left).
3. shone
Nepravilni glagol shine – shone – shone (ne »shined« v tem pomenu). Shine je nepravilni glagol: shine – shone – shone. Oblika shined se uporablja za »loščiti«, tu pa gre za sijaj.
4. had never seen
Predpreteklik: mačka pred tem še ni videla česa podobnega. Mačka »prej še nikoli ni videla« – izkušnja pred preteklim trenutkom, zato had never seen.
5. decided
Enkratno preteklo dejanje: past simple. Enkratna odločitev v pripovedi: decided (past simple).
6. had dragged
Dejanje se je zgodilo pred tem, ko sva prišla domov: past perfect. Robot je stvar odvlekel, preden sva prišla domov – prej od drugega preteklega dejanja: had dragged.
7. had been left
Trpnik v predpretekliku: vrata je nekdo pustil odprta pred tem. Vrata je nekdo pustil odprta pred tem trenutkom: trpnik v predpretekliku had been left.
8. have fallen
must have + 3. oblika za sklepanje o preteklosti. must have + 3. oblika = moralo se je zgoditi (sklepanje o preteklosti): must have fallen.
9. had landed
Mešani pogojnik: if + past perfect (pretekla nemožnost), posledica v sedanjosti (would be buying). Mešani pogojnik: pogoj v preteklosti (if it had landed), posledica v sedanjosti (we would be buying).
10. are closed
Stanje v sedanjosti, trpnik: the doors are closed. Splošno stanje zdaj, vrata nekdo zapre: trpnik v sedanjiku are closed.
11. riding / to ride
like + -ing ali like + to-nedoločnik. Za like stoji -ing ali to + nedoločnik; oba sta pravilna (riding / to ride).
12. have been
for years + present perfect: tla so čistejša, kot so bila že leta. »for years« + present perfect: tla niso bila tako čista že leta (have been).
13. had known
Tretji pogojnik: if + past perfect, … might have chosen. Tretji pogojnik (pretekla nemožnost): if + had + 3. oblika, posledica might have chosen.
14. doesn't run / does not run / wouldn't run / would not run
Splošna resnica (doesn't run) ali hipotetično (wouldn't run). Splošna resnica v sedanjiku (doesn't run) ali predstavljiva situacija (wouldn't run); obe obliki sta smiselni.
15. will have spent
Future perfect: by next summer – do tedaj že dokončano. »by next summer« = do prihodnjega poletja; dejanje bo takrat že končano: will have spent (future perfect).

naslov: Angleščina, visja raven, spomladanski rok 2026, izpitna pola 2: slušno razumevanje (vadbena pola Učilnica.com)
