naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a recording about Mary Anning, a fossil hunter from the south coast of England. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Today we remember a woman whose name was almost forgotten for more than a century: Mary Anning, who was born in 1799 in Lyme Regis, a small town on the Dorset coast. Her family was poor. Her father, Richard, was a carpenter who earned a little extra money by selling curiosities – shells and strange stones – to tourists who came to the seaside in summer.

The cliffs around Lyme Regis are made of soft rock that slips into the sea after every storm, and with each landslide new fossils appear. Richard took Mary and her brother Joseph along the beach to collect them. When he died in 1810, he left the family in debt, and fossil hunting turned from a hobby into the family's main income.

In 1811, Joseph found a strange skull. Over the next months, Mary, who was only twelve, uncovered the rest of the skeleton. It was an ichthyosaur, a marine reptile, and it was the first complete one ever identified. Later she discovered the first plesiosaur skeleton, an animal with a tiny head and an extremely long neck. When the French scientist Georges Cuvier saw the drawings, he thought it must be a fake. A meeting of experts was called, and only after they had examined the bones did Cuvier admit that he had been wrong.

Mary had almost no formal education, but she taught herself geology and anatomy. She even dissected modern fish and cuttlefish to understand the animals she was digging up. Gentlemen scientists visited her shop to ask for her opinion, yet when they published papers about her finds, her name was usually missing. As a woman, she could not join the Geological Society of London, and she was not allowed to attend its meetings.

The work was dangerous. In 1833, a landslide killed her dog, Tray, only a few metres away from her. Mary carried on working until she died of breast cancer in 1847, at the age of forty-seven.

Today, her story is told in museums, in children's books and even in a feature film. In 2010, the Royal Society named her one of the ten British women who have most influenced the history of science, and in 2022 a statue of her was finally unveiled in Lyme Regis.

Mary Anning

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

  1. 0.Mary Anning was born in the town of ___ in 1799.
    Lyme Regis
  2. 1.Mary Anning's father was a ___ who also sold curiosities to tourists.
  3. 2.New fossils appear at Lyme Regis after every ___.
  4. 3.When Richard died in 1810, the family was left ___.
  5. 4.The ichthyosaur Mary uncovered was the first ___ ever identified.
  6. 5.The plesiosaur had a tiny head and ___.
  7. 6.Cuvier admitted his mistake only after experts had ___.
  8. 7.To learn anatomy, Mary dissected ___.
  9. 8.In 1833, Mary nearly died when her dog was killed by ___.
  10. 9.In 2010, the Royal Society named her one of ten British women who most influenced ___.
naloge.rezultat:
1. carpenter
2. storm / landslide
3. in debt
4. complete one / complete skeleton
5. an extremely long neck
6. examined the bones
7. (modern) fish and cuttlefish
8. a landslide
9. the history of science
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. carpenter
»Her father, Richard, was a carpenter«. Pred vrzeljo je »a«, za njo »who also sold«, zato manjka samostalnik za poklic: carpenter (mizar).
2. storm / landslide
»slips into the sea after every storm, and with each landslide new fossils appear«. »after every« zahteva samostalnik v ednini: storm ali landslide (oba sta v posnetku).
3. in debt
»he left the family in debt«. »left in debt« = ostali so zadolženi; zveza je ustaljena (in debt).
4. complete one / complete skeleton
»the first complete one ever identified«. »the first … ever identified« – manjka »complete one/skeleton«; beseda complete je bistvena.
5. an extremely long neck
»an animal with a tiny head and an extremely long neck«. Za »and« manjka drugi del opisa: zelo dolg vrat. Pridevnik extremely naj ostane, ker je del opisa.
6. examined the bones
»only after they had examined the bones did Cuvier admit«. Za »had« stoji 3. oblika glagola: had examined the bones (predpreteklik).
7. (modern) fish and cuttlefish
»She even dissected modern fish and cuttlefish«. Za dissected manjka predmet: kaj je secirala (sodobne ribe in sipe).
8. a landslide
»a landslide killed her dog, Tray«. »killed by« zahteva vršilca: plaz (a landslide).
9. the history of science
»the ten British women who have most influenced the history of science«. »influenced« zahteva predmet: the history of science.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear an interview with Tom Blake, who keeps bees on the roofs of London. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, you look after bees in the middle of London. How did that start?

Tom: By accident, really. I was working in an office in the City, and one day a swarm landed on the window of our meeting room. Nobody knew what to do, so I phoned a beekeeper, and I was fascinated by how calmly she collected them. Within a year I had done a course and had two hives on my own balcony.

Interviewer: And now?

Tom: Now I manage about sixty hives on the roofs of hotels, banks and a hospital. Companies pay me to keep the bees, and in return they get honey with their own label. Many of them use it as a present for clients.

Interviewer: Isn't a city a strange place for bees?

Tom: People think so, but London is full of parks, private gardens and railway embankments. There is a greater variety of flowers than in the countryside, where you often have huge fields of just one crop. That's why city honey usually tastes more complex – every jar is a mixture of hundreds of plants.

Interviewer: Is there a downside?

Tom: Yes, and it's an important one. There are now so many hives in central London that there isn't enough food for all the bees, especially in late summer. Honeybees then compete with wild bees, and wild bees lose. So I tell companies that are thinking of getting hives: plant flowers first. A roof garden helps more than another hive.

Interviewer: What does a typical day look like for you?

Tom: In spring I open every hive once a week to check that the queen is laying eggs and that the colony isn't preparing to swarm. A strong colony can have fifty thousand bees, and if they swarm from a hotel roof onto a busy street, you get calls from the police. The hardest part of the job is carrying equipment up the stairs – most of these buildings don't let you use the lifts.

Interviewer: Do you get stung?

Tom: All the time! About once a day in summer. You stop reacting after a while, although I always carry medicine in case a visitor is allergic.

Interviewer: Finally, what is the most important thing your bees have taught you?

Tom: Patience. You can't hurry bees. If you move fast, they get nervous. So I've learned to slow down, which, for someone who used to work in finance, is quite a change.

An interview with a beekeeper

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Tom Blake keep his bees?
    On (the) roofs in London.
  2. 1.Where did the swarm that changed Tom's life land?
  3. 2.Where did Tom keep his first two hives?
  4. 3.What do companies get in return for paying Tom?
  5. 4.Why do the countryside fields offer bees less variety?
  6. 5.Which bees lose when there are too many hives?
  7. 6.What does Tom advise companies to do first?
  8. 7.What does Tom check every week in spring?
  9. 8.What is the hardest part of Tom's job?
  10. 9.What has working with bees taught Tom?
naloge.rezultat:
1. On the window of a meeting room (at his office).
2. On his (own) balcony.
3. Honey with their own label.
4. They have just one crop.
5. Wild bees.
6. (To) plant flowers.
7. That the queen is laying eggs. / Whether the colony is preparing to swarm.
8. Carrying equipment up the stairs.
9. Patience. / To slow down.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. On the window of a meeting room (at his office).
»a swarm landed on the window of our meeting room«. Vprašanje »Where … land?« sprašuje po kraju, zato odgovor začneš s predlogom (On the window …). Dodatek »at his office« ni nujen.
2. On his (own) balcony.
»two hives on my own balcony«. Ključna beseda »first two hives« te pripelje do začetka zgodbe; odgovor je kraj: balkon.
3. Honey with their own label.
»they get honey with their own label«. »In return for paying« = kaj dobijo v zameno za plačilo. Tom reče, da dobijo med z lastno nalepko (label).
4. They have just one crop.
»huge fields of just one crop«. Vprašanje »Why …?« zahteva razlog: polja imajo eno samo kulturo (just one crop), zato je hrane za čebele malo različne.
5. Wild bees.
»Honeybees then compete with wild bees, and wild bees lose«. Govorec primerja medonosne in divje čebele; izgubijo divje (wild bees). Pazi, da ne napišeš honeybees.
6. (To) plant flowers.
»plant flowers first. A roof garden helps more than another hive«. »First« v vprašanju ustreza »plant flowers first« v posnetku. Odgovor je dejanje, zato je dovolj glagol z dopolnilom.
7. That the queen is laying eggs. / Whether the colony is preparing to swarm.
Dovolj je eden od dveh podatkov, ki ju omeni. »Every week in spring« – Tom omeni dve stvari; dovolj je ena, saj vprašanje sprašuje »what«, ne »what two things«.
8. Carrying equipment up the stairs.
»The hardest part of the job is carrying equipment up the stairs«. »Hardest part« je v posnetku skoraj dobesedno ponovljen; odgovor je glagolnik (carrying …), ki opiše dejanje.
9. Patience. / To slow down.
»Patience. You can't hurry bees.« Zadnje vprašanje sprašuje po spoznanju; Tom ga pove z eno besedo: Patience. Sprejme se tudi parafraza »to slow down«.

naloge.besedilo:
Report

You have just returned from a five-day international youth conference on climate action in Copenhagen, where you represented your school. You took part in workshops on sustainable transport, food waste and green technology.

Write a report of 150–180 words for the conference organisers, in which you:

  • explain which workshop was the most useful for you and why,
  • comment on the organisation of the conference (accommodation, timetable, materials),
  • suggest one topic for next year's conference and justify your choice.
To: Conference Organisers
From: Dominik(a) Novak
Subject: Youth Climate Conference
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, tremi odstavki s podnaslovi (najkoristnejša delavnica z utemeljitvijo, ocena organizacije, predlog teme z utemeljitvijo) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain which workshop was the most useful for you and why
  3. comment on the organisation of the conference (accommodation, timetable, materials)
  4. suggest one topic for next year's conference and justify your choice
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Conference Organisers / From: Dominik(a) Novak / Subject: Youth Climate Conference, Copenhagen
Glava in naslov, nato uvod z namenom (The purpose of this report is to …).
Most useful workshop
The food waste workshop was the most valuable, as we designed a realistic plan that our school canteen has already started to use.
Utemeljitev s posledico (as a result, which means that) pokaže višjo raven.
Organisation
The accommodation was comfortable and close to the venue; however, the timetable was overloaded and left little time for networking.
Uravnotežena ocena: pohvala + kritika z however / although.
Recommendation
I would suggest a workshop on climate communication, since many participants felt unsure how to present their ideas to local authorities.
Predlog + utemeljitev. I would suggest + samostalnik / -ing.
Conclusion: Overall, the conference exceeded my expectations.
Kratek sklep, formalen slog, pasivne zgradbe in neosebni izrazi (It was felt that …).
Na višji ravni je meja 150–180 besed; ocenjevalci pričakujejo pestrejše besedišče in strukture.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Conference Organisers
From: Dominik Novak, Gimnazija Celje
Subject: Youth Climate Conference, Copenhagen

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to evaluate the five-day Youth Climate Conference which I attended in Copenhagen as a representative of my school.

The most useful workshop

The food waste workshop was by far the most valuable for me. Working in international groups, we designed a realistic plan to reduce waste in school canteens. As a result, our canteen has already started to offer smaller portions and to donate leftover bread.

Organisation

The accommodation was comfortable and close to the venue, and the materials were well prepared. However, the timetable was overloaded: sessions ran from eight in the morning until late in the evening, which left little time for networking with other participants.

Recommendation

I would suggest a workshop on climate communication for next year. Many participants felt unsure how to present their ideas to local authorities and the media, and practical training in this area would make our projects far more effective.

Conclusion

Overall, the conference exceeded my expectations.

Dominik Novak

Število besed: 177 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the importance of home and belonging in Nick Hornby's About a Boy and Claire Keegan's Foster.

Nick Hornby: About a Boy · Claire Keegan: Foster

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o domu in pripadnosti, ki jo dokazuje s prizori iz obeh del (Marcus in Will; deklica pri Kinsellovih) in obe deli neposredno primerja; brez obnove in življenjepisa; 250–300 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the importance of home and belonging in Nick Hornby's About a Boy and Claire Keegan's Foster.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja (primerjava dveh del)
Uvod: teza – both works show that a home is created by care and attention, not by a house or by blood ties.
Takoj povej, kaj boš dokazoval. Brez življenjepisa avtorjev in obnove zgodbe.
Jedro 1 – About a Boy: Marcus feels out of place at home and at school; Will's flat is stylish but empty. Both find belonging in an unusual 'family' at the end.
Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom (the afternoons watching Countdown at Will's flat, the trip to Cambridge).
Jedro 2 – Foster: the girl experiences neglect in her crowded family home and discovers warmth, routine and attention with the Kinsellas.
Navedi podrobnosti: washing her, the well, Kinsella's walks and the silence between them.
Jedro 3 – primerjava: in both works, the child teaches the adult something; the ending of Foster is uncertain, while About a Boy ends with a wider, hopeful network of people.
Primerjaj neposredno (Whereas …, Similarly …). To je jedro naloge, ne dve ločeni analizi.
Sklep: home is where one is seen and valued.
Sklep se vrne k tezi; ni novih podatkov.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija (tema), zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Home and belonging in About a Boy and Foster

Both Nick Hornby's About a Boy and Claire Keegan's Foster are about children who do not feel at home where they live. In both works, a home is not created by a house or by blood ties, but by care, attention and being truly seen by another person.

At the beginning of About a Boy, neither main character belongs anywhere. Marcus is bullied at school, and at home he has to look after his depressed mother, Fiona, instead of being looked after. Will's flat, on the other hand, is stylish but empty, which reflects his empty life. Gradually, the afternoons Marcus spends watching Countdown at Will's flat create a kind of home for both of them. By the end, Marcus belongs to a wider, unusual network of people, including Will, Ellie and Fiona.

In Foster, the girl is sent from her crowded, neglected family home to live with the Kinsellas for the summer. Small details show the difference: Edna washes her, gives her clean clothes and teaches her to fetch water from the well, while Kinsella takes her on evening walks to the sea. For the first time, someone pays attention to her, and silence becomes comfortable rather than frightening.

Whereas Marcus finds belonging in a group of friends, the girl finds it in a quiet couple who have lost their own son. Similarly, however, in both works the child also gives the adult a new sense of home. The ending of Foster is uncertain, as the girl must return to her family, while About a Boy ends more hopefully.

Both works therefore suggest that home is wherever we are seen and valued.

Število besed: 282 (zahtevanih 250–300). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Allotment

My grandfather had three loves: my grandmother, the radio cricket commentary and Plot 47 at the Riverside Allotments. Not necessarily in that order, my grandmother used to say.

Plot 47 was a strip of land about the size of a tennis court, rented from the town council for twelve pounds a year. Grandad had taken it over in 1971 from a retired bus driver who left him a shed, a broken wheelbarrow and a single instruction written on the shed door in white paint: "Never plant mint in the open ground." It took Grandad two summers and a great deal of digging to understand why. Mint, it turns out, spreads underground like a rumour.

I started going with him when I was seven, mostly because the allotment had a tap, a hose and a great deal of mud, and nobody seemed to mind if I combined the three. Gradually, though, I began to understand that the place had its own society. There was Mrs Okafor, who grew vegetables nobody else could name and gave them away in brown paper bags. There was Mr Lewandowski, who measured his onions with a ruler and entered them in competitions. And there was a long-running disagreement between the plots on the river side and the plots on the road side, which had started over a shared water barrel in 1985 and had never been properly resolved.

Grandad believed that you could judge a person by the state of their compost heap. His own was a work of art, built in layers like a cake: green leaves, brown cardboard, kitchen scraps, a spade of soil. He turned it every Sunday with the seriousness of a priest.

The summer I turned fifteen, Grandad's knees stopped cooperating. He could still sit in his folding chair by the shed and give instructions, but the digging became my job. I complained loudly and often. I was embarrassed when friends saw me cycling home with a bag of potatoes on the handlebars.

Then, in August, Mr Lewandowski fell ill a week before the town show, and Grandad sent me to water his onions. I measured them too, out of curiosity. The biggest was nineteen centimetres across. I entered it in his name, and it won second prize.

Grandad has been gone for four years now. I still rent Plot 47. The shed door still says "Never plant mint in the open ground." Underneath, in my own white paint, I have added: "Turn the compost on Sundays."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.What were the grandfather's three loves?
    Grandmother, cricket and the allotment.
  2. 1.How much did the plot cost per year?
  3. 2.Who had the plot before the grandfather?
  4. 3.What does mint do if it is planted in the open ground?
  5. 4.Why did the narrator like going to the allotment as a small child?
  6. 5.What did Mrs Okafor do with her vegetables?
  7. 6.What started the disagreement between the two groups of plots?
  8. 7.According to the grandfather, what could tell you about a person's character?
  9. 8.Why did the narrator have to take over the digging?
  10. 9.What embarrassed the narrator as a teenager?
  11. 10.What did the narrator add to the shed door?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Twelve pounds.
2. A retired bus driver.
3. It spreads underground.
4. To play with water and mud. / Because of the tap, hose and mud.
5. She gave them away (in paper bags).
6. A shared water barrel.
7. (The state of) their compost heap.
8. Grandad's knees were bad. / Grandad's knees stopped working.
9. Friends seeing him/her with potatoes. / Cycling home with potatoes.
10. Turn the compost on Sundays.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Twelve pounds.
»rented from the town council for twelve pounds a year«. »How much … per year« = cena na leto; »a year« v besedilu pomeni isto kot per year.
2. A retired bus driver.
»from a retired bus driver«. »Who« zahteva osebo: upokojeni voznik avtobusa.
3. It spreads underground.
»Mint … spreads underground like a rumour.« Primerjava pomeni, da se nenadzorovano širi. Primera »like a rumour« (kot govorica) pomeni, da se meta neopazno in hitro razširi pod zemljo.
4. To play with water and mud. / Because of the tap, hose and mud.
»had a tap, a hose and a great deal of mud«. »Why … like« zahteva razlog: pipa, cev in veliko blata – otrok se je igral z vodo.
5. She gave them away (in paper bags).
»gave them away in brown paper bags«. Gospa Okafor je zelenjavo podarjala (gave away), ne prodajala.
6. A shared water barrel.
»had started over a shared water barrel in 1985«. »What started« = kaj je sprožilo spor; skupen sod za vodo leta 1985.
7. (The state of) their compost heap.
»you could judge a person by the state of their compost heap«. Ded je značaj presojal po kompostnem kupu; »state« pomeni stanje.
8. Grandad's knees were bad. / Grandad's knees stopped working.
»Grandad's knees stopped cooperating«. »Knees stopped cooperating« je šaljiv izraz za bolna kolena.
9. Friends seeing him/her with potatoes. / Cycling home with potatoes.
»embarrassed when friends saw me cycling home with a bag of potatoes«. »Embarrassed« = v zadregi; najstnika je bilo sram, ko so ga prijatelji videli s krompirjem.
10. Turn the compost on Sundays.
Pripovedovalec nadaljuje dedovo navado in jo zapiše pod staro navodilo. Pripovedovalec doda dedovo navado na vrata lope; odgovor je zapisano sporočilo.

Five novels that still start arguments

Teachers love them, some parents fear them, and teenagers keep reading them. Here are five classics that regularly appear on school reading lists – and on lists of books that someone wants removed.

A To Kill a Mockingbird by Harper Lee (1960)

Told through the eyes of Scout, a young girl in a small town in Alabama, the novel follows her father's attempt to defend a Black man accused of a crime he did not commit. It won the Pulitzer Prize and has sold more than forty million copies. Some schools have taken it off the curriculum because of the racist language used by several characters, while others argue that this language is exactly what makes the book an honest lesson about injustice.

B The Hunger Games by Suzanne Collins (2008)

In a future North America, teenagers are forced to fight to the death on live television. Collins has said she got the idea while switching channels between a reality show and news from a war. Critics have complained that the book is too violent for young readers, yet many teachers use it to start discussions about the media, inequality and the way societies control people with entertainment.

C The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time by Mark Haddon (2003)

Fifteen-year-old Christopher, who is brilliant at maths but finds people confusing, decides to investigate the death of a neighbour's dog. The novel was praised for showing the world from an unusual point of view, and it became a hugely successful stage play. Haddon himself has said that he did not research the topic in depth and regrets that the book is sometimes treated as a guide to autism.

D Lord of the Flies by William Golding (1954)

A group of British schoolboys are stranded on an island after a plane crash and try to govern themselves, with terrible results. Golding, who had been a teacher, wrote the book partly as a reply to adventure stories in which shipwrecked boys behave like perfect gentlemen. It was rejected by more than twenty publishers before it was accepted, and it later helped him win the Nobel Prize.

E Wonder by R. J. Palacio (2012)

August Pullman, a boy born with a facial difference, goes to a normal school for the first time at the age of ten. Palacio wrote the novel after an incident in which her own young son reacted with fear to a girl with a similar condition. The book inspired a campaign against bullying called 'Choose Kind', and it is one of the few books on this list that almost nobody has tried to ban.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Which book has sold more than forty million copies? (A)
  2. 00.Which narrator is a young girl? (A)
  3. 000.Which book has rarely been the target of a ban? (E)
  4. 1.Which author was inspired by an event involving his or her own child?
  5. 2.Which novel had difficulty finding a publisher?
  6. 3.Which author regrets how the book is sometimes used?
  7. 4.Which novel was written partly in response to another kind of story?
  8. 5.Which book is criticised for the words some characters use?
  9. 6.Which novel was adapted for the theatre?
  10. 7.Which idea came from watching television?
  11. 8.Which book has led to a social campaign?
  12. 9.Which author had worked in education?
  13. 10.Which novel is used to talk about how entertainment can control people?

2. D

4. D

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

8. E
Kampanja proti medvrstniškemu nasilju »Choose Kind«. »social campaign« = kampanja »Choose Kind«.

The animal that makes great white sharks run away

The great white shark is one of (0) most feared predators in the ocean. Yet scientists have discovered that even this powerful hunter has an enemy it is desperate (1) avoid: the orca, or killer whale.

Researchers in California first noticed the behaviour (2) tracking sharks with electronic tags. Whenever orcas appeared near an island (3) the sharks hunted seals, the sharks left immediately – and they did not return for weeks, (4) for the rest of the season. "It was like flipping a switch," says one marine biologist. "One day the island was full of sharks, the next day it was empty."

Off the coast of South Africa, the story is even more dramatic. Since 2017, the bodies of several great whites (5) washed up on beaches with their livers missing. The liver of a shark is large, rich in fat and full of energy, (6) makes it a favourite meal for orcas. Two male orcas, known to scientists as Port and Starboard, are believed to be responsible (7) many of the attacks.

The disappearance of sharks has had consequences (8) nobody expected. Without them, other species have moved into the area, and some seal colonies have grown so quickly that they now compete with fishermen (9) food.

Scientists are still trying to understand why orcas started hunting sharks in the first place. Some think that a shortage of their usual prey has forced (10) to change their diet. Others believe it is simply a skill that one group of orcas has learned and passed on to its young, in the same way (11) humans pass on traditions.

What is clear is that the ocean's "top predator" is not always the animal we think it is. "We tend to imagine the great white (12) the king of the sea," says the biologist. "But in nature there is (13) anything as a permanent king. Even sharks have bad days." Studies like these remind us how (14) we still know about life under the waves, and how quickly the balance of an ecosystem can change when just one species changes (15) behaviour.

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. to
be desperate to + nedoločnik. be desperate to + nedoločnik = obupno si želeti.
2. while / when / by
while/when + -ing: med sledenjem; by tracking = s sledenjem. Ena beseda pred -ing: while/when (medtem ko) ali by (s tem, da).
3. where
Oziralni prislov za kraj (an island where the sharks hunted). Za island (kraj) where.
4. or
for weeks, or for the rest of the season – stopnjevanje z or. or (ali celo) poveže dve možnosti trajanja.
5. have
Present perfect od leta 2017: bodies have washed up (aktivna raba washed up). »Since 2017« zahteva present perfect: have washed up.
6. which
which se nanaša na celoten prejšnji stavek. which za vejico se nanaša na ves prejšnji stavek.
7. for
be responsible for. be responsible for = biti odgovoren za.
8. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za consequences. Oziralni zaimek za consequences (stvari): that/which.
9. for
compete with somebody for something. compete with somebody for something = tekmovati za kaj.
10. them
force somebody to do: osebni zaimek za orke (them). Predmetna oblika osebnega zaimka za orke: them.
11. that / as
in the same way that / as humans pass on traditions. in the same way that/as = na enak način kot.
12. as
imagine X as Y. imagine X as Y = predstavljati si X kot Y.
13. no
there is no such thing as … – stalna zveza. there is no such thing as = ne obstaja kaj takega.
14. little
how little we know – nasprotje znanja (neštevno). how little we know = kako malo vemo (nešteven pomen).
15. its
Svojilni zaimek za one species (ednina, žival): its behaviour. Svojilni zaimek za žival (ednina): its.

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. availability
the + samostalnik + of: available → availability. the + samostalnik + of: availability (razpoložljivost).
2. necessary
Pridevnik pred arrangements: necessity → necessary. Pridevnik pred samostalnikom arrangements: necessary.
3. frequently
Prislov ob glagolu are used: frequent → frequently. Prislov ob glagolu are used: frequently (pogosto).
4. unfortunately
Vrinjen prislov z negativnim pomenom (not suitable): un- + fortunately. Vrinjen prislov uvaja slabo novico: unfortunately.
5. accessible
fully + pridevnik: access → accessible. fully + pridevnik: accessible (dostopen).
6. arrivals / arrival
late + samostalnik: arrive → arrival(s). late + samostalnik: arrival(s).
7. appreciated
Trpnik would be appreciated. would be + 3. oblika (trpnik): appreciated.
8. failure
or + samostalnik ob Cancellations: fail → failure. Vzporedno z Cancellations samostalnik: failure (to arrive).
9. essential
is + pridevnik: essence → essential. is + pridevnik: essential (nujen).
10. atmosphere
our relaxed and friendly + samostalnik: atmospheric → atmosphere. Za pridevnikoma relaxed and friendly samostalnik: atmosphere.
11. youngest / younger
Presežnik/primernik pred guests: our youngest guests. Stopnjevanje pridevnika young pred guests: youngest/younger.
12. response
Your + samostalnik: respond → response. Your + samostalnik: response (odgovor).
13. hesitate
do not + glagol: hesitation → hesitate. do not + glagol (osnovna oblika): hesitate.
14. unforgettable
Pomen »v najboljšem smislu«: nepozaben – un- + forget + -able. »in the best sense« namiguje na pozitiven pomen: unforgettable (nepozaben).
15. warmest
With our warmest regards – presežnik. With our + presežnik + regards: warmest.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear a recording about Grace Darling, a lighthouse keeper's daughter who became a national heroine. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

In the early hours of the seventh of September 1838, a young woman looked out of a lighthouse window on the Farne Islands, off the coast of Northumberland, and saw something that would change her life. Her name was Grace Darling, she was twenty-two years old, and she had spent almost her whole life on the islands, where her father, William, was the lighthouse keeper.

That night a terrible storm was blowing. A steamship called the Forfarshire, carrying around sixty passengers and crew from Hull to Dundee, had problems with its engines and was driven onto a group of rocks called Big Harcar. The ship broke in two, and the back half sank almost immediately. Grace spotted the wreck at about a quarter to five in the morning, and through a telescope she could make out a few people clinging to the rocks.

The sea was far too rough for the lifeboat from the mainland to set out, so Grace and her father decided to row out themselves in a small fishing boat. They took the longer, more sheltered route, almost a mile, to reach the rocks. William jumped onto the rocks to help the survivors, while Grace kept the boat steady in the waves. They rescued nine people in two trips: the first time they took five, including an injured man, back to the lighthouse, and two of the rescued crew then helped William row back for the rest.

When the story appeared in the newspapers, Grace became a celebrity almost overnight. Artists travelled to the islands to paint her portrait, people wrote poems and songs about her, and she received hundreds of letters, some of them asking for a lock of her hair. Even Queen Victoria sent her fifty pounds. Grace found the attention exhausting; she was a shy person and did not understand why so much fuss was made, since her father had done just as much.

Sadly, she did not enjoy her fame for long. In 1842, just four years after the rescue, she died of tuberculosis at the age of twenty-six. Today there is a museum dedicated to her in the village of Bamburgh, and her name is still used for lifeboats around the British coast.

Grace Darling

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Grace Darling's father looked after a lighthouse. (T)
  2. 1.Grace Darling had lived on the Farne Islands for most of her life. T / F
  3. 2.The Forfarshire was travelling to Hull when it sank. T / F
  4. 3.The ship hit the rocks because of engine trouble. T / F
  5. 4.Grace saw the survivors without any help. T / F
  6. 5.The lifeboat from the mainland could not go out because of the weather. T / F
  7. 6.Grace and her father chose the shortest route to the rocks. T / F
  8. 7.Grace stayed in the boat during the rescue. T / F
  9. 8.Grace enjoyed being famous. T / F
  10. 9.Grace's name is still connected with rescue at sea today. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. T
6. F
7. T
8. F
9. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
»had spent almost her whole life on the islands«. T: »almost her whole life« = večino življenja.
2. F
Ladja je plula iz Hulla v Dundee. F: smer je obrnjena – iz Hulla v Dundee, ne v Hull.
3. T
»had problems with its engines and was driven onto a group of rocks«. T: težave z motorji so ladjo odnesle na skale.
4. F
Preživele je razločila z daljnogledom (»through a telescope«). F: preživele je videla z daljnogledom, torej s pomočjo.
5. T
»The sea was far too rough for the lifeboat … to set out«. T: morje je bilo preveč razburkano za rešilni čoln s kopnega.
6. F
Izbrala sta daljšo, bolj zaščiteno pot. F: izbrala sta daljšo, a bolj zaščiteno pot.
7. T
»Grace kept the boat steady in the waves«. T: Grace je ostala v čolnu in ga držala mirno.
8. F
Pozornost jo je utrujala, bila je sramežljiva. F: slava jo je utrujala; bila je sramežljiva.
9. T
Po njej še danes poimenujejo rešilne čolne. T: rešilni čolni še danes nosijo njeno ime.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear an interview with Dr Leila Hassan, an emergency doctor who advises colleagues in remote areas. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Hassan, you work in a London hospital, but you also help patients thousands of kilometres away. How does that work?

Dr Hassan: Through a very simple system. Doctors in remote clinics – in mountain villages, on small islands, sometimes in places affected by war – send me photographs, X-rays and short videos on their mobile phones. I look at them and we discuss the case over a video call. It's not science fiction; most of it works on an ordinary smartphone with a decent internet connection.

Interviewer: How did it all begin?

Dr Hassan: When I was a medical student, I spent a summer volunteering at a clinic in the mountains of Nepal. There was one doctor for about twenty thousand people. I remember a young boy with a broken leg who had to be carried for two days to reach us. I promised myself then that I would find a way to help places like that, even if I couldn't be there in person.

Interviewer: What kind of cases do you deal with?

Dr Hassan: Mostly emergencies – injuries, burns, difficult births. Often the local doctor knows exactly what to do but needs a second opinion before taking a big decision, like whether to send a patient on a long journey to a hospital. Sometimes I simply confirm what they already think. That confidence can save a life.

Interviewer: Are there limits to what you can do?

Dr Hassan: Of course. I can't touch the patient, and a photograph doesn't show everything. The biggest problem, though, is electricity. In many clinics, the power goes off for hours every day, so we've started giving them solar chargers. A phone with an empty battery is no use to anyone.

Interviewer: You also train volunteers.

Dr Hassan: Yes, we now have about four hundred doctors in twenty countries who give their time for free. Before they start, they do an online course about working with different cultures – how to explain things politely, how to ask questions without making a colleague feel stupid. That part is just as important as the medicine.

Interviewer: What's your next goal?

Dr Hassan: We want to translate our training materials into more languages. At the moment they exist only in English and French, which excludes many of the people who need them most.

A doctor who works from a distance

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Dr Hassan work?
    In a London hospital.
  2. 1.What do doctors in remote clinics send Dr Hassan?
  3. 2.What equipment does most of the system need?
  4. 3.Where did Dr Hassan volunteer as a student?
  5. 4.How long did the boy with the broken leg travel to the clinic?
  6. 5.Why do local doctors often contact her?
  7. 6.What is the biggest practical problem in many clinics?
  8. 7.What have they started giving clinics?
  9. 8.What is the online course for volunteers about?
  10. 9.Why do they want to translate the materials?
naloge.rezultat:
1. Photographs, X-rays and videos.
2. An (ordinary) smartphone (and internet).
3. In (the mountains of) Nepal.
4. Two days.
5. For a second opinion.
6. Electricity. / Power cuts.
7. Solar chargers.
8. Working with different cultures.
9. They exist only in English and French. / To reach more people.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Photographs, X-rays and videos.
»send me photographs, X-rays and short videos«. Zdravniki pošiljajo tri vrste gradiv; ker vprašanje sprašuje »what«, navedeš vse tri.
2. An (ordinary) smartphone (and internet).
»works on an ordinary smartphone with a decent internet connection«. »Equipment« = oprema; dovolj je navaden pametni telefon (z internetom).
3. In (the mountains of) Nepal.
»a clinic in the mountains of Nepal«. »Where« = kraj; klinika v gorah Nepala.
4. Two days.
»had to be carried for two days«. »How long« = koliko časa; dva dneva so ga nosili.
5. For a second opinion.
»needs a second opinion before taking a big decision«. »Why« = razlog; potrebujejo drugo mnenje pred veliko odločitvijo.
6. Electricity. / Power cuts.
»The biggest problem, though, is electricity.« »The biggest problem, though« – »though« opozori na novo, pomembno informacijo: elektrika.
7. Solar chargers.
»we've started giving them solar chargers«. »Started giving« = začeli dajati; solarne polnilnike, ki rešijo težavo z elektriko.
8. Working with different cultures.
»an online course about working with different cultures«. »About« = tema tečaja: delo z različnimi kulturami.
9. They exist only in English and French. / To reach more people.
Gradiva so samo v angleščini in francoščini, zato izključujejo mnoge. »Why … translate« zahteva razlog: zdaj so samo v angleščini in francoščini; dovolj je tudi namen (da dosežejo več ljudi).

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You are looking for a summer job. You have seen an advertisement from a national park in Slovenia that is looking for an English-speaking assistant at its visitor centre.

Write an e-mail of application of 120–150 words to the visitor centre manager, in which you:

  • explain why you would like to work at the visitor centre,
  • describe your skills and knowledge that are relevant for the job,
  • ask about the working hours and accommodation.
TO: info@park-visitors.si
SUBJECT: Summer job application
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-sporočilo (prošnja) z ustreznim nagovorom in zaključkom, z vsemi tremi iztočnicami (razlog, znanja, vprašanje o urniku in nastanitvi); 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. explain why you would like to work at the visitor centre
  3. describe your skills and knowledge that are relevant for the job
  4. ask about the working hours and accommodation
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba prošnje
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor, ker naslovnika ne poznaš; konec: Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak.
I am writing to apply for the position of English-speaking assistant, which was advertised on your website.
Prvi stavek pove namen in kje si oglas videl/a.
I have always been interested in nature conservation, and I would love to share my knowledge of the Julian Alps with foreign visitors.
1. iztočnica: razlog z osebno noto.
I am a final-year secondary school student, I speak fluent English and some German, and I have completed a first aid course.
2. iztočnica: znanja, ki se ujemajo z delom (jeziki, delo z ljudmi, poznavanje okolja).
Could you please let me know what the working hours would be and whether accommodation is provided?
3. iztočnica: vljudno vprašanje (Could you … / I would be grateful if …).
I look forward to hearing from you. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni zaključek. Brez skrajšanih oblik.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of English-speaking assistant at your visitor centre, which I saw advertised on your website.

I would like to work at the visitor centre because I love the mountains and spend most weekends hiking in the Julian Alps. I would be happy to share my enthusiasm with visitors from abroad.

I believe I have the right skills for the job. I speak fluent English and basic German, and I am friendly and patient with people. Last summer I worked at a tourist information office in Bled, where I answered questions and sold tickets. I also know a lot about local plants and animals.

Could you please tell me what the working hours are? I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided for assistants.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Tina Golob

Število besed: 147 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Schools should teach students how to manage money.
  2. Famous people have a duty to be good role models.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, dvema ali tremi argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (e.g. I strongly believe that financial education belongs in every school).
Teza v uvodu.
Argument 1 + primer: young people sign phone contracts and use online payments without understanding interest or debt.
Konkreten primer prepriča bolj kot splošna trditev.
Argument 2 + primer: families cannot always teach this; school gives everyone the same chance.
Povezovalci: Moreover, In addition.
Protiargument: the curriculum is already overloaded. Zavrnitev: it could be part of maths lessons.
Upoštevaj nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi.
Sklep: povzemi stališče.
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: young fans copy celebrities; influence brings responsibility. Against: celebrities are ordinary people; parents and teachers are the real role models.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Schools should teach students how to manage money.

Every year, young people leave school able to solve equations and analyse poems, yet many of them have no idea how to plan a monthly budget. For this reason, I strongly agree that schools should teach students how to manage money.

Firstly, financial mistakes made at a young age can have serious consequences. Many students take out loans or buy expensive phones in instalments without understanding interest rates. A few lessons on budgeting and debt could prevent years of problems and help young people avoid falling into debt traps.

Secondly, not all students can learn about money at home. Some parents are not confident with finances themselves, while others prefer not to discuss them. If financial education were part of the curriculum, every student would have the same chance to learn these essential skills. In our school, an economics teacher once organised a workshop on saving, and many of my classmates said it was the most useful lesson of the year.

Critics argue that the timetable is already overloaded and that money management is the responsibility of families. However, it would not require a new subject; basic financial topics could easily be included in mathematics or social studies.

To sum up, teaching students how to manage money would make them more independent and better prepared for adult life.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Sleeper

Nobody in the village of Upper Wendle could remember exactly when Old Tobias had fallen asleep, only that it had been a Tuesday, that it had been raining, and that he had gone into the woods to look for a lost goat.

He was found two days later under an oak tree, breathing peacefully, with the goat grazing beside him. They carried him home on a door, laid him on his bed, and waited for him to wake up. He did not. The doctor came from the market town, listened to his heart, shone a light into his eyes, and pronounced him perfectly healthy, "apart from the obvious". He prescribed fresh air and patience, charged a guinea, and left.

At first the village treated the matter as an inconvenience. Tobias was the only man who knew how to repair the church clock, and within a month it had stopped at twenty past three. His wife, Martha, took over his duties at the mill, and found – somewhat to her own surprise – that she was better at the accounts than he had ever been. The baker's boy was sent every morning with a bowl of soup, which Martha fed to the sleeping man with a spoon, and which he swallowed without opening his eyes.

Years passed. Children who had been born after Tobias fell asleep were taken to see him as a kind of local attraction, and a few brave ones were allowed to touch his beard, which by now reached his belt. A travelling scientist wrote an article about him for a London journal, describing him as "a living clock that has stopped". The vicar preached sermons about him as an example of the patience of God.

Twenty years after he had gone into the woods, Tobias opened his eyes, sat up and asked for his goat. He was, everyone agreed later, remarkably calm about the whole thing. He walked to the inn, where he failed to recognise anyone, and was mildly offended when nobody recognised him either. He spoke confidently about the price of wheat, which had tripled, and about the young king, who had been dead for eleven years.

What troubled him most was not that the world had changed, but that it had managed so well without him. The mill was prospering. The church clock had been replaced by a new one from Birmingham. And Martha, he discovered, had been running the parish council for a decade.

"You might have waited," he said to her.
"I did," said Martha. "For about a week."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.On what day of the week did Tobias fall asleep?
    (On a) Tuesday.
  2. 1.Why did Tobias go into the woods?
  3. 2.How was Tobias transported home?
  4. 3.What treatment did the doctor recommend?
  5. 4.What practical problem did Tobias's sleep cause the village?
  6. 5.What did Martha discover about herself at the mill?
  7. 6.How did the children of the village see Tobias?
  8. 7.How did the scientist describe Tobias?
  9. 8.What was the first thing Tobias asked for when he woke up?
  10. 9.What upset Tobias most after he woke up?
  11. 10.How long did Martha wait before getting on with her life?
naloge.rezultat:
1. To look for a lost goat.
2. On a door.
3. Fresh air and patience.
4. The church clock stopped. / Nobody could repair the clock.
5. She was good at (the) accounts.
6. As a (local) attraction.
7. As a living clock that has stopped.
8. His goat.
9. That the world managed without him.
10. About a week.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. To look for a lost goat.
»gone into the woods to look for a lost goat«. »Why« zahteva namen: iskal je izgubljeno kozo.
2. On a door.
»They carried him home on a door«. »How … transported« = kako so ga prenesli: na vratih (namesto nosil).
3. Fresh air and patience.
»He prescribed fresh air and patience«. Zdravnik je predpisal svež zrak in potrpljenje; oboje je del odgovora.
4. The church clock stopped. / Nobody could repair the clock.
Tobias je edini znal popraviti cerkveno uro, ki se je ustavila. Ker je bil Tobias edini, ki je znal popraviti uro, se je ura ustavila.
5. She was good at (the) accounts.
»she was better at the accounts than he had ever been«. Martha je odkrila, da je boljša v računovodstvu kot mož.
6. As a (local) attraction.
»taken to see him as a kind of local attraction«. Otroci so ga hodili gledat kot lokalno znamenitost.
7. As a living clock that has stopped.
Citat iz članka: »a living clock that has stopped«. Znanstvenik je uporabil metaforo: živa ura, ki se je ustavila.
8. His goat.
»asked for his goat«. Prvo, kar je vprašal, je bila koza – humoren preobrat.
9. That the world managed without him.
»not that the world had changed, but that it had managed so well without him«. Najbolj ga je prizadelo, da je svet dobro shajal brez njega.
10. About a week.
Ironičen konec: »For about a week.« Ironični konec »For about a week« pomeni, da je čakala le kak teden.

The quiet power of Victorian women writers

They were told to stay at home – so they turned home into the most important stage in literature.

In the nineteenth century, a respectable middle-class woman was expected to marry, run a household and avoid public life. [0] Yet some of the most influential writers of the age were women who used the narrow world they knew to say something about society as a whole.

Many of them began by hiding who they were. Mary Ann Evans published under the name George Eliot, and the three Brontë sisters first appeared as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell. [1] As Charlotte Brontë later explained, they feared that critics would judge their work differently if they knew it had been written by women.

Their fears were justified. When the truth came out, some reviewers who had praised the novels suddenly found them "coarse" or "unnatural". [2] Charlotte complained bitterly that critics paid more attention to her sex than to her sentences.

The home, which was supposed to limit these writers, became their greatest subject. In novels such as Jane Eyre and Middlemarch, kitchens, drawing rooms and bedrooms are places of conflict, ambition and moral choice. [3] Readers recognised their own lives in these pages, and the novels sold in enormous numbers.

Money mattered, too. For many women, writing was one of the very few respectable ways of earning an income. [4] Elizabeth Gaskell used her earnings to buy a house for her family, a purchase she kept secret from her husband until the deal was done.

Not all women writers were rebels. Some, like Charlotte Yonge, wrote stories that celebrated obedience and duty. [5] Their success shows how varied the female reading public was, and how much publishers depended on it.

By the end of the century, the situation had begun to change. [6] More women went to university, worked as journalists and spoke at public meetings. Novelists such as Thomas Hardy and George Gissing began to write about "the new woman", who wanted independence rather than marriage.

Today, critics often read Victorian novels by women as early feminist texts. [7] Many of these writers would not have used the word "feminist" at all, and some were openly opposed to women voting.

What unites them is perhaps less a political programme than a determination to be taken seriously. [8] It is a demand that still sounds familiar today. And their books, unlike many written by the famous men who reviewed them, are still read in classrooms around the world. [9]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AThis interpretation is not entirely wrong, but it can be misleading.
  2. BIn other words, they insisted that a story about a governess could be as important as a story about a general.
  3. CEven the best-selling ones were often paid far less than their male colleagues.
  4. DWriting novels was not part of this plan.
  5. EMarried women gained the right to keep their own property, and education slowly opened up.
  6. FThe names were carefully chosen to be neither clearly male nor clearly female.
  7. GOne critic even suggested that a woman who could write such a book must have lost her femininity.
  8. HPerhaps that is the final irony of their story.
  9. IHer books were especially popular with the clergy and with parents choosing presents for their daughters.
  10. JA woman's decision about whom to marry can carry as much weight as a battle.
  11. KTheir husbands usually approved of their literary work.
  12. LMost of them never earned anything from their books.
naloge.rezultat:
1. F
2. G
3. J
4. C
5. I
6. E
7. A
8. B
9. H
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. F
Psevdonimi Brontëjevih – naslednja poved pojasni, zakaj so skrile spol. Poved o skrbno izbranih imenih (ne moških ne ženskih) uvede psevdonime; naslednja pojasni razlog.
2. G
Nadaljuje misel o kritikih, ki so knjige nenadoma ocenili kot »nenaravne«. »even« stopnjuje kritiko: kritik je trdil, da je pisateljica izgubila ženskost.
3. J
Poved konkretizira, kako so dom in odločitve v njem prizorišče konflikta. Poved pokaže, da je odločitev o poroki lahko tako pomembna kot bitka – dom kot prizorišče konflikta.
4. C
Za »Money mattered« in pred zgledom Gaskell – omejitev: plačane so bile manj kot moški. »Even the best-selling ones« omeji trditev o denarju: tudi najuspešnejše so bile plačane manj.
5. I
Her se nanaša na Charlotte Yonge; zgodbe o poslušnosti so bile priljubljene pri duhovščini in starših. »Her« se nanaša na Charlotte Yonge; poved pove, kdo je knjige bral.
6. E
Konec stoletja: spremembe (lastnina, izobrazba), naslednja poved nadaljuje z univerzo in novinarstvom. Poved našteje spremembe ob koncu stoletja; naslednja nadaljuje z univerzo.
7. A
»This interpretation« se nanaša na branje kot feminističnih besedil; nato sledi omejitev. »This interpretation« se nanaša na prej omenjeno feministično branje.
8. B
In other words razloži »determination to be taken seriously«. »In other words« razloži prejšnjo misel z drugimi besedami.
9. H
Zadnja poved: ironija, da se berejo bolj kot knjige moških kritikov. Zaključna poved: ironija, da jih danes berejo bolj kot moške kritike.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take

which se nanaša na celoten prejšnji stavek. which za vejico se nanaša na ves prejšnji stavek.

Prislov med modalnim glagolom in nedoločnikom. Prislov med modalnim glagolom in nedoločnikom: also/even.

Oziralni zaimek za guidebook. Oziralni zaimek za guidebook: that/which.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).

5. to see

6. control
Splošna resnica: present simple, množina (parts). Splošna resnica, osebek množina: control.
7. hunted
Sklep o preteklosti s probably: past simple. »probably« s sklepom o preteklosti: hunted.
8. to swim
wait for somebody to do something: waited for fish to swim past. wait for somebody to do something: to swim.
9. hadn't had / had not had
Tretji pogojnik: if + past perfect. Tretji pogojnik: if + past perfect (hadn't had).
10. would have had
Hipotetična preteklost: would have + 3. oblika. Posledica v tretjem pogojniku: would have had.
11. were published / have been published
Trpnik; since + past simple (were published). Trpnik (rezultate je nekdo objavil): were/have been published.
12. may not fill
Modalni glagol + nedoločnik brez to. may + nedoločnik brez to: may not fill.

14. will have scanned
By the end of this decade – future perfect. by the end of this decade → future perfect: will have scanned.
15. will have disappeared
Future perfect: do takrat bo že izginila. Future perfect: do tedaj bo že izginila.
