Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Has the word "autism" become too broad?

For decades, autism was thought to be rare and (0) (DEBILITATE). Today, it is diagnosed far more often, and many of those diagnosed live (1) (INDEPENDENCE) lives, study at university and hold demanding jobs. Some experts now ask whether a single word can still describe such a wide range of (2) (EXPERIENCED).

The change is partly the result of greater (3) (AWARE). Teachers and doctors are better at recognising the signs, and adults who struggled for years without knowing why are finally receiving a (4) (DIAGNOSE). Many describe the moment as a huge (5) (RELIEVE).

At the same time, the "neurodiversity" movement has encouraged people to see autism not as an illness but as a natural (6) (VARY) in the way human brains work. Supporters argue that this view reduces stigma and celebrates the (7) (STRONG) of autistic people, such as attention to detail and honesty.

Critics, however, worry that the focus on (8) (SUCCESS) autistic adults hides the needs of those who are most severely affected. Some parents of children who cannot speak or look after themselves feel that their situation has become (9) (VISIBLE) in public debate. "When people say autism is a superpower, they are not talking about my son," says one mother.

Researchers are divided on the best (10) (SOLVE). Some propose separate categories for different levels of support, while others fear that this would bring back old (11) (DIVIDE) between "high-functioning" and "low-functioning" people, terms that many find (12) (OFFEND).

What both sides agree on is that services are under enormous pressure. Waiting lists for (13) (ASSESS) in some areas are now longer than two years, and families often feel (14) (HELP) while they wait. Whatever the label, they say, what really matters is that every person receives the support they need, as early and as (15) (APPROPRIATE) as possible.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. independent
Pridevnik pred lives: independence → independent. Pridevnik pred lives: independent.
2. experiences
a wide range of + samostalnik v množini. Za range of množina: experiences.
3. awareness
greater + samostalnik: aware → awareness. greater + samostalnik: awareness (ozaveščenost).
4. diagnosis
a + samostalnik: diagnose → diagnosis. a + samostalnik: diagnosis.
5. relief
a huge + samostalnik: relieve → relief. a huge + samostalnik: relief (olajšanje).
6. variation
a natural + samostalnik: vary → variation. a natural + samostalnik: variation.
7. strengths
the + samostalnik v množini (attention to detail, honesty). Našteti so prednosti (več) → množina: strengths.
8. successful
Pridevnik pred adults: success → successful. Pridevnik pred adults: successful.
9. invisible
Občutek, da njihova situacija ni vidna: in- + visible. Občutek, da jih nihče ne vidi: in- + visible.
10. solution
the best + samostalnik: solve → solution. the best + samostalnik: solution.
11. divisions
old + samostalnik v množini: divide → divisions. old + samostalnik v množini: divisions (delitve).
12. offensive
find + pridevnik: offend → offensive. find something + pridevnik: offensive (žaljiv).
13. assessment / assessments
Samostalnik: assess → assessment. Samostalnik: assessment (ocena, presoja).
14. helpless
feel + pridevnik: brez pomoči – help + -less. feel + pridevnik; -less pomeni »brez«: helpless (nemočen).
15. appropriately
as early and as … as possible – prislov: appropriately. as early and as … as possible – vzporedno s prislovom early: appropriately.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Anna Berg, a Norwegian free diver who swims under frozen lakes. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Anna, you hold a world record for swimming under ice without breathing equipment. How far did you swim?

Anna: Ninety-five metres, in a lake in northern Norway, on a single breath. The water was about two degrees, and the ice above me was half a metre thick. I wore only a swimsuit, goggles and a hat.

Interviewer: Why no wetsuit?

Anna: For this record the rules don't allow one. Many people think that's crazy, but the body is surprisingly well designed for cold. In the first seconds your heart rate drops and the blood moves away from your arms and legs towards the organs that matter most. It's called the diving reflex, and every human has it, even babies.

Interviewer: How did you get into this sport?

Anna: I grew up on a farm next to a lake, and my grandmother swam in it every morning, all year round. When I was twelve she took me with her in January. I screamed, but I was hooked. I didn't start free diving seriously until I was thirty, after a difficult divorce. I needed something that made my mind completely quiet.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Anna: Very, if you're careless. Under ice you can't simply come up for air – you have to find the hole you went in through. So we drill a second hole every twenty-five metres in case something goes wrong, and I'm connected to a safety line. I have a team of six divers and a doctor with me. The cold isn't the biggest risk. Panic is.

Interviewer: How do you train?

Anna: Mostly in a normal swimming pool, and on land. I do yoga and breathing exercises, and I spend a lot of time in cold showers. Mental training is half the work. Before a dive I imagine every metre, every stroke, until it feels like something I've already done.

Interviewer: What's next?

Anna: I want to use the attention to talk about climate change. The lakes where I train used to freeze in November. Now we sometimes wait until January. In twenty years, there may not be enough ice for this sport at all.

Swimming under the ice

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

  1. 0.Anna swam under the ice without ___.
    breathing equipment
  2. 1.Anna set her record in a lake in ___.
  3. 2.During the record, the ice above her was ___.
  4. 3.Apart from a swimsuit, Anna wore ___.
  5. 4.When the body enters cold water, the ___ drops.
  6. 5.Anna started free diving seriously at the age of ___.
  7. 6.For safety, Anna is connected to ___.
  8. 7.Anna is accompanied by six divers and ___.
  9. 8.Before a dive, Anna imagines ___.
  10. 9.Anna wants to use her fame to talk about ___.
naloge.rezultat:
1. northern Norway
2. half a metre thick
3. goggles and a hat
4. heart rate
5. thirty
6. a safety line
7. a doctor
8. every metre (and every stroke)
9. climate change
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. northern Norway
»in a lake in northern Norway«. »in« + kraj: northern Norway (oba dela sta del podatka).
2. half a metre thick
»the ice above me was half a metre thick«. Za »was« pridevniška zveza: half a metre thick.
3. goggles and a hat
»only a swimsuit, goggles and a hat«. »Apart from a swimsuit« izključi kopalke; ostaneta očala in kapa.
4. heart rate
»your heart rate drops«. »the ___ drops« – manjka samostalnik: heart rate (srčni utrip).
5. thirty
»I didn't start … until I was thirty«. »at the age of« + število: thirty.
6. a safety line
»I'm connected to a safety line«. »connected to« + samostalnik: a safety line.
7. a doctor
»a team of six divers and a doctor«. »six divers and« + oseba: a doctor.
8. every metre (and every stroke)
»I imagine every metre, every stroke«. »imagines« + predmet: every metre.
9. climate change
»to talk about climate change«. »talk about« + tema: climate change.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Dr Mia Torres about communication among wild chimpanzees. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Torres, you've spent fifteen years watching chimpanzees in Uganda. What were you looking for?

Dr Torres: Gestures. Chimpanzees use their voices, of course, but they also use their hands, faces and bodies to send very specific messages. We've now recorded more than seventy different gestures, and we're still finding new ones.

Interviewer: How do you study animals that live high in the trees?

Dr Torres: With enormous patience. The first rule is to behave as boringly as possible. If you're quiet and predictable, after a few months the chimps stop paying attention to you, and that's when they show you their real lives. I spend most days sitting on the ground with a video camera and a notebook, often for ten hours at a time.

Interviewer: Can you give an example of a gesture?

Dr Torres: One of my favourites is a gentle touch on the back of another chimp's hand. It means 'let's go' – a mother uses it with her baby when she wants to move on. Another is a loud slap on the ground, which is a way of saying 'stop that' or 'go away'. What's fascinating is that the meanings seem to be the same in different groups that have never met.

Interviewer: Does that tell us something about human language?

Dr Torres: We think it might. Babies point and wave long before they can speak, and many of their gestures look very similar to those of young chimps. One study even found that adults could guess the meaning of chimpanzee gestures from videos more often than chance would predict. That suggests that our ancestors may have communicated with their hands before they used words.

Interviewer: What are the biggest threats to the chimps you study?

Dr Torres: Loss of forest, mainly to farming, and diseases that humans pass on to them – a simple cold can kill a chimpanzee. That's why researchers in our project wear masks and keep a distance of at least seven metres.

How chimpanzees talk to each other

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Where does Dr Torres study chimpanzees?
    In Uganda.
  2. 1.How many different chimpanzee gestures have been recorded?
  3. 2.What is the first rule when studying chimpanzees?
  4. 3.What equipment does Dr Torres use in the forest?
  5. 4.What does a gentle touch on the back of the hand mean?
  6. 5.What does a loud slap on the ground mean?
  7. 6.What is surprising about the meanings of the gestures?
  8. 7.What do babies do before they can speak?
  9. 8.Why do researchers wear masks?
naloge.rezultat:
1. More than seventy.
2. To behave as boringly as possible. / To be quiet and predictable.
3. A video camera and a notebook.
4. Let's go.
5. Stop that. / Go away.
6. They are the same in different groups.
7. Point and wave.
8. To protect chimps from human diseases.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. More than seventy.
»more than seventy different gestures«. »How many« = število; »more than« je del podatka.
2. To behave as boringly as possible. / To be quiet and predictable.
»behave as boringly as possible«. »The first rule« v vprašanju ustreza pravilu, ki ga dr. Torres navede prvo; »boringly« pomeni, da šimpanzov ne vznemirjaš.
3. A video camera and a notebook.
»with a video camera and a notebook«. »Equipment« = oprema; navedeš oba predmeta (kamera in zvezek).
4. Let's go.
»It means 'let's go'«. Pomen geste pove s premim govorom: 'let's go' (gremo).
5. Stop that. / Go away.
Dovolj je ena od obeh razlag. Govorec navede dve razlagi udarca po tleh; zadošča ena.
6. They are the same in different groups.
»the meanings seem to be the same in different groups that have never met«. »Surprising« = presenetljivo; pomeni so enaki v skupinah, ki se nikoli niso srečale.
7. Point and wave.
»Babies point and wave long before they can speak«. »Before they can speak« = preden znajo govoriti; dojenčki kažejo in mahajo, kar je podobno gestam šimpanzov.
8. To protect chimps from human diseases.
Človeške bolezni so za šimpanze smrtno nevarne; zato maske in razdalja. »Why« zahteva namen: zaščititi šimpanze pred človeškimi boleznimi (ne obratno).

E-mail

You are a young amateur musician who wants to improve your skills. You have seen the following advertisement:

THE LONDON SUMMER ACADEMY OF MUSIC
Intensive 4-week course for young performers (16–20)
For talented and committed musicians with stage experience • Audition required (video accepted)
Fee: £3,500 • Scholarships available

Your notes on the advertisement: what instruments? / accommodation? / online lessons after the course?

Using the information from the advertisement and your notes, write an e-mail of application of 150–180 words, in which you:

  • explain why you are a suitable candidate for a scholarship,
  • ask about the information in your notes.
TO: admissions@londonsummermusic.co.uk
SUBJECT: Scholarship application
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalna prošnja, ki utemelji primernost za štipendijo (izkušnje, dosežki, finančni razlog) in v posrednih vprašanjih vpraša o vseh treh opombah; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain why you are a suitable candidate for a scholarship
  3. ask about the information in your notes
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba prošnje
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor.
I am writing to apply for a place on your summer course and for one of the scholarships mentioned in your advertisement.
Namen v prvem stavku: prijava in štipendija.
I have played the cello for nine years, performed as a soloist with my school orchestra and won second prize at a national competition.
Dokazi, da izpolnjuješ pogoje (talent, izkušnje na odru).
Since my family could not afford the full fee, a scholarship would make it possible for me to attend.
Utemeljitev, zakaj štipendija – vljudno in stvarno.
I would be grateful if you could tell me which instruments are included, whether accommodation is provided, and if online lessons continue after the course.
Vse tri opombe v posrednih vprašanjih.
I look forward to your reply. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni zaključek.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for a place on your four-week summer course and for one of the scholarships mentioned in your advertisement.

I am a seventeen-year-old cellist from Slovenia. I believe I am a suitable candidate for a scholarship because I am both committed and experienced on stage. I practise at least three hours a day, and last year I won second prize at the national competition for young musicians. I also perform regularly with our regional youth orchestra. Unfortunately, my family cannot afford the full fee of £3,500, so a scholarship would make it possible for me to attend.

I would be grateful if you could answer a few questions. First, which instruments are included in the course? Secondly, is accommodation provided for students from abroad, and if so, is it included in the fee? Finally, are there any online lessons available after the course ends?

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Nika Kralj

Število besed: 164 (zahtevanih 150–180). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the importance of memory in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.

Kazuo Ishiguro: Never Let Me Go

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej s tezo o pomenu spomina, podprt s pripovedno obliko (Kathy se spominja), s simboli (kaseta, Norfolk) in s koncem romana; 250–300 besed, brez obnove.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the importance of memory in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – for Kathy, memory is the only thing she can truly own; remembering is her way of giving meaning to a short life.
Teza na začetku; brez življenjepisa avtorja.
Jedro 1 – the narrative itself: Kathy tells the story as a carer looking back on Hailsham; her memories are selective and sometimes unreliable ('I may be wrong').
Pokaži, kako oblika romana (pripoved v spominih) podpira temo.
Jedro 2 – objects and places: the lost cassette tape and Norfolk, 'England's lost corner', where lost things are found.
Simboli spomina in izgube; razloži pomen.
Jedro 3 – loss: as Ruth and Tommy die, Kathy keeps them alive by remembering; at the end she says she will not lose her memories of them.
Poveži s koncem romana.
Sklep: memory gives the clones identity and dignity that society denies them.
Vrnitev k tezi.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Memory in Never Let Me Go

In Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go, memory is not just the way the story is told; it is the main thing that gives the characters' short lives meaning. Kathy H., the narrator, looks back on Hailsham, the Cottages and her years as a carer because her memories are the only possession that no one can take from her.

The whole novel is a long act of remembering. Kathy often corrects herself, admits that she may be wrong or says that Ruth remembered an event differently. This uncertainty shows that memory is personal and fragile, but also precious. By telling her story, Kathy tries to keep Ruth and Tommy alive after they have "completed".

Objects play an important role in this process. At Hailsham, the students collect their treasures in wooden boxes, and Kathy treasures a cassette with the song "Never Let Me Go". When she loses it, she and Tommy later find a copy in Norfolk, the "lost corner" of England. The scene suggests that lost things, and lost people, can be recovered in memory.

Memory also connects the clones with the donors they care for. One donor asks Kathy to describe Hailsham again and again, so that he can borrow her memories as if they were his own. This moment reveals how much people need a past in order to feel human.

At the end, Kathy stands by a fence in Norfolk, imagines Tommy appearing and then drives away. She accepts her fate, but she will keep her memories until the end. Ishiguro thus suggests that memory is what makes a life, however short, truly one's own.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

Twenty Years: a documentary about waiting

How long can a family wait for someone? In the remarkable documentary Twenty Years, director Ana Ruiz follows a woman from Texas, Denise Carter, whose husband was sentenced to twenty years in prison for his part in a robbery in which nobody was hurt. Denise was twenty-four at the time, with two small sons and no job.

The film is built almost entirely from home videos. Denise started recording messages for her husband on a cheap camera the week he went to prison, so that he would not miss his sons growing up. Over two decades she filled more than three hundred tapes: birthday parties, first days at school, a broken arm, a graduation. Ruiz found the tapes by chance, when Denise mentioned them during a radio interview, and spent four years editing them.

What makes the film so powerful is that it is not only about prison. It is about the strange, stretched kind of time that families live in when someone is missing. In the early tapes, Denise is angry and frightened. Later she is tired, then determined. She goes back to college, becomes a teacher and starts a campaign for shorter sentences for non-violent crimes.

Her sons, Marcus and Jay, are perhaps the film's real heroes. As children, they speak to the camera as if their father were in the room. As teenagers, they refuse to record anything at all. One of the most moving scenes shows Jay, aged sixteen, finally sitting down in front of the camera and saying nothing for almost a minute before he begins to cry.

The film does not ask us to feel sorry for the father. He made a terrible mistake, and he says so. What it asks is whether a punishment that lasts twenty years punishes only the person who committed the crime. Ruiz never answers the question directly. Instead, she lets the tapes speak.

The ending, when the father is finally released, is shown without music. He walks out of the gate, looks at two grown men he hardly recognises, and asks if he can hold the camera. It is one of the most powerful final scenes I have seen in years.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.How long was the husband's sentence?
    Twenty years.
  2. 1.What was the husband's crime?
  3. 2.Why did Denise start recording videos?
  4. 3.How many tapes did Denise record?
  5. 4.How did the director learn about the tapes?
  6. 5.What job did Denise get later?
  7. 6.What does Denise's campaign aim for?
  8. 7.How did the sons behave towards the camera as teenagers?
  9. 8.What question does the film raise about long sentences?
  10. 9.What does the father ask for at the end?
naloge.rezultat:
1. (Taking part in) a robbery.
2. So her husband wouldn't miss his sons growing up.
3. More than three hundred.
4. From a radio interview.
5. (A) teacher.
6. Shorter sentences for non-violent crimes.
7. They refused to record. / They wouldn't record anything.
8. Whether they punish only the criminal. / Whether families are punished too.
9. To hold the camera.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. (Taking part in) a robbery.
»for his part in a robbery«. »Crime« = kaznivo dejanje; v besedilu »his part in a robbery« – sodeloval je pri ropu.
2. So her husband wouldn't miss his sons growing up.
»so that he would not miss his sons growing up«. »Why« zahteva namen: da mož ne bi zamudil odraščanja sinov (so that he would not miss …).
3. More than three hundred.
»more than three hundred tapes«. »How many« = število; »more than« je del podatka, zato ga ne izpustiš.
4. From a radio interview.
»when Denise mentioned them during a radio interview«. »How did … learn« = kako je izvedel; prek radijskega intervjuja, v katerem jih je Denise omenila.
5. (A) teacher.
»becomes a teacher«. »What job« = poklic; odgovor je samostalnik teacher.
6. Shorter sentences for non-violent crimes.
»a campaign for shorter sentences for non-violent crimes«. »Aim for« = kaj želi doseči; krajše kazni za nenasilna kazniva dejanja. Oba dela (shorter, non-violent) sta bistvena.
7. They refused to record. / They wouldn't record anything.
»As teenagers, they refuse to record anything at all.« Kot najstnika sta zavrnila snemanje; »refuse to record anything« pove nasprotno od otroštva, ko sta snemala rada.
8. Whether they punish only the criminal. / Whether families are punished too.
»whether a punishment … punishes only the person who committed the crime«. Film postavi vprašanje, ali kazen kaznuje le storilca ali tudi družino; dovolj je ena od parafraz.
9. To hold the camera.
»asks if he can hold the camera«. Na koncu oče prosi, ali lahko drži kamero – simbol, da zdaj on beleži družino.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentence parts below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence part can be used only once. There are two extra sentence parts which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (M).

The last two northern white rhinos

The day the last male northern white rhino died, his keepers sat beside him in the rain, [0]. His name was Sudan, he was forty-five years old, and with his death in 2018 only two members of his subspecies remained on Earth: his daughter Najin and granddaughter Fatu.

The two females live in a nature reserve in Kenya, [1]. Neither of them can carry a pregnancy, and without a male, the subspecies seemed certain to disappear.

Northern white rhinos were once found across several countries in central Africa. Their numbers fell dramatically in the 1970s and 1980s, [2]. Rhino horn, which is made of the same material as human fingernails, is still believed in some countries to cure illnesses, [3].

The story might have ended there. However, before Sudan died, scientists collected and froze samples of his sperm, [4]. They have since removed eggs from Fatu and used them to create embryos in a laboratory in Italy, [5].

The plan is to place these embryos in a southern white rhino, a close relative, [6]. In 2024 the team announced the first successful pregnancy of this kind using southern white embryos, [7].

Not everyone supports the project. Some conservationists argue that the money – millions of euros – would be better spent protecting species [8]. Others point out that a population created from a handful of animals will have very little genetic variety, [9].

The scientists accept that the criticism is fair. But they believe the techniques they are developing could also help other endangered animals. "If we can do this for the northern white rhino," says one of the team, "we can do it for species [10]."

For the keepers in Kenya, the work is more personal. Every day they walk with Najin and Fatu, feed them carrots and talk to them, [11]. "They are not a scientific project to us," says one of them. "They are family."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. Awhere they are guarded day and night by armed rangers
  2. Bwhich can live for up to fifty years
  3. Calthough there is no scientific evidence for this
  4. Dwhich will act as a surrogate mother
  5. Ethat still have a chance of survival in the wild
  6. Fas if the animals could understand every word
  7. Gas hunters killed thousands of animals for their horns
  8. Hthat are disappearing right now
  9. Iwhich are now stored in liquid nitrogen
  10. Jwhich makes them vulnerable to disease
  11. Ktogether with the eggs of other, already dead females
  12. Lwhich proved that the method works
  13. Mknowing that they were saying goodbye to a whole subspecies
  14. Nbecause rhinos have very poor eyesight
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. G
3. C
4. K
5. I
6. D
7. L
8. E
9. J
10. H
11. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
Rezervat, kjer ju noč in dan varujejo oboroženi čuvaji (where se nanaša na kraj). Za »reserve« (kraj) sledi where; pomen: varujejo ju čuvaji podnevi in ponoči.
2. G
as = ker: lovci so pobijali živali zaradi rogov – razlog za upad. as tu pomeni »ker«; del pove razlog, zakaj je nosorogov hitro zmanjkalo.
3. C
although – nasprotje: verjamejo v zdravilnost, a ni dokazov. although uvede nasprotje: ljudje verjamejo v zdravilnost roga, čeprav ni dokazov.
4. K
Zamrznili so spermo skupaj z jajčeci že poginulih samic. »together with« doda, kaj so še zamrznili: jajčeca drugih, že poginulih samic.
5. I
Zarodki so zdaj shranjeni v tekočem dušiku (which → embryos). which se nanaša na zarodke (embryos) iz prejšnjega stavka; zdaj so v tekočem dušiku.
6. D
Južni beli nosorog bo nadomestna mati. which uvede vlogo južnega belega nosoroga: bo nadomestna mati.
7. L
Uspešna brejost je dokazala, da metoda deluje. which se nanaša na celo uspešno brejost; ta je dokazala, da metoda deluje.
8. E
Denar bi raje porabili za vrste, ki imajo še možnost preživetja v naravi. that za species: vrste, ki še imajo možnost preživeti v naravi – nasprotje skoraj izumrlega nosoroga.
9. J
Majhna genska raznolikost – zato so dovzetne za bolezni. which se nanaša na majhno gensko raznolikost; posledica je dovzetnost za bolezni.
10. H
Tehnike bi pomagale vrstam, ki izginjajo prav zdaj. that za species; »right now« poudari nujnost.
11. F
Govorijo z njima, kot da bi razumeli vsako besedo. as if = kot da bi; čuvaji govorijo z živalma, kot da bi razumeli vsako besedo.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Why some chefs are giving up avocados

Give peas a chance – as well (0) broad beans and pistachios. A growing number of restaurants in Britain have taken avocados off their menus, arguing that the fashionable fruit has become (1) expensive for the planet.

Avocados need huge amounts of water. It takes around 320 litres to grow a single fruit, and (2) of the world's avocados are grown in dry regions of Mexico, Peru and Chile. In some areas, farmers have been accused of illegally taking water from rivers, leaving local villages (3) enough for drinking.

The fruit's popularity has (4) caused other problems. In Mexico, forests have been cut down to make room for avocado farms, and criminal gangs have taken control (5) parts of the trade. Because avocados are transported thousands of kilometres, often by air, (6) carbon footprint is also high.

"I love avocados as (7) as anyone," says one London chef who removed them from her menu last year. "But I couldn't keep serving something (8) I knew was causing so much damage." Instead, she now makes a green spread from British peas, mint and lemon, (9) she says many customers prefer.

Not everyone is convinced. Some experts argue (10) singling out one fruit is unfair, since meat, cheese and coffee also have a large environmental impact. Others point out that millions of small farmers depend on avocados for (11) living, and that a boycott could hurt them more than the big companies.

What most people agree on is that consumers should think more about (12) their food comes from. Buying fruit that is in season and grown closer to home is (13) of the simplest ways to reduce our impact. "Nobody is saying you can (14) eat another avocado," says the chef. "Just eat them less often – and enjoy them more (15) you do."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

naloge.rezultat:
1. too
2. most / many / much
3. without
4. also
5. of
6. their
7. much
8. that / which
9. which
10. that
11. a / their
12. where

14. never / not
15. when
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. too
too + pridevnik: preveč drag za planet. too + pridevnik = preveč (too expensive for the planet). Very ne ustreza, ker gre za čezmernost.
2. most / many / much
Količinski zaimek: most of the world's avocados. Pred »of the world's avocados« stoji količinski zaimek (most/many/much of).
3. without
leave somebody without something. leave somebody without something = pustiti koga brez česa.
4. also
Prislov med pomožnim in glavnim glagolom: has also caused. also stoji med pomožnim (has) in glavnim glagolom (caused).
5. of
take control of. take control of = prevzeti nadzor nad; predlog je vedno of.
6. their
Svojilni zaimek za avocados (množina). Svojilni zaimek se nanaša na avokade (množina): their.
7. much
as much as anyone. as much as anyone = toliko kot kdorkoli; za nešteven pomen much.
8. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za something (najpogosteje that); »I knew« je vrinjen. Oziralni zaimek za something: that ali which; vrinjeni »I knew« ne spremeni zgradbe.
9. which
Nedoločni oziralni stavek po vejici. Za vejico (nedoločni oziralni stavek) za stvar samo which.
10. that
argue that + stavek. argue that + stavek: trditi, da …
11. a / their
make a living / depend on something for their living. make a living = preživljati se; z depend on … for their living tudi their.
12. where
where their food comes from. Odvisno vprašanje o kraju: where their food comes from.
13. one
one of the simplest ways. one of the + presežnik + množina = eden izmed.
14. never / not
you can never eat / can not eat another one. Nikalnica pred eat: never ali not; smisel je »nikoli več ne moreš jesti«.
15. when
when you do. Časovni veznik when: ko to storiš.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Changing times in British boarding schools

While sending children away to school used (0) (TAKE) for granted among wealthy British families, things have changed a great deal. Fifty years ago, many pupils (1) (SEND) to boarding school at the age of seven and only saw their parents during the holidays. Today, most boarding schools (2) (OFFER) "flexi-boarding", which allows pupils to go home at weekends.

The number of full-time boarders (3) (FALL) steadily for decades. Head teachers say that parents today (4) (NOT / WANT) to miss their children's childhood, and many pupils say they would rather (5) (LIVE) at home. "When I was at school, you (6) (EXPECT) to cope on your own," says a former pupil, now in his sixties. "Nobody asked how you were feeling."

Schools (7) (FORCE) to adapt in other ways, too. Dormitories that once slept thirty boys (8) (DIVIDE) into small rooms for two or four. Mobile phones, which were banned completely until about fifteen years ago, are now allowed in the evenings. And wellbeing staff, who were unheard of a generation ago, (9) (NOW / EMPLOY) by almost every school.

Some traditions remain. Pupils still eat together in a dining hall, and many schools insist on (10) (WEAR) uniforms, even at weekends. Sport is as important as ever, and pupils at one school in Yorkshire told me they (11) (TRAIN) since six o'clock that morning when I arrived at nine.

Rising fees are another challenge. If prices (12) (CONTINUE) to rise at the current rate, many families will no longer be able to afford them. Several schools have already closed, and experts predict that by 2030 a number of others (13) (MERGE) with nearby schools.

Will boarding schools survive? Most head teachers are optimistic. "Parents (14) (ALWAYS / LOOK) for an education that gives their children independence," says one. "If we hadn't changed, we (15) (DISAPPEAR) long ago. But we have, and that is why we are still here."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. to be taken
naloge.rezultat:
1. were sent
2. offer
3. has fallen / has been falling
4. do not want / don't want
5. live
6. were expected
7. have been forced
8. have been divided
9. are now employed
10. wearing
11. had been training
12. continue
13. will have merged
14. have always looked / will always look / are always looking
15. would have disappeared
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. were sent
Trpnik v pretekliku: pupils were sent. Učence je nekdo pošiljal (niso sami šli) in to v preteklosti: trpnik were sent.
2. offer
Sedanja splošna resnica: present simple, množina. Splošno dejstvo zdaj, osebek množina (schools): offer brez -s.
3. has fallen / has been falling
for decades – present perfect (continuous). »for decades« pomeni od nekdaj do zdaj, zato present perfect (continuous).
4. do not want / don't want
Splošna resnica, nikalna oblika. Splošna resnica v sedanjiku, nikalna oblika z do not.
5. live
would rather + nedoločnik brez to. would rather + nedoločnik brez to: would rather live.
6. were expected
Trpnik v pretekliku: you were expected to cope. Od tebe so pričakovali (trpnik), preteklost: were expected.
7. have been forced
Present perfect v trpniku; vpliv na sedanjost. Present perfect v trpniku: dogodek s posledico do zdaj (have been forced).
8. have been divided
Trpnik v present perfect (stanje zdaj). Stanje, ki je nastalo in velja zdaj: have been divided.
9. are now employed
Trpnik v sedanjiku s prislovom now. now kaže na sedanjost; trpnik are employed.
10. wearing
insist on + -ing. insist on + glagolnik (-ing): wearing.
11. had been training
Past perfect continuous: trenirali so že od šestih, ko sem prišel ob devetih. Dejanje je trajalo pred drugim preteklim trenutkom (od šestih do devetih): had been training.
12. continue
Prvi pogojnik: if + present simple. Prvi pogojnik: v if-stavku present simple (continue).
13. will have merged
by 2030 – future perfect. »by 2030« = do tedaj že končano: will have merged.
14. have always looked / will always look / are always looking
Ponavljajoče se dejanje do sedanjosti: have always looked. »always« z dejanjem do zdaj: have always looked; sprejemljive so tudi druge smiselne oblike.
15. would have disappeared
Tretji pogojnik: if we hadn't changed, we would have disappeared. Tretji pogojnik: if we hadn't changed → would have disappeared (pretekla neresničnost).

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Rosie Clarke, a British comedian and actress, about her career. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Rosie, you've been making people laugh for thirty years, in Britain and in America. Where did it start?

Rosie: In a school canteen in Leeds, actually. I was terribly shy, and I discovered that if I did impressions of the teachers, people stopped noticing that I was shy. Comedy was a disguise. It still is, in a way.

Interviewer: Your first job was not in comedy, though.

Rosie: No, I trained as a dancer. I spent two years in the chorus of West End musicals, and I was quite bad. I was always one step behind everyone else. A director once told me I'd be better off making the audience laugh on purpose, since I was doing it by accident anyway.

Interviewer: And then television.

Rosie: Yes, I got a small part in a sketch show in 1995. Within two years I had my own programme, which was unusual for a woman then. In those days the writers' room was almost entirely male. I remember suggesting a sketch about a mother of four and being told that "women's stuff" wouldn't be funny. It became the most popular sketch of the series.

Interviewer: Why did you move to Los Angeles?

Rosie: Love, mostly. My husband is American, and we decided our children should grow up near both sets of grandparents – so we split our time. It was hard at first. American audiences didn't know me at all, so I had to start again in small clubs, which was terrifying but very good for me.

Interviewer: You're known for playing dozens of different characters. How do you create them?

Rosie: I listen. I sit on buses and in cafés and I eavesdrop shamelessly. Every character starts with a voice – the way someone says a single phrase. Costumes and make-up come much later.

Interviewer: Is there anything you wouldn't joke about?

Rosie: I don't make fun of people who have less power than I do. Politicians, celebrities, myself – yes, all the time. But not people who can't answer back.

A life in comedy

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Rosie Clarke has worked in two countries. (T)
  2. 1.Rosie started doing comedy to hide her shyness. T / F
  3. 2.Rosie was a talented dancer. T / F
  4. 3.A director suggested that Rosie should try comedy. T / F
  5. 4.In the 1990s, most comedy writers on television were women. T / F
  6. 5.The sketch about a mother of four was not successful. T / F
  7. 6.Rosie moved to America mainly for her career. T / F
  8. 7.In America, Rosie had to perform in small venues at first. T / F
  9. 8.Rosie's characters usually begin with a voice. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. F
6. F
7. T
8. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
»people stopped noticing that I was shy. Comedy was a disguise.« T: komedija je bila »preobleka« (disguise), ki je skrila sramežljivost.
2. F
»I was quite bad. I was always one step behind«. F: sama pravi, da je bila slaba plesalka (quite bad).
3. T
»I'd be better off making the audience laugh on purpose«. T: režiser ji je rekel, naj občinstvo spravlja v smeh namenoma – to je predlog za komedijo.
4. F
»the writers' room was almost entirely male«. F: »almost entirely male« = skoraj samo moški; trditev pravi nasprotno.
5. F
»It became the most popular sketch of the series.« F: skeč je postal najbolj priljubljen v seriji.
6. F
»Love, mostly.« F: »Love, mostly« – preselila se je zaradi ljubezni, ne kariere. Mainly v trditvi je ključna beseda.
7. T
»I had to start again in small clubs«. T: začela je znova v majhnih klubih (small venues = small clubs).
8. T
»Every character starts with a voice«. T: vsak lik se začne z glasom.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a radio programme about city pigeons and the people who study them. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: They're everywhere – on statues, railway stations and café tables – and most of us see them as pests. But pigeons have a surprisingly rich history, and scientists are discovering that they're much cleverer than we think. Our reporter, Dan Moss, has been finding out more.

Dan: Pigeons have lived alongside humans for at least five thousand years. They were probably the first birds to be domesticated, kept for their meat and for their droppings, which made an excellent fertiliser. Their most famous skill, of course, is finding their way home. In both world wars, pigeons carried messages across the battlefield, and one of them, a bird called Cher Ami, saved almost two hundred soldiers in 1918.

Dr Ellis: What fascinates me is how they navigate. We know they use the position of the sun, and they seem to be able to sense the Earth's magnetic field. But recent studies suggest they also follow human roads. Pigeons tracked with GPS often fly along motorways and even turn at roundabouts.

Dan: Dr Sarah Ellis studies pigeons at a university in Oxford. Her research has shown that the birds can recognise individual human faces.

Dr Ellis: In one experiment, two researchers fed pigeons in a park. One was friendly, the other chased the birds away. After a few days they swapped coats, but the pigeons still avoided the unfriendly one. They weren't fooled by clothes – they remembered the face.

Dan: Pigeons can also learn to tell the difference between paintings by Monet and Picasso, and they can count up to nine. So why do we dislike them so much?

Dr Ellis: Partly because there are so many of them, and partly because of their droppings, which damage buildings. But the real problem is us. City pigeons are descended from birds that escaped from farms, and they survive on the food we throw away. If we stopped feeding them, their numbers would fall naturally within a few years.

Dan: Some cities are trying a gentler solution: special pigeon lofts where the birds are encouraged to nest, and where their eggs are replaced with plastic ones. In Basel, in Switzerland, the population has been halved this way, without a single bird being killed.

The hidden lives of pigeons

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.How do most people see pigeons?
    As pests.
  2. 1.For how long have pigeons lived with humans?
  3. 2.What were pigeon droppings used for?
  4. 3.What did Cher Ami do in 1918?
  5. 4.Apart from the sun, what helps pigeons to navigate?
  6. 5.What do pigeons tracked with GPS sometimes do at roundabouts?
  7. 6.What did the two researchers exchange in the experiment?
  8. 7.How did the pigeons recognise the unfriendly researcher?
  9. 8.Up to what number can pigeons count?
  10. 9.What would happen if people stopped feeding pigeons?
  11. 10.What happens to pigeons' eggs in the special lofts?
naloge.rezultat:
1. (At least) five thousand years.
2. (As) fertiliser.
3. Saved almost two hundred soldiers.
4. The Earth's magnetic field. / Roads.
5. Turn.
6. (Their) coats.
7. By his/her face.
8. Nine.
9. Their numbers would fall.
10. They are replaced with plastic ones.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. (At least) five thousand years.
»for at least five thousand years«. »For how long« = koliko časa; odgovor je časovni podatek. »At least« (vsaj) je del podatka, a ni obvezen.
2. (As) fertiliser.
»droppings, which made an excellent fertiliser«. »Used for« = za kaj so jih uporabljali; odgovor je namen: kot gnojilo (fertiliser).
3. Saved almost two hundred soldiers.
»saved almost two hundred soldiers in 1918«. Vprašanje »What did … do« zahteva dejanje: rešil je skoraj dvesto vojakov. Številka je bistvena.
4. The Earth's magnetic field. / Roads.
Magnetno polje ali ceste – oboje je navedeno. »Apart from the sun« izključi sonce; govorec omeni dve drugi pomoči (magnetno polje, ceste) – zadošča ena.
5. Turn.
»even turn at roundabouts«. »At roundabouts« je v posnetku z besedo even (celo), kar poudari presenetljivost; dejanje je turn.
6. (Their) coats.
»they swapped coats«. »Exchange« = »swap«; zamenjala sta si plašča. Parafraza v vprašanju je pogosta past.
7. By his/her face.
»they remembered the face«. »How …recognise« = po čem; po obrazu, ne po plašču – to je bistvo poskusa.
8. Nine.
»they can count up to nine«. »Up to what number« = do katerega števila; odgovor je število nine.
9. Their numbers would fall.
»their numbers would fall naturally«. Pogojnik »What would happen if …« zahteva posledico: število golobov bi naravno upadlo.
10. They are replaced with plastic ones.
»their eggs are replaced with plastic ones«. Trpnik v vprašanju (What happens to …) → odgovor v trpniku: jajca zamenjajo s plastičnimi.

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You are a Slovenian secondary school student applying for a two-week exchange programme with a school in Norway. The programme focuses on protecting the oceans.

Write an e-mail of 120–150 words to the Norwegian programme coordinator, in which you:

  • explain why you are interested in the programme,
  • describe any experience or knowledge you have related to the environment,
  • explain how the programme will help you in your future studies.
TO: exchange@oslo-school.no
SUBJECT: Exchange application
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-sporočilo z vsemi tremi iztočnicami (zanimanje, izkušnje, korist za študij) in formalnim nagovorom ter zaključkom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. explain why you are interested in the programme
  3. describe any experience or knowledge you have related to the environment
  4. explain how the programme will help you in your future studies
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba e-sporočila
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor.
I am writing to apply for the exchange programme on ocean protection.
Namen.
I have always been fascinated by the sea, and I am worried about plastic pollution in the Adriatic.
Razlog za zanimanje z osebno noto.
Last year I organised a beach clean-up with my class and took part in a school project on microplastics.
Konkretna izkušnja.
I would like to study marine biology, so the programme would give me practical experience and international contacts.
Korist za prihodnji študij.
Thank you for considering my application. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni zaključek.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the two-week exchange programme on ocean protection at your school.

I have always been fascinated by the sea, as I spend every summer on the Slovenian coast. At the same time, I am worried about the amount of plastic I see in the Adriatic, and I would like to learn how Norway deals with this problem.

Last year I organised a beach clean-up in Piran with my class, and we collected more than two hundred kilograms of rubbish. I also took part in a school project on microplastics, in which we examined samples of sea water under a microscope.

I would like to study marine biology after my final exams. The programme would give me practical experience, as well as contacts with students and teachers from another country.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Maja Kovač

Število besed: 149 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Dangerous online challenges should be banned.
  2. Tourists should pay more to visit popular places.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt
Uvod: stališče (online challenges that put lives at risk should be removed from social media).
Jasna teza.
Argument 1: young people copy what they see; examples of injuries.
Primer.
Argument 2: platforms profit from views, so they must take responsibility.
Povezovalci.
Protiargument: bans limit free speech and are hard to enforce; zavrnitev: safety comes first.
Upoštevaj nasprotno stran.
Sklep: a combination of bans and education.
Odgovori na vprašanje.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: tourist taxes fund maintenance and reduce crowds (Venice). Against: travel becomes a privilege of the rich.
Izberi en naslov.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dangerous online challenges should be banned.

Every few months a new "challenge" spreads across social media, and young people film themselves doing something risky to impress their followers. Some of these challenges have ended in serious injuries or even death. In my opinion, dangerous online challenges should be banned, although a ban alone will not solve the problem.

Firstly, children and young teenagers often cannot judge risk properly. When they see hundreds of videos of other people holding their breath or jumping from moving cars, the activity seems normal and safe. A ban would remove these videos before they reach millions of viewers.

Secondly, platforms earn money from every view, so they have little reason to act on their own. If the law required them to delete dangerous content quickly, they would have to invest in better moderation. A similar rule already exists for violent and illegal content.

Critics argue that a ban limits freedom of speech and that it is impossible to control everything posted online. This is partly true. However, freedom of speech has never included the right to encourage others to harm themselves.

All things considered, I believe that dangerous challenges should be banned. At the same time, schools and parents should talk to young people about online pressure, because the best protection is a teenager who can say no.
