naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and complete the sentences below. Use 1–5 words in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Sentence 0.

The Telegram

Knowing that Mrs Hale had a weak heart, the family took great care to tell her the news as gently as possible. It was her sister Clara who did it, in broken sentences and half-finished hints, while Mr Hale's old friend Robert waited in the hall. He had been at the newspaper office when the telegram arrived, listing the names of those lost in the railway accident, and Brently Hale's name had been at the top.

Mrs Hale did not react as other women might have done, unable to accept the truth. She wept at once, suddenly and wildly, in her sister's arms. When the first storm of grief was over, she went to her room alone. She would have no one follow her.

There, facing the open window, stood a comfortable armchair. She sank into it, exhausted. Outside, the tops of the trees were trembling with new spring life. The smell of rain was in the air. In the street below a man was selling vegetables, and somewhere a voice was singing. Sparrows were arguing on the roof.

She sat quite still, except when a sob came up into her throat and shook her, like a child who has cried itself to sleep and continues to sob in its dreams. She was young, with a calm face whose lines showed a certain strength.

Something was coming to her, and she was waiting for it, fearfully. What was it? She did not know; it was too subtle to name. But she felt it creeping out of the sky, through the sounds and the colours that filled the air.

When she let it come, a little whispered word escaped from her lips. She said it over and over: "Free, free, free!" The empty stare and the look of terror went from her eyes. Her pulse beat fast, and her blood warmed every part of her body.

She knew that she would weep again when she saw his kind hands folded in death. But beyond that bitter moment she saw a long procession of years that would belong to her absolutely. There would be no one to live for during those coming years; she would live for herself.

Clara was kneeling at the closed door, begging her to come out. "You will make yourself ill," she said. But Mrs Hale was drinking in the very air of life through that open window.

At last she rose and opened the door. There was a feverish triumph in her eyes, and she carried herself unconsciously like a goddess of victory. Someone was opening the front door with a key. It was Brently Hale who entered, a little dusty, carrying his bag and umbrella. He had been far from the scene of the accident and did not even know there had been one.

When the doctors came, they said she had died of heart disease – of joy that kills.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com, po motivih kratke zgodbe Kate Chopin)

  1. 0.Mrs Hale suffered from ___.
    a weak heart
  2. 1.The person who broke the news to Mrs Hale was ___.
  3. 2.Robert had learned about the accident at ___.
  4. 3.Unlike many women, Mrs Hale reacted to the news by ___.
  5. 4.After crying, Mrs Hale wanted to be ___.
  6. 5.Through the window she noticed signs of ___.
  7. 6.Her occasional sobbing is compared to that of ___.
  8. 7.The feeling that came to her was too subtle ___.
  9. 8.The word she kept repeating was ___.
  10. 9.She looked forward to years in which she would live ___.
  11. 10.Mr Hale had not been in the accident because ___.
  12. 11.The doctors believed that Mrs Hale had died of ___.
naloge.rezultat:
1. her sister (Clara)
2. the newspaper office
3. weeping at once
4. alone (in her room)
5. (new) spring life / spring
6. a child (crying in its sleep)
7. to name
8. free
9. for herself
10. he had been far from the scene
11. joy (that kills) / heart disease
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami tako, da je slovnično pravilna in pomensko skladna z besedilom.
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved z vrzeljo in ugotovi, kakšna beseda manjka (samostalnik, glagol v določeni obliki, števnik). Nato v besedilu poišči podatek.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede mesto v besedilu. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna (pazi na ednino/množino in čas).
  • Pasti: podatek je pravi, a slovnično ne sede v poved; prepišeš preveč besed.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. her sister (Clara)
»It was her sister Clara who did it«. Za »was« manjka oseba; poved »It was her sister Clara who did it« poudari, kdo je povedal novico.
2. the newspaper office
»He had been at the newspaper office when the telegram arrived«. »at« + kraj: the newspaper office; tam je bil, ko je prišel telegram.
3. weeping at once
»She wept at once, suddenly and wildly«. »by« + glagolnik (-ing): weeping at once. »Unlike many women« pomeni, da ni otrpnila, ampak je takoj zajokala.
4. alone (in her room)
»she went to her room alone. She would have no one follow her«. »wanted to be« + pridevnik: alone. Nikomur ni dovolila, da bi ji sledil.
5. (new) spring life / spring
»trembling with new spring life«. »signs of« + samostalnik: nove pomladne življenjskosti.
6. a child (crying in its sleep)
»like a child who has cried itself to sleep«. »that of« + samostalnik: kot otrok, ki se je zjokal v spanec.
7. to name
»it was too subtle to name«. »too subtle« + to + nedoločnik: too subtle to name = preveč neulovljivo, da bi ga poimenovala.
8. free
»Free, free, free!« Ponavlja besedo free; bistvo zgodbe je občutek svobode.
9. for herself
»she would live for herself«. »live« + for herself: živela bo zase, ne za drugega.
10. he had been far from the scene
»He had been far from the scene of the accident«. Za because sledi stavek: bil je daleč od kraja nesreče.
11. joy (that kills) / heart disease
Ironija: zdravniki mislijo, da je umrla od veselja. Ironija: zdravniki mislijo, da je umrla od veselja; bralec ve, da od šoka, ker se je svoboda izgubila.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (D).

A billion users can't all be wrong

Many people still think of TikTok as an app for dance videos. [0] For millions of young people, it has become a place to learn, to find a community and, increasingly, to get the news.

When politicians discuss the platform, they usually focus on two issues: data security and the effect of short videos on attention spans. [1] What they rarely discuss is why so many people use the app in the first place.

The answer, according to researchers, is the algorithm. Unlike older social networks, TikTok does not depend mainly on who you follow. [2] As a result, an unknown creator can reach millions of viewers with a single video.

This has changed who gets heard. [3] A nurse explaining a medical procedure, a farmer showing how cheese is made, a teenager talking about living with a disability – all of them can find an audience without the help of a television channel or a publisher.

Of course, the same system can spread false information just as quickly. [4] Fact-checkers say they cannot keep up with the speed at which misleading videos go viral.

Young users are not as naïve as adults often assume, however. [5] Many say they check information they see on TikTok against other sources, and that they treat the app as a starting point rather than an authority.

There is also a question of fairness. [6] If the platform were banned, they argue, millions of small businesses that sell products through the app would lose an important source of income.

Supporters of tighter regulation reply that this is precisely why rules are needed. [7] They call for more transparency about how the algorithm works and stronger protection for children.

Perhaps the real lesson is that politicians need to understand the platforms they want to control. [8] Until they do, they risk making decisions that a billion users will simply ignore. [9]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. ABoth are serious concerns that deserve attention.
  2. BInstead, it shows each user videos it predicts they will enjoy, from anyone at all.
  3. CSurveys suggest that they are often more sceptical than their parents.
  4. DThat impression is now several years out of date.
  5. EVoices that were once ignored by traditional media are now among the most popular.
  6. FA video with a shocking claim can be watched ten million times before anyone corrects it.
  7. GMany creators point out that TikTok is not only entertainment but also work.
  8. HWhen a company has that much influence, it cannot be left to regulate itself.
  9. IThat means spending time on them, not just talking about them.
  10. JAnd a billion users, as the title of this article suggests, are hard to ignore in return.
  11. KThe company was founded in China in 2016.
  12. LMost users spend less than ten minutes a day on the app.
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. B
3. E
4. F
5. C
6. G
7. H
8. I
9. J
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
Both se nanaša na dve vprašanji (varnost podatkov in pozornost). Both se nanaša na dve skrbi iz prejšnje povedi; poved jih povzame kot resni.
2. B
Instead – algoritem ne temelji na sledenju, ampak predvideva, kaj ti bo všeč. Instead uvede nasprotje: algoritem ne sledi prijateljem, ampak napove, kaj bo všeč.
3. E
Kdo je slišan: glasovi, ki jih tradicionalni mediji niso opazili; sledijo primeri. Poved odgovori na vprašanje, kdo je slišan; za njo sledijo primeri takih glasov.
4. F
Lažne informacije se širijo hitro – primer z deset milijoni ogledov. Primer z deset milijoni ogledov ponazori hitro širjenje lažnih trditev.
5. C
Mladi so bolj skeptični, kot mislijo odrasli; naslednja poved to podkrepi. »they« = mladi; anketa pokaže, da so bolj skeptični od staršev, kar podpre naslednja poved.
6. G
Vprašanje pravičnosti: TikTok je tudi delo; nato argument o malih podjetjih. Poved odpre temo pravičnosti: TikTok je za ustvarjalce delo, ne le zabava.
7. H
Zagovorniki pravil: tako vpliven podjetje se ne more samo nadzorovati. »that much influence« se navezuje na prej opisano moč podjetja; posledica: potrebna so pravila.
8. I
That means … – razumeti platforme pomeni preživeti čas na njih. »That means« pojasni prejšnjo misel o razumevanju platform.
9. J
Zaključna poved se vrne k naslovu (a billion users). Zadnja poved se vrne k naslovu (billion users) in zaokroži članek.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The dark story behind Bambi

Most people know Bambi as the cute little deer from the 1942 Disney film. Far fewer know that the story was originally a novel written for adults, and (0) it was banned by the Nazis.

Its author, Felix Salten, was a journalist in Vienna. He published Bambi: A Life in the Woods in 1923, and it quickly became a success across Europe. Unlike the film, the book is a serious, often violent story (1) shows how hard life is for animals in the forest. Deer are hunted, friends die, and the young Bambi learns that he must survive alone.

Many readers saw the novel as a political allegory. Salten was Jewish, and the hunted deer were interpreted as a symbol of Jewish people (2) faced persecution in Europe. For this reason, the book was banned in Nazi Germany in 1936, and Salten was forced to leave Austria two years (3). He spent the rest of his life in Switzerland, where he died in 1945.

By then, Walt Disney (4) bought the film rights – reportedly for just 1,000 dollars. Disney's team spent several years working on the film. They brought real deer into the studio (5) the artists could study how they moved, and they even visited forests in Maine to photograph the light.

The finished film was much gentler than the book, (6) it still contained one of the most famous scenes in cinema history: the death of Bambi's mother. Generations of children have been shocked by it, and (7) adults admit that they still cannot watch it without crying.

Salten earned almost nothing from the film's enormous success. He had sold the rights to an American director, (8) then sold them to Disney, and the money he received was small. Today his name is barely remembered, (9) the deer he created is known all over the world.

In recent years, a new English translation of the novel (10) appeared, restoring the darkness of the original. Its translator argues that Salten's message is more relevant (11) ever. "This is a book about how fear changes us," she says. "It asks (12) we can stay kind in a world full of danger."

Perhaps (13) is why the story still matters. Behind the cartoon, there is a warning about what happens when one group is hunted by (14). It is a warning that Salten learned from (15) own experience.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. that
naloge.rezultat:
1. that / which
2. who
3. later
4. had
5. so
6. but / although / though
7. many / some
8. who
9. but / while / although / though / yet
10. has
11. than
12. whether / if / how
13. that / this
14. another / others
15. his
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za story. Oziralni zaimek za story (stvar): that ali which.
2. who
Oziralni zaimek za osebe: people who faced persecution. Za people (osebe) who.
3. later
two years later. »two years later« = dve leti pozneje.
4. had
Predpreteklik: do takrat je že kupil pravice. Pravice je kupil že prej kot drugi pretekli dogodek: had bought (past perfect).
5. so
so (that) the artists could study. so (that) izraža namen: da bi umetniki lahko študirali živali.
6. but / although / though
Nasprotje: nežnejši, a vseeno … Nasprotje dveh lastnosti: nežnejši, a vseeno …
7. many / some
Količinski zaimek: many adults admit. Količinski zaimek za ljudi (adults): many/some.
8. who
Nedoločni oziralni stavek za osebo (director). Za vejico in osebo (director) who.
9. but / while / although / though / yet
Nasprotje: ime je pozabljeno, srnjak pa poznan. Nasprotje: ime avtorja je pozabljeno, srnjak pa ne.
10. has
Present perfect: has appeared. Present perfect (dejanje do zdaj): has appeared; osebek ednina.
11. than
more relevant than ever. more … than ever = bolj kot kdajkoli.
12. whether / if / how
Odvisno vprašanje: asks whether we can stay kind. Odvisno vprašanje: asks whether/if (ali).
13. that / this
Perhaps that is why. Kazalni zaimek za prejšnjo misel: that/this is why.
14. another / others
hunted by another (group). another (en drug) ali others (drugi) – lovijo jih drugi.
15. his
Svojilni zaimek: his own experience. Svojilni zaimek za avtorja (moški): his own.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Is New Zealand really a safe place to escape the apocalypse?

New Zealand has become the favourite destination for the world's (0) (WEALTH) elite. Over the past decade, several billionaires have bought large properties there, some of them with underground bunkers. Their reasoning is simple: in the event of a global (1) (CATASTROPHIC), a remote island nation might be the safest place on Earth.

Researchers have even published studies supporting this idea. One paper ranked New Zealand first among the countries most likely to survive a (2) (BREAK) of global trade, thanks to its ability to produce food and its (3) (ISOLATE) from conflict zones.

But many New Zealanders are (4) (COMFORT) with their country's new reputation. Critics say the arrival of rich foreigners has pushed up property prices and made housing (5) (AFFORD) for local families. Others point out the (6) (ODD) of the whole idea: if civilisation collapses, a bunker full of tinned food will not protect anyone for long.

There is also the question of (7) (DEPEND). New Zealand imports nearly all of its fuel, medicines and electronic equipment. Without them, modern life would quickly become (8) (SUSTAIN). The country also faces natural risks of its own, including earthquakes and volcanic (9) (ERUPT).

Some locals have responded with humour. A popular website offers "survival tips for billionaires", including "learn the names of your neighbours" – a reminder that in a real crisis, communities matter far more than private (10) (PROTECT).

The government, meanwhile, has introduced new rules. Since 2018, most foreign buyers have been (11) (ABLE) to purchase existing homes, although exceptions are made for large (12) (INVEST).

Perhaps the real lesson is about our (13) (FASCINATE) with escape. Instead of planning how to survive the end of the world, argue the critics, the super-rich would do better to use their wealth to make it less (14) (LIKE). As one columnist put it: "There is no safe haven from a disaster you helped to create." It is an (15) (COMFORT) thought, but a necessary one.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. wealthiest
naloge.rezultat:
1. catastrophe
2. breakdown
3. isolation
4. uncomfortable
5. unaffordable
6. oddity / oddness
7. dependence / dependency
8. unsustainable
9. eruptions
10. protection
11. unable
12. investments / investors
13. fascination
14. likely
15. uncomfortable
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. catastrophe
a global + samostalnik: catastrophic → catastrophe. »a global« zahteva samostalnik: catastrophe (pridevnik catastrophic je dan).
2. breakdown
a + samostalnik: break → breakdown (sestavljenka). Za a sledi samostalnik: breakdown (zlom, razpad).
3. isolation
its + samostalnik: isolate → isolation. Za its samostalnik: isolation.
4. uncomfortable
Nezadovoljstvo z ugledom: un- + comfortable. Pridevnik z nikalnim pomenom (ljudem je neprijetno): un- + comfortable.
5. unaffordable
make + pridevnik z nikalnim pomenom: un- + afford + -able. make + pridevnik: unaffordable (nedosegljivo po ceni).
6. oddity / oddness
the + samostalnik: odd → oddity. Za the samostalnik: oddity/oddness (nenavadnost).
7. dependence / dependency
the question of + samostalnik. »the question of« + samostalnik: dependence/dependency.
8. unsustainable
become + pridevnik (nevzdržno): un- + sustain + -able. become + pridevnik: unsustainable (nevzdržen).
9. eruptions
volcanic + samostalnik v množini. volcanic + samostalnik v množini (več izbruhov): eruptions.
10. protection
private + samostalnik: protect → protection. private + samostalnik: protection.
11. unable
have been unable to purchase. have been + pridevnik + to: unable to purchase.
12. investments / investors
large + samostalnik v množini: investments ali investors. large + samostalnik v množini: investments ali investors (oboje smiselno).
13. fascination
our + samostalnik + with. our + samostalnik, ki se veže z with: fascination with.
14. likely
make it less + pridevnik. make it less + pridevnik: likely.
15. uncomfortable
an + pridevnik z nikalnim pomenom (but a necessary one). an + pridevnik pred samostalnikom; an zahteva samoglasnik: uncomfortable.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Rosie Clarke, a British comedian and actress, about her career. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Rosie, you've been making people laugh for thirty years, in Britain and in America. Where did it start?

Rosie: In a school canteen in Leeds, actually. I was terribly shy, and I discovered that if I did impressions of the teachers, people stopped noticing that I was shy. Comedy was a disguise. It still is, in a way.

Interviewer: Your first job was not in comedy, though.

Rosie: No, I trained as a dancer. I spent two years in the chorus of West End musicals, and I was quite bad. I was always one step behind everyone else. A director once told me I'd be better off making the audience laugh on purpose, since I was doing it by accident anyway.

Interviewer: And then television.

Rosie: Yes, I got a small part in a sketch show in 1995. Within two years I had my own programme, which was unusual for a woman then. In those days the writers' room was almost entirely male. I remember suggesting a sketch about a mother of four and being told that "women's stuff" wouldn't be funny. It became the most popular sketch of the series.

Interviewer: Why did you move to Los Angeles?

Rosie: Love, mostly. My husband is American, and we decided our children should grow up near both sets of grandparents – so we split our time. It was hard at first. American audiences didn't know me at all, so I had to start again in small clubs, which was terrifying but very good for me.

Interviewer: You're known for playing dozens of different characters. How do you create them?

Rosie: I listen. I sit on buses and in cafés and I eavesdrop shamelessly. Every character starts with a voice – the way someone says a single phrase. Costumes and make-up come much later.

Interviewer: Is there anything you wouldn't joke about?

Rosie: I don't make fun of people who have less power than I do. Politicians, celebrities, myself – yes, all the time. But not people who can't answer back.

A life in comedy

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

  1. 0.Rosie Clarke has been a comedian for ___.
    thirty years
  2. 1.Rosie first discovered comedy in a school canteen in ___.
  3. 2.At school, she did impressions of ___.
  4. 3.Before comedy, Rosie trained as a ___.
  5. 4.Rosie got her first television role in a ___ in 1995.
  6. 5.Rosie was told that sketches about ___ would not be funny.
  7. 6.Rosie and her husband wanted their children to live near ___.
  8. 7.To create characters, Rosie listens to people on buses and ___.
  9. 8.Rosie does not make jokes about people with ___.
naloge.rezultat:
1. Leeds
2. the teachers
3. dancer
4. sketch show
5. women's stuff / women
6. both sets of grandparents
7. in cafés
8. less power (than her)
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. Leeds
»In a school canteen in Leeds«. Za »in« manjka kraj: Leeds.
2. the teachers
»if I did impressions of the teachers«. »impressions of« + oseba: the teachers.
3. dancer
»I trained as a dancer«. »trained as a« + poklic: dancer.
4. sketch show
»a small part in a sketch show in 1995«. »a« + samostalnik: sketch show.
5. women's stuff / women
»'women's stuff' wouldn't be funny«. »sketches about« + tema: »women's stuff«.
6. both sets of grandparents
»near both sets of grandparents«. »near« + oseba ali kraj: both sets of grandparents.
7. in cafés
»I sit on buses and in cafés«. Vzporedno z »on buses and« manjka drug kraj: in cafés.
8. less power (than her)
»people who have less power than I do«. »people with« + samostalnik: less power.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to a radio programme about city pigeons and the people who study them. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: They're everywhere – on statues, railway stations and café tables – and most of us see them as pests. But pigeons have a surprisingly rich history, and scientists are discovering that they're much cleverer than we think. Our reporter, Dan Moss, has been finding out more.

Dan: Pigeons have lived alongside humans for at least five thousand years. They were probably the first birds to be domesticated, kept for their meat and for their droppings, which made an excellent fertiliser. Their most famous skill, of course, is finding their way home. In both world wars, pigeons carried messages across the battlefield, and one of them, a bird called Cher Ami, saved almost two hundred soldiers in 1918.

Dr Ellis: What fascinates me is how they navigate. We know they use the position of the sun, and they seem to be able to sense the Earth's magnetic field. But recent studies suggest they also follow human roads. Pigeons tracked with GPS often fly along motorways and even turn at roundabouts.

Dan: Dr Sarah Ellis studies pigeons at a university in Oxford. Her research has shown that the birds can recognise individual human faces.

Dr Ellis: In one experiment, two researchers fed pigeons in a park. One was friendly, the other chased the birds away. After a few days they swapped coats, but the pigeons still avoided the unfriendly one. They weren't fooled by clothes – they remembered the face.

Dan: Pigeons can also learn to tell the difference between paintings by Monet and Picasso, and they can count up to nine. So why do we dislike them so much?

Dr Ellis: Partly because there are so many of them, and partly because of their droppings, which damage buildings. But the real problem is us. City pigeons are descended from birds that escaped from farms, and they survive on the food we throw away. If we stopped feeding them, their numbers would fall naturally within a few years.

Dan: Some cities are trying a gentler solution: special pigeon lofts where the birds are encouraged to nest, and where their eggs are replaced with plastic ones. In Basel, in Switzerland, the population has been halved this way, without a single bird being killed.

The hidden lives of pigeons

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.How do most people see pigeons?
    As pests.
  2. 1.For how long have pigeons lived with humans?
  3. 2.What were pigeon droppings used for?
  4. 3.What did Cher Ami do in 1918?
  5. 4.Apart from the sun, what helps pigeons to navigate?
  6. 5.What do pigeons tracked with GPS sometimes do at roundabouts?
  7. 6.What did the two researchers exchange in the experiment?
  8. 7.How did the pigeons recognise the unfriendly researcher?
  9. 8.Up to what number can pigeons count?
  10. 9.What would happen if people stopped feeding pigeons?
  11. 10.What happens to pigeons' eggs in the special lofts?
naloge.rezultat:
1. (At least) five thousand years.
2. (As) fertiliser.
3. Saved almost two hundred soldiers.
4. The Earth's magnetic field. / Roads.
5. Turn.
6. (Their) coats.
7. By his/her face.
8. Nine.
9. Their numbers would fall.
10. They are replaced with plastic ones.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. (At least) five thousand years.
»for at least five thousand years«. »For how long« = koliko časa; odgovor je časovni podatek. »At least« (vsaj) je del podatka, a ni obvezen.
2. (As) fertiliser.
»droppings, which made an excellent fertiliser«. »Used for« = za kaj so jih uporabljali; odgovor je namen: kot gnojilo (fertiliser).
3. Saved almost two hundred soldiers.
»saved almost two hundred soldiers in 1918«. Vprašanje »What did … do« zahteva dejanje: rešil je skoraj dvesto vojakov. Številka je bistvena.
4. The Earth's magnetic field. / Roads.
Magnetno polje ali ceste – oboje je navedeno. »Apart from the sun« izključi sonce; govorec omeni dve drugi pomoči (magnetno polje, ceste) – zadošča ena.
5. Turn.
»even turn at roundabouts«. »At roundabouts« je v posnetku z besedo even (celo), kar poudari presenetljivost; dejanje je turn.
6. (Their) coats.
»they swapped coats«. »Exchange« = »swap«; zamenjala sta si plašča. Parafraza v vprašanju je pogosta past.
7. By his/her face.
»they remembered the face«. »How …recognise« = po čem; po obrazu, ne po plašču – to je bistvo poskusa.
8. Nine.
»they can count up to nine«. »Up to what number« = do katerega števila; odgovor je število nine.
9. Their numbers would fall.
»their numbers would fall naturally«. Pogojnik »What would happen if …« zahteva posledico: število golobov bi naravno upadlo.
10. They are replaced with plastic ones.
»their eggs are replaced with plastic ones«. Trpnik v vprašanju (What happens to …) → odgovor v trpniku: jajca zamenjajo s plastičnimi.

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

A European youth magazine is looking for young writers from Central Europe to write a monthly column about the lives of teenagers in their countries. You have decided to apply to the editorial board.

Write an e-mail of application of 150–180 words, in which you:

  • explain why you would like to write about young people's lives,
  • describe your experience in writing or journalism,
  • outline two topics you would like to write about and explain why.
TO: editors@youngeurope.eu
SUBJECT: Columnist application
Dear Members of the Editorial Board,
naloge.rezultat: Formalna prošnja z vsemi tremi iztočnicami: motivacija, izkušnje (konkretno) in dve temi z utemeljitvijo; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain why you would like to write about young people's lives
  3. describe your experience in writing or journalism
  4. outline two topics you would like to write about and explain why
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba prošnje
Dear Members of the Editorial Board,
Formalni nagovor skupini naslovnikov.
I am writing to apply for the position of columnist advertised in your latest issue.
Namen.
I believe that teenagers are often described by adults but rarely given the chance to describe themselves.
Motivacija – izvirna misel prinese točke za vsebino.
For two years I have edited our school newspaper and published an article in a national youth magazine.
Izkušnje z dokazi.
I would like to write about the housing crisis, which forces young people to live with their parents until their thirties, and about mental health, since many of my peers struggle with anxiety.
Dve temi in utemeljitev za vsako.
I would be delighted to send you samples of my work. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Zaključek s ponudbo.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Members of the Editorial Board,

I am writing to apply for the position of monthly columnist advertised in your latest issue.

I believe that teenagers are often described by adults but rarely given the chance to describe themselves. As a seventeen-year-old from Slovenia, I would like to show your readers what our lives are really like, beyond the usual headlines about smartphones.

For the past two years I have been the editor of our school newspaper, which is published four times a year. Last spring one of my articles, about students who work part-time to support their families, was published in a national youth magazine.

I would like to write about two topics in particular. The first is the housing crisis, which forces many young people to live with their parents until their thirties. The second is mental health, since a growing number of my peers struggle with anxiety but are afraid to ask for help.

Please find attached two samples of my writing. I would be happy to provide any further information.

Yours sincerely,
Luka Zupan

  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).

Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba

  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).

Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – the most disturbing aspect of the novel is not the cruelty of the system but how calmly the characters accept it.
Teza že v uvodu.
Jedro 1 – education at Hailsham: the students are 'told and not told'; Miss Lucy's warning is ignored.
Pokaži, kako vzgoja oblikuje sprejemanje.
Jedro 2 – the rumour of deferrals: Kathy and Tommy hope for more time, not for escape; they never think of running away.
Ključno: tudi upanje ostane znotraj pravil sistema.
Jedro 3 – Tommy's anger in the field vs. Kathy's quiet acceptance at the end in Norfolk.
Primerjava dveh odzivov.
Sklep: Ishiguro makes readers ask what they accept in their own lives without question.
Širši pomen v sklepu.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Acceptance in Never Let Me Go

The most disturbing aspect of Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go is not the cruelty of the system that creates clones for organ donation, but the calmness with which the clones accept their fate. Kathy, Ruth and Tommy never try to run away; instead, they spend their short lives hoping for small favours.

This acceptance is the result of their education at Hailsham. The students are, as Miss Lucy says, "told and not told": they learn about donations so early and so gradually that the knowledge never shocks them. When Miss Lucy finally tells them the truth plainly, she is dismissed, and the children treat her warning as an embarrassing outburst rather than a call to resist.

As adults, the characters still look for exceptions within the system rather than ways out of it. Ruth dreams of working in an office, and Kathy and Tommy believe the rumour that couples in love can get a deferral. When they finally visit Madame and Miss Emily, they learn that deferrals never existed. Tommy's scream in the dark field is the only moment of open rage, and even that ends quietly.

Kathy's narrative voice reflects the same acceptance. She describes her work as a carer with pride and speaks about "completing" instead of dying. This calm, polite tone makes the reader feel the horror that she herself does not express.

In the end, Ishiguro suggests that the clones are not so different from us. Most people also accept limits they did not choose and find meaning in friendship, memory and small pleasures. The novel's quiet acceptance is therefore both deeply sad and uncomfortably human.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Pre-Party

As soon as the date for the school leavers' ball was announced, Martin's father, Greg, decided to host the "pre-party". He was not asked. He simply announced it at dinner, with the confidence of a man who had already ordered the balloons.

"Your mum and I will do canapés," he said. "Champagne for the parents, something fizzy and non-alcoholic for you lot. Photos in the garden. The roses will be out by then."

Martin, who was seventeen and had been hoping to arrive at the ball quietly with his two best friends, put down his fork. "Nobody does pre-parties any more, Dad."

"Everybody does pre-parties," said Greg. "Ask Sophie's mother."

It turned out that Sophie's mother had been planning her own pre-party for months, and that she regarded Greg's announcement as a declaration of war. Within a week, the school's parent group had divided into two camps. Messages flew. Some families accepted both invitations and spent anxious evenings working out how to be at two houses at the same time. Others accepted neither and said they would "see how things go", which everyone understood to mean that they were waiting to see which party had the better food.

Martin's mother, Helen, tried to stay out of it. She had been through the same thing when Martin's older sister left school, and she knew that the excitement of parents was always greater than the excitement of their children. But even she could not resist redesigning the garden. She bought new lights for the apple tree and spent a weekend painting the fence a colour called "Seaside Mist".

The night before the ball, it began to rain. It rained all night and all morning, and by lunchtime the garden was a small lake. The roses had been flattened. Greg stood at the kitchen window for an hour without speaking.

At four o'clock, the phone rang. It was Sophie's mother. Her marquee had collapsed in the wind, and she wondered – rather stiffly – whether the two parties might be combined, indoors, at Greg's house, which was bigger.

That evening, forty teenagers and sixty parents squeezed into the living room, the hall and the kitchen. Someone's grandmother played the piano. The photographs, taken on the stairs, were the best anybody could remember. And Martin, to his own surprise, did not want to leave.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.Who decided to host the pre-party?
    Martin's father (Greg).
  2. 1.How did Greg let the family know about the pre-party?
  3. 2.Where were the photographs going to be taken?
  4. 3.How had Martin wanted to arrive at the ball?
  5. 4.How did Sophie's mother see Greg's plan?
  6. 5.What problem did families who accepted both invitations have?
  7. 6.What were the families who accepted neither invitation really waiting for?
  8. 7.What had Helen learned when her daughter left school?
  9. 8.What happened to the garden before the ball?
  10. 9.Why did Sophie's mother call?
  11. 10.Where were the best photographs taken?
naloge.rezultat:
1. He announced it at dinner.
2. In the garden.
3. Quietly, with his two best friends.
4. As a declaration of war.
5. How to be at two houses at once.
6. To see which party had better food.
7. Parents are more excited than their children.
8. It flooded. / It became a lake.
9. To combine the two parties. / Her marquee had collapsed.
10. On the stairs.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. He announced it at dinner.
»He simply announced it at dinner«. »How did … let the family know« = kako je povedal; preprosto je napovedal pri večerji.
2. In the garden.
»Photos in the garden.« »Where« = kraj fotografiranja; na vrtu.
3. Quietly, with his two best friends.
»hoping to arrive at the ball quietly with his two best friends«. Martin je želel priti mirno, s prijateljema; navedeš oba dela.
4. As a declaration of war.
»regarded Greg's announcement as a declaration of war«. »How did … see« = kako je razumela; kot napoved vojne (metafora).
5. How to be at two houses at once.
»working out how to be at two houses at the same time«. Težava družin z dvema povabiloma: kako biti v dveh hišah hkrati.
6. To see which party had better food.
»waiting to see which party had the better food«. »Really waiting for« = kaj so v resnici čakali; kje bo boljša hrana (ironija).
7. Parents are more excited than their children.
»the excitement of parents was always greater than the excitement of their children«. Helen je spoznala, da so starši bolj vznemirjeni kot otroci.
8. It flooded. / It became a lake.
»the garden was a small lake«. »What happened« = dogodek; vrt je poplavilo, postal je majhno jezero.
9. To combine the two parties. / Her marquee had collapsed.
Šotor se je podrl, zato predlaga skupno zabavo. »Why … call« = razlog: zaradi podrtega šotora predlaga skupno zabavo.
10. On the stairs.
»The photographs, taken on the stairs«. »Where« = kraj; na stopnicah – ironija, saj so vrt načrtovali.

Five children's authors who weren't afraid of the dark

Fairy tales were never meant to be comfortable. These five writers knew that children can handle more than adults think.

A Hans Christian Andersen

The Danish writer's stories are full of suffering: a little mermaid who feels as if she is walking on knives, a match girl who freezes to death on New Year's Eve. Andersen grew up in poverty, and he never forgot it. Although he became famous across Europe and was received by kings, he remained convinced all his life that he was an outsider, and many of his heroes share that feeling.

B The Brothers Grimm

Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm did not invent their stories – they collected them from storytellers, many of them women from middle-class families. The first edition of their collection, published in 1812, was criticised for being too violent and not suitable for children, so later editions were rewritten. Ironically, the brothers removed some of the sexual content but added even more violence.

C Roald Dahl

Dahl's books are packed with cruel adults who get what they deserve. He worked as a fighter pilot in the Second World War and suffered serious head injuries in a crash, an experience that some biographers believe influenced his dark sense of humour. In 2023 his publisher changed hundreds of words in his books, a decision that caused a huge public argument and led to the original versions being republished.

D Neil Gaiman

Gaiman's novel Coraline tells the story of a girl who discovers a door to another world, where a woman with buttons for eyes wants to keep her forever. Many adults found the book terrifying, but Gaiman noticed that children usually read it as an adventure. He wrote it, he says, for his own daughter, who complained that there were not enough scary stories for girls.

E Lemony Snicket

Behind the pen name Lemony Snicket is the American writer Daniel Handler. His thirteen-book series about three orphans warns readers on the very first page that the story will not have a happy ending. Handler has said that he was inspired by the frustration he felt as a child with books in which everything turned out fine. The series has been adapted for film and television.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Whose stories include a character who dies of cold? (A)
  2. 1.Which writer felt like an outsider despite his success?
  3. 2.Whose work was changed after critics complained?
  4. 3.Whose books were edited by a publisher in recent years?
  5. 4.Which writer wrote for a member of his family?
  6. 5.Who writes under a different name?
  7. 6.Which writers did not create their stories themselves?
  8. 7.Whose experience of war may have shaped his writing?
  9. 8.Which author tells readers immediately that the story will end badly?
  10. 9.Who noticed that young and adult readers reacted differently?
  11. 10.Whose childhood circumstances are reflected in his characters?
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. B
3. C
4. D
5. E
6. B
7. C
8. E
9. D
10. A
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
»remained convinced all his life that he was an outsider«. »outsider« = odrinjen; vse življenje se je počutil tako.
2. B
Prva izdaja preveč nasilna, poznejše izdaje so prepisali. »changed after critics complained« = predelane izdaje po kritikah.
3. C
Leta 2023 je založnik spremenil več sto besed. »edited in recent years« = leta 2023 so spremenili besede.
4. D
Coraline je napisal za hčer. »for a member of his family« = za hčer.
5. E
Lemony Snicket je psevdonim Daniela Handlerja. »different name« = psevdonim.
6. B
Zgodbe sta zbrala pri pripovedovalcih. »did not create their stories themselves« = zgodbe so zbrali od pripovedovalcev.
7. C
Vojaški pilot, poškodba glave v nesreči. »experience of war« = vojaški pilot, poškodba v nesreči.
8. E
»warns readers on the very first page«. »immediately« = že na prvi strani opozori na slab konec.
9. D
Odrasli so se bali, otroci so knjigo brali kot pustolovščino. »reacted differently« = odrasli so se bali, otroci so brali kot pustolovščino.
10. A
Revščina v otroštvu; junaki delijo občutek odrinjenosti. »childhood circumstances« = revščina v otroštvu, ki jo delijo junaki.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. although / while / whereas / though
Nasprotje: v skledi sama, v naravi v skupinah. Nasprotje med dvema situacijama: although/while/whereas.
2. which
Nedoločni oziralni stavek po vejici za rabbits (živali). Za vejico za živali which.
3. been
Trpnik v present perfect: have been bred. Present perfect trpnik: have been bred.
4. from
suffer from. suffer from = trpeti zaradi.
5. for
call for something to be done. call for = zahtevati.
6. for
for the first time. for the first time = prvič.
7. after
look after = skrbeti za. look after = skrbeti za.
8. that
agree that + stavek. agree that + stavek.
9. whether / if
Odvisno vprašanje: whether we should keep pets. Odvisno vprašanje da/ne: whether/if.
10. Every / Each / An / Any
Določilo pred owner (ednina). Določilo pred števnim samostalnikom v ednini: every/each/an/any.
11. to
be suited to. be suited to = biti primeren za.
12. no
no exotic animals … at all. no + samostalnik … at all = sploh nobenih.
13. that
agree that + stavek. agree that + stavek.
14. no
no longer = ne več. no longer = ne več.
15. their
of their own. of their own = lasten.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

A brief history of Boxing Day

It is a day we now associate with sales, sport and the (0) (ENJOY) of Christmas leftovers. But what is Boxing Day, and where does its unusual name come from?

Boxing Day, celebrated on 26 December, is a public holiday in Britain and several other countries. Despite what some people believe, it has nothing to do with the (1) (SPORT) activity of boxing. The name probably comes from the "Christmas boxes" that wealthy families gave to their servants and to local (2) (TRADE) as a reward for their work during the year.

In Victorian times, servants were expected to work on Christmas Day, serving their employers' (3) (CELEBRATE). The following day, they were given time off to visit their own families, taking with them a box of gifts, money and food. For many poor families, this was a very (4) (VALUE) addition to their household budget.

Another possible origin is the alms box placed in churches during Advent. On 26 December, the money that had been collected was opened and (5) (DISTRIBUTION) to the poor. The day is also the feast of St Stephen, who was known for his (6) (GENEROUS) towards people in need.

Over time, the (7) (TRADITION) meaning of the day has largely disappeared. For many people today, Boxing Day is about (8) (RELAX): watching football, going for a walk or simply staying at home in front of the television. Horse racing and football matches attract huge crowds, and the day is one of the busiest of the year for the (9) (ENTERTAIN) industry.

It is also, (10) (INCREASE), a day for shopping. Big stores open early, and some shoppers queue through the night in the hope of finding (11) (BARGAIN). In recent years, however, many sales have moved online, and some retailers have even decided to stay closed so that their staff can enjoy a (12) (DESERVE) break.

Whatever people choose to do, Boxing Day remains a uniquely British (13) (INSTITUTE). Perhaps its greatest appeal lies in its (14) (SIMPLE): after the stress of Christmas, it offers a rare chance to do nothing at all – a tradition that most people find (15) (SURPRISE) easy to keep.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. enjoyment

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. sporting
Pridevnik pred activity: sport → sporting. Pridevnik pred activity: sporting.
2. tradesmen / traders / tradespeople
local + oseba v množini. local + osebe v množini: tradesmen/traders.
3. celebrations
employers' + samostalnik v množini. Za svojilnim employers' samostalnik v množini: celebrations.
4. valuable
a very + pridevnik: value → valuable. a very + pridevnik: valuable.
5. distributed
was opened and distributed – trpnik. Vzporedno z opened (trpnik): distributed.
6. generosity
his + samostalnik: generous → generosity. his + samostalnik: generosity.
7. traditional
Pridevnik pred meaning. Pridevnik pred meaning: traditional.
8. relaxation / relaxing
about + samostalnik ali -ing. about + samostalnik/glagolnik: relaxation/relaxing.
9. entertainment
the … industry: samostalnik kot prilastek. Samostalnik kot prilastek pred industry: entertainment.
10. increasingly
Prislov, vrinjen med vejici. Vrinjen prislov: increasingly (vse bolj).
11. bargains
finding + samostalnik v množini. finding + množina: bargains (ugodni nakupi).
12. well-deserved / deserved
Pridevnik pred break. Pridevnik pred break: well-deserved.
13. institution
a uniquely British + samostalnik. a … British + samostalnik: institution.
14. simplicity
its + samostalnik: simple → simplicity. its + samostalnik: simplicity.
15. surprisingly
Prislov pred pridevnikom easy. Prislov pred pridevnikom easy: surprisingly.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear a recording in which Liam Doyle, the lead singer of an Irish rock band, talks about his life. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

I got my nickname, 'Sparrow', at school in Dublin, because I was the smallest boy in the class and I never stopped singing. I hated it at first. Now it's on the cover of every album, so I suppose I've made my peace with it.

We started the band forty years ago in my parents' garage. There were four of us, all fifteen, and only one of us could actually play an instrument. Our first concert was at a school disco, and we were so nervous that we played the same song three times because we'd forgotten the others. Somehow, people danced anyway.

It's strange, but the four of us are still together. People often ask how we've managed it, and the honest answer is that we never let money divide us. From the very first day, everything has been split equally – four ways – no matter who wrote the song. That has saved us from a lot of arguments.

My mother died when I was fourteen, and I think that's really why I started writing songs. I didn't know how to talk about what I felt, so I wrote it down instead. Many of our most famous songs are, if you listen carefully, about loss.

Over the years I've used our success to support causes I care about, especially the fight against poverty in Africa. I've met presidents and prime ministers, and I'm sometimes criticised for that. People say a rock star should stick to music. But if a politician will listen to me for ten minutes because I'm famous, I think I'd be foolish not to use those ten minutes.

These days I still write every morning, usually before anyone else in the house is awake. I'm not as fast as I used to be. But I've learned that the best songs often come when you stop trying so hard.

A singer looks back

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Liam got his nickname at school. (T)
  2. 1.Liam liked his nickname from the start. T / F
  3. 2.The band was formed in a garage. T / F
  4. 3.All four members could play an instrument when they started. T / F
  5. 4.At their first concert, the band played one song several times. T / F
  6. 5.The band members share their income equally. T / F
  7. 6.Liam started writing songs after the death of a family member. T / F
  8. 7.Liam agrees that rock stars should not get involved in politics. T / F
  9. 8.Liam writes faster now than when he was young. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. F
2. T
3. F
4. T
5. T
6. T
7. F
8. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. F
»I hated it at first.« F: sprva ga je sovražil.
2. T
»in my parents' garage«. T: v garaži staršev.
3. F
»only one of us could actually play an instrument«. F: le eden je znal igrati inštrument.
4. T
»we played the same song three times«. T: isto pesem so zaigrali trikrat.
5. T
»everything has been split equally – four ways«. T: vse delijo enako na štiri dele.
6. T
Mama mu je umrla pri štirinajstih. T: pisati je začel po materini smrti.
7. F
Meni, da bi bil neumen, če ne bi izkoristil teh deset minut. F: meni, da mora izkoristiti priložnost za politiko.
8. F
»I'm not as fast as I used to be.« F: ni več tako hiter kot nekoč.

naloge.besedilo:
You will hear a recording about a new book on Harold Gillies, a pioneer of plastic surgery. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Today I'm talking to the historian Dr Laura Finch, whose new book tells the story of Harold Gillies, the man often called the father of modern plastic surgery. Laura, why did you want to write about him?

Dr Finch: Simply because it's a wonderful story. Gillies was a New Zealander who came to England to study medicine and ended up working as an ear, nose and throat surgeon. When the First World War began, he volunteered for the Red Cross and was sent to France.

Presenter: And that changed his career?

Dr Finch: Completely. The war produced injuries that doctors had never seen before. New weapons, especially shells and machine guns, caused terrible damage to soldiers' faces. In the trenches, a man's head was often the only part of his body above ground, so facial wounds were extremely common.

Presenter: What did Gillies do differently?

Dr Finch: Before him, surgeons simply closed the wound as quickly as possible, which often left men unable to eat or speak properly. Gillies insisted on rebuilding the face step by step, using skin and bone from other parts of the patient's own body. He also made detailed drawings before each operation, with the help of an artist, so that he could plan the result.

Presenter: Where did this work take place?

Dr Finch: At a special hospital in Sidcup, near London, which opened in 1917. More than five thousand men were treated there. Gillies developed a technique called the 'tubed pedicle', a tube of skin that stayed attached to the body and kept its blood supply while it was moved to the face.

Presenter: What happened to the patients after the war?

Dr Finch: Many of them found it very hard to return to normal life. In some towns, benches were painted blue as a signal to the public that men sitting on them might have injured faces. That detail affected me more than anything else I discovered while researching the book.

The surgeon who rebuilt faces

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.What was the main reason Dr Finch wrote the book?
    It's a wonderful story.
  2. 1.Where was Harold Gillies from?
  3. 2.What organisation did Gillies volunteer for?
  4. 3.Why were face injuries so common in the trenches?
  5. 4.What problems did the old method often leave patients with?
  6. 5.Who helped Gillies to plan operations?
  7. 6.When did the hospital in Sidcup open?
  8. 7.How many men were treated at Sidcup?
  9. 8.What did blue benches signal to the public?
naloge.rezultat:
1. New Zealand.
2. The Red Cross.
3. The head was above ground.
4. They couldn't eat or speak properly.
5. An artist.
6. In 1917.
7. More than five thousand.
8. That men on them might have injured faces.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. New Zealand.
»Gillies was a New Zealander«. »Where … from« = od kod; Nova Zelandija (New Zealander).
2. The Red Cross.
»he volunteered for the Red Cross«. »What organisation« = katera organizacija; Rdeči križ.
3. The head was above ground.
»a man's head was often the only part of his body above ground«. »Why« = razlog; glava je bila pogosto edini del telesa nad jarkom.
4. They couldn't eat or speak properly.
»unable to eat or speak properly«. »What problems« = kakšne težave; niso mogli pravilno jesti in govoriti (obe težavi).
5. An artist.
»with the help of an artist«. »Who« = oseba; umetnik (slikar) mu je pomagal načrtovati operacije.
6. In 1917.
»which opened in 1917«. »When« = kdaj; leta 1917.
7. More than five thousand.
»More than five thousand men«. »How many« = število; več kot pet tisoč.
8. That men on them might have injured faces.
Modre klopi so opozarjale na moške s poškodovanim obrazom. »Signal« = opozorilo javnosti; na modrih klopeh so sedeli moški s poškodovanim obrazom.

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

Last month you ordered a pair of wireless headphones online as a birthday present for your brother. The delivery was two weeks late, and when the parcel arrived, the headphones did not work properly.

Write an e-mail of complaint of 120–150 words to the online shop SoundStore, in which you:

  • describe the problems caused by the late delivery,
  • explain what was wrong with the headphones,
  • say what you expect the shop to do.
TO: info@soundstore.com
SUBJECT: Complaint
Dear Sir or Madam,
naloge.rezultat: Formalna pritožba z vsemi tremi iztočnicami (posledice zamude, napaka izdelka, jasna zahteva) ter formalnim nagovorom in zaključkom; 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. describe the problems caused by the late delivery
  3. explain what was wrong with the headphones
  4. say what you expect the shop to do
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba pritožbe
Dear Sir or Madam,
Formalni nagovor.
I am writing to complain about an order I placed on your website on 3 May (order no. 4512).
Namen in podatki o naročilu.
The headphones arrived two weeks late, which meant that I had nothing to give my brother on his birthday.
1. iztočnica: posledice zamude.
Moreover, the left earphone does not work and the battery lasts only twenty minutes instead of the advertised twenty hours.
2. iztočnica: konkretne napake.
I would therefore like a full refund, or a replacement sent by express delivery at no extra cost.
3. iztočnica: jasna zahteva.
I look forward to your prompt reply. Yours faithfully, Dominik(a) Novak
Formalni, vljuden, a odločen ton.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a pair of wireless headphones, order number 48213, which I bought from your online shop last month.

I ordered the headphones as a birthday present for my brother, and your website promised delivery within three days. However, the parcel arrived two weeks late, which meant that my brother received nothing on his birthday.

Unfortunately, the headphones did not work properly either. The left earphone makes a loud crackling noise, and the battery lasts less than an hour instead of the twenty hours stated in the description.

I would therefore like you to replace the headphones with a new pair as soon as possible or give me a full refund. I would also expect you to pay the cost of returning them.

I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Matej Kranjc

Število besed: 141 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. We are what we read.
  2. Artificial intelligence makes students lazy.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
