naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Lodger

The lodger arrived on the first Monday of October, carrying a single suitcase and a cello case that was almost as tall as he was. My mother had put a card in the newsagent's window – ROOM TO LET, QUIET PERSON PREFERRED – and I think she regretted the word "quiet" the moment she saw the cello.

His name was Mr Adler, and he was older than she had expected, with white hair and a coat that had once been expensive. He paid three months' rent in cash, in advance, which was more money than I had ever seen on our kitchen table. My mother counted it twice and then hid it in the biscuit tin.

For the first week we hardly heard him. He left the house at seven every morning and came back after dark. Then, on Saturday afternoon, the music began. It came through the ceiling of my bedroom, slow and deep, and I sat on the floor with my back against the wall and did not move until it stopped. I was twelve, and I had never heard anything like it.

After that I began to wait for Saturdays. Sometimes he played the same short passage again and again, as if he were trying to find something he had lost. My mother complained that it gave her a headache, but I noticed she stopped hoovering whenever he started.

In December, Mr Adler fell ill. My mother took him soup and, because he could not climb the stairs to the bathroom, she moved him into our front room. That was when I learned that he had played in an orchestra in Vienna, that he had left in a hurry many years before, and that he had not spoken to his brother since.

He recovered by the spring, and in April he told us he was leaving. A letter had come from Vienna. On his last evening he played for us in the front room, with the curtains open, and people stopped in the street to listen. The next morning his room was empty, except for an envelope addressed to me. Inside was a ticket for a concert, and a note: "For the girl who listens through walls."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.What did the lodger carry when he arrived?
    A suitcase and a cello (case).
  2. 1.What did the narrator's mother think when she saw the cello?
  3. 2.What suggested that Mr Adler had once had money?
  4. 3.Where did the mother keep the rent money?
  5. 4.When did Mr Adler first play the cello in the house?
  6. 5.How did the narrator react to the music the first time?
  7. 6.What did Mr Adler's repetition of a passage seem like to the narrator?
  8. 7.What shows that the mother secretly liked the music?
  9. 8.Why was Mr Adler moved into the front room?
  10. 9.Who had Mr Adler not spoken to for many years?
  11. 10.What did Mr Adler leave for the narrator?
naloge.rezultat:
1. That she should not have written 'quiet' (in the card). / That he would not be quiet.
2. His (once expensive) coat.
3. In the biscuit tin.
4. On Saturday afternoon (in his first week).
5. She sat on the floor and did not move until it stopped.
6. Like looking for something he had lost.
7. She stopped hoovering when he played.
8. He could not climb the stairs (to the bathroom).
9. His brother.
10. A (concert) ticket and a note.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. That she should not have written 'quiet' (in the card). / That he would not be quiet.
»she regretted the word 'quiet'«. Mati je obžalovala besedo »quiet« v oglasu, ker je violončelo videti glasno.
2. His (once expensive) coat.
»a coat that had once been expensive«. »once expensive« coat = nekoč drag plašč; nakazuje nekdanje premoženje.
3. In the biscuit tin.
»hid it in the biscuit tin«. »Where« = kraj; v škatli za piškote.
4. On Saturday afternoon (in his first week).
»Then, on Saturday afternoon, the music began«. »When« = kdaj; v soboto popoldne (prvi teden).
5. She sat on the floor and did not move until it stopped.
Sedela je pri steni in se ni premaknila. Odziv: sedela je na tleh in se ni premaknila, dokler glasba ni prenehala.
6. Like looking for something he had lost.
»as if he were trying to find something he had lost«. Ponavljanje odlomka je bilo kot iskanje nečesa izgubljenega (primera z as if).
7. She stopped hoovering when he played.
Pritoževala se je, a je nehala sesati, ko je začel igrati. Dokaz je dejanje: nehala je sesati, ko je igral.
8. He could not climb the stairs (to the bathroom).
»because he could not climb the stairs«. »Why« = razlog; ni več mogel po stopnicah.
9. His brother.
»had not spoken to his brother since«. »Who« = oseba; brat.
10. A (concert) ticket and a note.
Ovojnica z vstopnico za koncert in listkom. Pustil ji je vstopnico za koncert in listek; navedeš oboje.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (B).

The psychology of keeping things

Almost everyone has a drawer full of objects they never use but cannot throw away: old concert tickets, a broken watch, a stone from a beach. [0] Psychologists have long been interested in why we hold on to such things.

Part of the answer lies in memory. [1] An old ticket can bring back an entire evening – the music, the weather, the people we were with.

Objects can also help us feel connected to people we have lost. [2] For many, a parent's handwriting on a birthday card is more precious than any expensive gift.

Interestingly, the attachment often begins in early childhood. [3] Around the age of two, many children choose a blanket or a soft toy that comforts them when their parents are not there.

In one famous experiment, researchers offered young children an identical copy of their favourite toy. [4] Most refused to swap, even though the copy was, in every way, the same.

Adults behave in a similar way. [5] Economists call this the "endowment effect": once something is ours, we value it more highly than before.

For some people, however, keeping things becomes a serious problem. [6] Their homes fill up until there is no room to cook, sleep or move safely.

Therapists who work with such people do not simply tell them to throw everything away. [7] Instead, they help them understand what each object represents, and find other ways of keeping the memory alive.

Some families have found their own solutions. [8] One woman photographed every object in her late father's workshop before giving the tools to a local school.

In the end, perhaps what we keep says less about the objects themselves than about who we are. [9] A drawer of "useless" things may, in fact, be a kind of autobiography. [10]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AWe are often unwilling to sell something for the price we would pay to buy it.
  2. BEach of these objects carries a story.
  3. CThat approach usually makes the anxiety worse.
  4. DThey believed that the original had something the copy lacked.
  5. EA familiar object can act as a key that opens the door to the past.
  6. FPsychologists call these 'transitional objects'.
  7. GThis condition, known as hoarding disorder, affects around two per cent of adults.
  8. HInstead of keeping the things, they keep a record of them.
  9. IClothes that still smell of someone, for instance, can be impossible to give away.
  10. JThey tell the story of what we have loved and lost.
  11. KAnd, unlike a diary, nobody else can read it.
  12. LChildren usually lose interest in their toys by the age of five.
  13. MMost people throw away the majority of their possessions every few years.
naloge.rezultat:
1. E
2. I
3. F
4. D
5. A
6. G
7. C
8. H
9. J
10. K
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. E
Spomin: predmet kot ključ do preteklosti; sledi primer vstopnice. Poved uvede misel o spominu; naslednja da primer (vstopnica).
2. I
Povezanost z umrlimi – oblačila, ki še dišijo po nekom; sledi primer voščilnice. »for instance« napove primer oblačil, ki še dišijo po nekom.
3. F
Navezanost v otroštvu – »prehodni predmeti«; sledi opis odeje ali igrače. »these« = predmeti iz otroštva; psihologi jih imenujejo prehodni predmeti.
4. D
Poskus s kopijo – otroci so verjeli, da ima izvirnik nekaj, česar kopija nima. »They« = otroci v poskusu; izvirnik ima po njihovem nekaj, česar kopija nima.
5. A
Odrasli: učinek lastništva – predmet, ki je naš, cenimo više. Učinek lastništva: svojih stvari ne prodamo za ceno, ki bi jo plačali.
6. G
Resna težava – kopičenje (hoarding disorder); sledi opis domov. »This condition« poimenuje kopičenje; sledi opis.
7. C
Terapevti ne rečejo »vrzi vse stran«, ker to poveča tesnobo; Instead … »That approach« = »vrzi vse stran«; tesnobo poslabša. Naslednja poved začne z Instead.
8. H
Družinske rešitve: namesto predmetov hranijo zapis; sledi primer fotografij. »Instead of keeping the things« – hranijo zapis; sledi primer fotografij.
9. J
Kaj hranimo – zgodba o tem, kaj smo imeli radi in izgubili. »They« = predmeti, ki jih hranimo; povedo zgodbo o tem, kar smo ljubili.
10. K
Predal kot avtobiografija, ki je nihče drug ne more prebrati. »unlike a diary« dopolni primerjavo predala z avtobiografijo.

Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The island where people talk by whistling

On La Gomera, one of the smaller Canary Islands, you may hear something strange as you walk through the mountains: two people having a conversation (0) a single spoken word. They are using Silbo Gomero, a language (1) consists entirely of whistles.

The island is full of deep valleys, and walking from one village to the next can take hours. Whistling, (2) the other hand, can be heard up to five kilometres away. For centuries, shepherds and farmers used it to pass on news, warn of danger and arrange meetings (3) having to leave their fields.

Silbo is not a code but a way of whistling Spanish. Speakers replace vowels and consonants (4) changes in pitch and length, and listeners who know the language can understand (5) is being said almost as easily as normal speech.

In the second half of the twentieth century, the language nearly disappeared. Roads and telephones made it less necessary, and many young people moved away (6) search of work. By the 1980s, only a few elderly speakers were left, and linguists feared that within a generation it would be lost (7) ever.

The turning point came in 1999, (8) the local government made Silbo a compulsory subject in island schools. Today every child on La Gomera learns it for at (9) two years, and in 2009 UNESCO added it to its list of the world's intangible cultural heritage.

Scientists have become interested (10) well. Brain scans show that experienced whistlers process Silbo in the same areas of the brain that are used for spoken language, (11) suggests that the brain treats it as real language rather than as music.

Not everyone is optimistic about the future. Although children learn the language at school, few of them use it in everyday life, (12) there are fewer and fewer reasons to whistle across a valley. "(13) a language is not spoken at home, it becomes a museum piece," warns one teacher. Others point out that Silbo has survived (14) worse moments. As long as there are people willing to learn it, they say, the mountains of La Gomera will not fall silent – (15) yet.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. without
naloge.rezultat:
1. which / that
2. on
3. without
4. with
5. what
6. in
7. for
8. when
9. least
10. as
11. which
12. because / as / since
13. If / When / Once
14. even
15. not
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. which / that
Oziralni zaimek za stvari: a language which consists of. Oziralni zaimek za language: which/that.
2. on
on the other hand – stalna zveza. on the other hand = po drugi strani.
3. without
without + -ing. without + -ing = ne da bi.
4. with
replace something with something. replace something with something.
5. what
understand what is being said – samostalniški odvisnik. what = tisto, kar (understand what is being said).
6. in
in search of – stalna zveza. in search of = v iskanju.
7. for
lost for ever. for ever = za vedno.
8. when
Časovni oziralni odvisnik za letnico. when za letnico.
9. least
at least – vsaj. at least = vsaj.
10. as
as well – tudi. as well = tudi.
11. which
which se nanaša na ves predhodni stavek. which za vejico se nanaša na ves prejšnji stavek.
12. because / as / since
Vzrok: ker je vse manj razlogov. Vzrok: because/as/since.
13. If / When / Once
Pogoj: če se jezik ne govori doma. Pogoj: If/When/Once.
14. even
survived even worse moments – poudarek. even za poudarek: celo še hujše trenutke.
15. not
not yet – še ne. not yet = še ne.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Gone without a word: the rise of ghosting

It happens to almost everyone sooner or later. You have been chatting with someone for weeks, and then, (0) (SUDDEN), they stop answering. No explanation, no goodbye – just silence. The practice has become so common that it has its own name: ghosting.

Although the word is new, the behaviour is not. People have always found ways to avoid (1) (PLEASANT) conversations. What has changed is how easy it has become. When most of our (2) (RELATION) are carried on through screens, ending one requires nothing more than ignoring a (3) (NOTIFY).

For the person who is ghosted, the experience can be surprisingly painful. Psychologists say that the lack of an (4) (EXPLAIN) is the worst part: without one, people tend to blame themselves and go over every message, looking for a mistake. Some describe a feeling of (5) (HELP), because they have no chance to respond.

Why do people ghost? Surveys suggest that most do it not out of (6) (CRUEL) but to avoid conflict. Many say they did not want to hurt the other person, or simply did not know what to say. Others admit that the relationship was so (7) (SIGNIFY) to them that they did not think an ending was necessary.

Ghosting is not limited to romance. Friends drift apart in the same way, and even employers have been accused of ghosting job (8) (APPLY) after several rounds of interviews. Interestingly, the opposite also happens: (9) (INCREASE) numbers of new employees accept a job offer and then never turn up on their first day.

Experts disagree about how serious the problem is. Some see ghosting as a sign of a wider (10) (WILLING) to deal with difficult emotions, made worse by technology. Others argue that it is sometimes (11) (JUSTIFY), for example when someone feels unsafe or has been treated badly.

What most agree on is that a short, honest message is almost always (12) (PREFER) to silence. It does not need to be long or detailed. A simple "I don't think this is working, but I wish you well" can save the other person weeks of (13) (CERTAIN). As one psychologist puts it, "Closure is a form of (14) (KIND). It costs us a few seconds, and it shows that we respect the other person's (15) (FEEL)."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. unpleasant
Pridevnik pred conversations; smisel: neprijetni pogovori. Pridevnik pred conversations z nikalnim pomenom: unpleasant.
2. relationships
our + samostalnik v množini: relation → relationships. our + samostalnik v množini: relationships.
3. notification
a + samostalnik: notify → notification. a + samostalnik: notification (obvestilo).
4. explanation
an + samostalnik: explain → explanation. an + samostalnik: explanation.
5. helplessness
a feeling of + samostalnik: help → helplessness. a feeling of + samostalnik: helplessness (nemoč).
6. cruelty
out of + samostalnik: cruel → cruelty. out of + samostalnik (iz česa): cruelty (krutost).
7. insignificant / unimportant
Smisel: odnos jim ni bil pomemben: in- + significant. Odnos jim ni pomemben: insignificant/unimportant.
8. applicants
job + oseba v množini: apply → applicants. job + oseba v množini: applicants (kandidati).
9. increasing
Pridevnik pred numbers: increase → increasing. Pridevnik pred numbers: increasing.
10. unwillingness
a wider + samostalnik z nikalno predpono: un- + willing + -ness. a wider + samostalnik z nikalnico: unwillingness.
11. justified / justifiable
is + pridevnik: justify → justified. is + pridevnik: justified/justifiable.
12. preferable
preferable to – boljši od. be preferable to = biti boljši od.
13. uncertainty
weeks of + samostalnik: un- + certain + -ty. weeks of + samostalnik: uncertainty (negotovost).
14. kindness
a form of + samostalnik: kind → kindness. a form of + samostalnik: kindness.
15. feelings
the other person's + samostalnik v množini. the other person's + množina: feelings.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Tom Hughes, a volunteer with a mountain rescue team in the Lake District. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Tom, how long have you been a mountain rescue volunteer?

Tom: Eighteen years now. I joined when I was twenty-four, after I twisted my ankle on a mountain myself and had to be carried down. I was so grateful that I decided I wanted to give something back.

Interviewer: Are all the team members volunteers?

Tom: Every one of them. We have about forty members – teachers, farmers, a dentist, two nurses. Nobody is paid, and we even raise most of the money for our equipment ourselves. A new vehicle costs around sixty thousand pounds, so we spend a lot of weekends shaking collection boxes.

Interviewer: What happens when someone calls for help?

Tom: They ring 999 and ask for the police, who then contact us. Our phones beep, and whoever is free drops what they are doing. I've left a birthday party, a wedding and once even a dentist's chair with my mouth still numb. Usually we're on our way within fifteen minutes.

Interviewer: What kind of people do you rescue?

Tom: All kinds. Many are walkers who are lost or injured, often because they started too late in the day. In summer we see a lot of people in trainers who are not prepared for the weather, which can change very quickly up there. Mobile phones have changed things a lot. People use them to call us, but they also rely on them for maps, and then the battery dies.

Interviewer: What was your most difficult rescue?

Tom: A climber who fell at night in a snowstorm. It took us nine hours to reach him and bring him down. We couldn't use the helicopter because of the wind. He survived, and every Christmas he sends us a card. That makes it all worthwhile.

Interviewer: Any advice for our listeners?

Tom: Tell someone where you're going and when you expect to be back. And carry a paper map. It never runs out of battery.

Mountain rescue volunteer

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

  1. 0.Tom has been a volunteer for ___.
    eighteen years
  2. 1.Tom decided to volunteer because he felt ___ after his own rescue.
  3. 2.The team has about ___ members.
  4. 3.A new rescue vehicle costs about ___.
  5. 4.On weekends, team members often collect money with ___.
  6. 5.The team is usually on its way within ___.
  7. 6.In summer many walkers are wearing ___.
  8. 7.Walkers who rely on phones for maps get into trouble when ___.
  9. 8.Tom's most difficult rescue took ___.
  10. 9.Every Christmas the climber sends the team ___.
naloge.rezultat:
1. grateful / so grateful
2. forty
3. sixty thousand pounds / £60,000
4. collection boxes
5. fifteen minutes
6. trainers
7. the battery dies
8. nine hours
9. a card
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. grateful / so grateful
»I was so grateful that I decided …«. »felt« + pridevnik: grateful (hvaležen).
2. forty
»about forty members«. »about« + število: forty.
3. sixty thousand pounds / £60,000
»around sixty thousand pounds«. »costs about« + znesek: sixty thousand pounds.
4. collection boxes
»shaking collection boxes«. »with« + samostalnik: collection boxes.
5. fifteen minutes
»within fifteen minutes«. »within« + čas: fifteen minutes.
6. trainers
»people in trainers«. »wearing« + oblačilo: trainers (superge).
7. the battery dies
»and then the battery dies«. »when« + stavek: the battery dies.
8. nine hours
»It took us nine hours«. »took« + čas: nine hours.
9. a card
»every Christmas he sends us a card«. »sends« + predmet: a card.

naloge.besedilo:
You are going to listen to an interview with Dr Priya Shah, an ecologist who plants small forests in cities. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Shah, what exactly is a tiny forest?

Dr Shah: It's a very dense forest about the size of a tennis court. The method comes from a Japanese botanist, Akira Miyawaki, who developed it in the 1970s. Instead of planting a few trees far apart, you plant around six hundred young trees very close together – three per square metre.

Interviewer: Why so close?

Dr Shah: Because the trees compete for light, so they grow upwards very fast – about ten times faster than in a normal plantation. After three years the forest needs no more care at all. We also use only native species, at least thirty different ones, so the forest is similar to the one that would have grown there naturally.

Interviewer: What are the benefits in a city?

Dr Shah: Many. A tiny forest can be several degrees cooler than the street next to it on a hot day. It absorbs rainwater, reduces noise and attracts wildlife. In our first forest in Leeds, volunteers counted over five hundred species of insects and animals within two years.

Interviewer: Who does the planting?

Dr Shah: Local people, especially schoolchildren. A planting day usually takes a single morning. We think it's important that people feel the forest belongs to them, so each forest has a group of "tree keepers" from the neighbourhood who collect data and organise events.

Interviewer: Are there any critics?

Dr Shah: Yes. Some foresters say the method is expensive, and that not all the trees will survive in such crowded conditions. That's true – some will die. But that is exactly what happens in a natural forest too.

Tiny forests

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Who developed the method?
    Akira Miyawaki.
  2. 1.How big is a tiny forest?
  3. 2.How many trees are planted per square metre?
  4. 3.How much faster do the trees grow than in a normal plantation?
  5. 4.After how many years does the forest need no more care?
  6. 5.What kind of tree species are used?
  7. 6.How many species were counted in the Leeds forest?
  8. 7.What do the 'tree keepers' do?
  9. 8.What do some foresters criticise about the method?
naloge.rezultat:
1. About the size of a tennis court.
2. Three.
3. About ten times faster.
4. Three (years).
5. Native species (at least thirty).
6. Over five hundred.
7. Collect data and organise events.
8. It is expensive. / Not all trees survive.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. About the size of a tennis court.
»about the size of a tennis court«. »How big« = kako velik; odgovor je primerjava z znano velikostjo (teniško igrišče).
2. Three.
»three per square metre«. »Per square metre« = na kvadratni meter; odgovor je število: tri.
3. About ten times faster.
»about ten times faster«. »How much faster« zahteva primerjavo: približno desetkrat hitreje.
4. Three (years).
»After three years the forest needs no more care«. »After how many years« = po koliko letih; tri leta.
5. Native species (at least thirty).
»we also use only native species«. »What kind of« = katere vrste; samo domače (avtohtone) vrste.
6. Over five hundred.
»over five hundred species … within two years«. »How many species« = število vrst; več kot petsto v dveh letih.
7. Collect data and organise events.
»who collect data and organise events«. »What do … do« zahteva dejavnosti; zbirajo podatke in organizirajo dogodke (obe dejavnosti).
8. It is expensive. / Not all trees survive.
Dovolj je ena od obeh kritik. Gozdarji navedejo dve kritiki; zadošča ena (dražje ali ne preživijo vsa drevesa).

naslov: Angleščina, visja raven, jesenski rok 2024, izpitna pola 3: pisno sporočanje (vadbena pola Učilnica.com)

naloge.besedilo:
Report

Last summer you spent four weeks working as a volunteer guide at a city museum in your town as part of a youth volunteering programme. The programme organisers have asked participants to write a report.

Write a report of 150–180 words in which you:

  • describe your main tasks at the museum,
  • explain what you found most challenging and how you dealt with it,
  • recommend one change that would make the programme better for future volunteers.
To: Programme Organisers
From: Dominik(a) Novak
Subject: Volunteering at the City Museum
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, tremi odstavki s podnaslovi (naloge, izziv in rešitev, predlog izboljšave z utemeljitvijo) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. describe your main tasks at the museum
  3. explain what you found most challenging and how you dealt with it
  4. recommend one change that would make the programme better for future volunteers
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Programme Organisers / From: Dominik(a) Novak / Subject: Volunteering at the City Museum
Glava in naslov.
Introduction: The aim of this report is to describe my four-week placement at the City Museum and to suggest an improvement.
Namen.
Main tasks
I guided groups of foreign tourists through the permanent exhibition and helped with children's workshops at weekends.
Konkretne naloge.
Challenges
The greatest challenge was answering detailed historical questions; I dealt with it by preparing notes with the curators and admitting politely when I did not know an answer.
Izziv + rešitev; višja raven: zapletenejše povedi.
Recommendation
I would recommend a short training course before the placement begins, as this would give new volunteers more confidence.
Predlog + utemeljitev.
Conclusion: Overall, the experience was extremely valuable, and I would encourage other students to take part.
Kratek sklep.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Youth Volunteering Programme Organisers
From: Sara Mlakar
Subject: Volunteer guide at the City Museum

Introduction

This report describes my four weeks as a volunteer guide at the City Museum last summer.

Main tasks

My main task was to lead guided tours of the permanent exhibition for groups of foreign tourists, mostly in English. I also helped with children's workshops and answered visitors' questions at the information desk.

Challenges

The most challenging part was speaking in front of large groups, as I had never done this before. At first I was so nervous that I forgot important dates. I dealt with this by writing short notes for each room and practising the tour with other volunteers, and after a week I felt much more confident.

Recommendation

I would strongly recommend organising a two-day training course before the volunteers start. It would give future participants basic presentation skills and more knowledge of the collection.

Conclusion

Overall, the programme was a valuable experience which I would recommend to other students.

naloge.besedilo:
Discuss the role of Hailsham in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.

Kazuo Ishiguro: Never Let Me Go

Write an essay of 250–300 words. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general.
naloge.rezultat: Esej o vlogi Hailshama: privilegirano otroštvo (umetnost, Galerija) in hkrati iluzija (»told and not told«), razkritje Miss Emily ter pomen Hailshama za Kathyjin spomin; 250–300 besed, brez obnove.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Discuss the role of Hailsham in Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go.
  2. Do not write about the text and/or the author in general (no plot summary, no biography).
  3. Write 250–300 words.
Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu
Esej o književnem delu: zgradba
  • Uvod: avtor, naslov in teza, ki neposredno odgovori na navodilo (Will Freeman changes from a selfish man into …). Brez življenjepisa avtorja.
  • Jedro: dva do trije odstavki, vsak z eno trditvijo. Vsako trditev podpri s konkretnim prizorom ali kratkim navedkom in razloži, kaj pokaže (to je analiza).
  • Primerjava (če gre za dve deli): primerjaj neposredno z »Whereas …«, »Similarly, …«, »In contrast, …«, ne napiši dveh ločenih esejev.
  • Sklep: vrni se k tezi in pokaži, kaj pove o delu kot celoti.
Analiza namesto obnove
  • Navodilo pravi »Do not write about the text and/or the author in general«: ne obnavljaj zgodbe in ne piši splošno o avtorju.
  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).
  • Glagoli za analizo: shows, suggests, reveals, highlights, emphasises, symbolises.
Uporabne zveze
  • This is evident when … · A turning point comes when … · This scene suggests that …
  • At the beginning of the novel, … By the end, … · Gradually, …
  • Whereas X …, Y … · Both novels show … · Unlike …, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – Hailsham is both a protective home and a carefully built illusion that prepares the students to accept their fate.
Teza na začetku; brez obnove.
Jedro 1 – a privileged childhood: art, Exchanges and the Gallery give the students a sense of being special; the guardians protect them from the outside world.
Konkretni prizori: Exchanges, Madame's Gallery.
Jedro 2 – 'told and not told': the students learn about donations gradually, so they never really question them; Miss Lucy is the only guardian who tells the truth.
Pokaži dvoumnost vzgoje.
Jedro 3 – Hailsham after Hailsham: Kathy keeps returning to it in memory; Miss Emily reveals it was an experiment to prove that clones have souls.
Razkritje na koncu spremeni pomen kraja.
Sklep: Hailsham gave its students a happy childhood but not freedom; it is the centre of Kathy's identity.
Vrnitev k tezi.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The role of Hailsham in Never Let Me Go

In Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go, Hailsham is much more than a boarding school. It is the place that shapes the identity of Kathy, Ruth and Tommy, protects them from the truth about their future and, at the same time, prepares them to accept it.

At first, Hailsham seems an ideal childhood world. The students are encouraged to paint and write poems, they collect treasures from the Sales and Exchanges, and the guardians care about their health. Kathy remembers it with great affection, and other carers later envy her for having been there. Hailsham therefore gives the students a sense of being special.

However, this protection is also a form of control. The guardians tell the children about donations so gradually that they never fully understand them; as Miss Lucy says, they are "told and not told". When she finally speaks openly, she is dismissed. Hailsham's kindness thus makes the students obedient rather than rebellious.

Later, Hailsham becomes a memory that the characters cling to. Kathy keeps returning to it in her mind, and a donor asks her to describe it again and again. When Kathy and Tommy finally visit Madame and Miss Emily, they learn the real purpose of the school: it was an experiment to prove that clones have souls, and it has since been closed.

In conclusion, Hailsham represents both the best and the worst of the clones' world. It gives them art, friendship and memories, yet it also teaches them to accept a fate that no human being should accept. Its loss reflects the loss of every illusion in the novel.

Read the text below and choose the correct answer (A, B, C or D). There is an example at the beginning (0).

The Summer of the Kite

The summer I turned fourteen, my parents sent me to stay with my uncle Theo on the island of Inishmore. They said it was because the sea air would be good for me. I knew the real reason: they needed a few weeks to decide whether they still wanted to be married, and they did not want me around while they decided.

Theo lived in a whitewashed cottage at the end of a road that turned into a footpath, then into a field, then into nothing at all. He was my mother's older brother, a former engineer who had come to the island for a month twenty years earlier and simply never left. He had no television and no internet, and his telephone sat on the windowsill like an ornament, because it rang about once a week.

For the first three days I hardly spoke to him. I sat in my room reading the same comic over and over and sending messages to my friends that never arrived, because there was no signal. On the fourth morning Theo knocked on my door with a roll of brown paper, a ball of string and two thin sticks of wood. "The wind is perfect," he said. "We are going to build a kite."

I told him that I was too old for kites. He did not argue. He simply sat down at the kitchen table and started cutting the paper, humming to himself. After twenty minutes my curiosity was stronger than my pride, and I sat down beside him.

Building the kite took the whole day. Theo explained everything as he worked – why the sticks had to cross at exactly the right point, why the tail had to be long and light, how the wind would push against the paper and lift it. He never told me what to do. He asked questions instead, and waited, sometimes for a very long time, until I found the answer myself.

The first flight was a disaster. The kite rose, spun twice and crashed into a stone wall. I was ready to give up, but Theo just laughed and said that every good engineer learns more from a crash than from a success. We repaired it that evening and tried again the next day. This time it climbed so high that it became a small brown dot against the clouds.

We flew it nearly every afternoon after that. Sometimes we talked, sometimes we said nothing for an hour. I told him about school and about my parents, things I had not told anyone. He listened the way he flew the kite: patiently, letting the string out a little at a time.

When my mother came to fetch me at the end of August, she looked tired, but she was smiling, and she held my father's hand on the ferry. I took the kite home with me. It hangs on my bedroom wall now, a little torn, still tied to its string.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.At the beginning of the story, the narrator
    A had just turned fourteen.B was fourteen years old.C was visiting the island with her parents.D had lived on the island before.
    Answer: A
  2. 1.The narrator's parents sent her to the island because they
    A were worried about her health.B wanted time to think about their relationship.C were going on a long holiday.D wanted her to meet her uncle.
  3. 2.The description of the road to Theo's cottage suggests that the cottage was
    A difficult to find.B very isolated.C badly looked after.D close to the sea.
  4. 3.Theo came to live on the island
    A after he retired as an engineer.B because he had a job there.C after a short visit that he extended.D to be close to his sister.
  5. 4.What does the comparison of the telephone to an ornament tell us?
    A It was very old.B It was beautifully decorated.C It was rarely used.D It did not work.
  6. 5.During her first days on the island, the narrator
    A was unable to contact her friends.B talked to Theo about her parents.C explored the island alone.D read all of Theo's books.
  7. 6.Why did the narrator finally join Theo at the table?
    A He asked her to help him.B She wanted to know what he was doing.C She was bored with her comic.D She felt sorry for him.
  8. 7.While they were building the kite, Theo
    A gave her clear instructions.B did most of the work himself.C encouraged her to find solutions.D told her stories about his job.
  9. 8.How did Theo react when the kite crashed?
    A He was disappointed.B He saw it as useful experience.C He decided to build a new one.D He blamed the wind.
  10. 9.The phrase "letting the string out a little at a time" describes Theo's
    A way of listening.B skill as an engineer.C fear of losing the kite.D lack of interest.
naloge.rezultat:
1. B
2. B
3. C
4. C
5. A
6. B
7. C
8. B
9. A
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: izbrati eno od štirih možnosti (A–D).
  • Postopek: najprej preberi vprašanje brez možnosti in v besedilu poišči odgovor; šele nato preberi možnosti in izberi tisto, ki pove isto z drugimi besedami (parafraza).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilna možnost se ujema s pomenom besedila; napačne možnosti pogosto uporabijo iste besede kot besedilo, a povedo nekaj drugega, preveč posplošijo (always, never) ali so resnične, a ne odgovarjajo na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Pripovedovalka pove, da je »sea air« le izgovor: »I knew the real reason: they needed a few weeks to decide whether they still wanted to be married«. Možnost A je uradni, ne pravi razlog.
2. B
Cesta se spremeni v pešpot, nato v polje in nato »into nothing at all« – opis poudarja osamljenost hiše. O tem, ali jo je težko najti (A), besedilo ne govori.
3. C
»had come to the island for a month twenty years earlier and simply never left« – načrtoval je kratek obisk, nato pa ostal.
4. C
Okras (ornament) samo stoji in ga ne uporabljaš; razlaga sledi takoj: »because it rang about once a week«.
5. A
Pošiljala je sporočila, »that never arrived, because there was no signal«. O starših je govorila šele pozneje (B), ko sta spuščala zmaja.
6. B
»my curiosity was stronger than my pride« – radovednost je premagala ponos. Theo je ni prosil za pomoč, »He did not argue«.
7. C
»He never told me what to do. He asked questions instead, and waited … until I found the answer myself.« Možnost A je ravno nasprotje.
8. B
Theo se je zasmejal in rekel, da se dober inženir »learns more from a crash than from a success«. Zmaja sta popravila, novega nista gradila (C).
9. A
Primerjava: »He listened the way he flew the kite: patiently …« – opis vrvice se nanaša na to, kako je poslušal, potrpežljivo in brez pritiska.

Farming on the rooftops

In cities around the world, people are growing food in the most unlikely places.

On a summer morning in Brooklyn, New York, a group of volunteers is picking tomatoes six floors above the traffic, [0]. The farm covers almost a hectare and produces more than twenty tonnes of vegetables a year.

Urban farming is not a new idea. During both world wars, governments encouraged citizens to turn parks and gardens into vegetable plots, [1]. In London, even the moat of the Tower of London was used for growing food.

What is new is the scale. Today, farms are appearing on roofs, in empty car parks and in old factories, [2]. Some of them use no soil at all: the plants grow in water containing nutrients, under special lights that can be switched on day and night.

Supporters say that city farms bring many benefits. Food that is grown close to the people who eat it does not need to be transported for long distances, [3]. Green roofs also keep buildings cooler in summer and absorb rainwater that would otherwise flood the streets.

There are social benefits, too. Many urban farms are run by community groups [4]. Schools bring pupils to learn where vegetables come from, and some farms employ people who have been out of work for a long time.

Critics, however, point out that city farming is expensive. Land in cities costs far more than in the countryside, and indoor farms use huge amounts of electricity, [5]. They also argue that urban farms will never be able to feed whole cities, [6].

Even supporters admit that the numbers are small. But they believe that the real value of city farms is not measured in tonnes. A child [7] is more likely to eat them, they say, and an adult who spends an afternoon digging may start to think differently about food waste.

The Brooklyn farm now sells its vegetables to local restaurants and runs a weekly market. Its manager, a former bank worker, says she has never been happier. "I used to look at numbers on a screen all day," she says. "Now I look at the sky, [8]."

Perhaps, in the future, every new building will have a garden on its roof, [9]. Architects are already designing towers [10], and several cities now offer lower taxes to building owners [11].

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  2. Bwhich was known as "Dig for Victory" in Britain
  3. Cbecause they need much more space than the city has
  4. Dwhich means that their food is not always green

  6. Fwhere nobody would have expected to see a field
  7. Gwhile taxi drivers sound their horns in the street below
  8. Hwho has grown his own carrots
  9. Ijust as every old one once had a chimney
  10. Jbecause I want to know whether it is going to rain
  11. Kwhen they finally decided to stop
  12. Lalthough nobody knows exactly who started it
  13. Mwhose walls are covered in fruit trees and climbing plants
  14. Nwho turn their roofs into green spaces

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. B
Pred vrzeljo je govor o vojnih kampanjah; oziralni »which was known as …« poimenuje to kampanjo. Ločilo pred vrzeljo (vejica) kaže na nedoločilni oziralni stavek.
2. F
Strehe, parkirišča in stare tovarne so kraji, kjer polja ne bi pričakovali: »where nobody would have expected to see a field« se navezuje na naštete kraje.
3. A
Hrana, ki ne potuje daleč: posledica je manj onesnaževanja in bolj sveža hrana. »which« se nanaša na vso prejšnjo trditev.
4. E
»community groups [4]« – samostalnik potrebuje oziralni stavek, ki ga opiše: skupine, ki vabijo prebivalce k skupnemu vrtnarjenju (that invite …).
5. D
Velika poraba elektrike pomeni, da hrana ni nujno »zelena« (okolju prijazna). »which means that« izraža posledico.
6. C
Kritiki trdijo, da mestne kmetije ne bodo nahranile mest, razlog pa je pomanjkanje prostora: »because they need much more space than the city has«.
7. H
»A child [7] is more likely to eat them« – osebek potrebuje oziralni stavek za osebo (who), »them« pa se nanaša na korenje iz dela H.
8. J
Nekdanja bančna uslužbenka zdaj gleda v nebo; razlog je praktičen in kmečki: zanima jo, ali bo deževalo. Ujema se tudi prva oseba (I).
9. I
Primerjava prihodnosti s preteklostjo: »just as every old one once had a chimney« – »one« nadomešča »building« iz prvega dela povedi.
10. M
»towers [10]« potrebuje opis; »whose walls« izraža svojino (stolpi, katerih stene so prekrite z drevjem).
11. N
»building owners [11]« – osebe, zato oziralni »who«; davčne olajšave dobijo lastniki, ki strehe spremenijo v zelene površine.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Why borrow a book when you can borrow a drill?

How often do you use an electric drill? According to one estimate, the average drill is used for just thirteen minutes in its whole life. That is (0) a growing number of towns are opening "libraries of things", where people can borrow tools, tents, sewing machines and even musical instruments instead of buying them.

The first library of this kind in Britain opened in London in 2014. It was started by three friends (1) wanted to reduce waste and help their neighbours save money. Today there are more (2) thirty similar libraries across the country, and the idea is spreading quickly in Europe and North America.

The system is simple. Members pay a small fee, usually between two and ten pounds, (3) borrow an item for a few days. Most libraries are run by volunteers, and many of the objects (4) been donated by local people. "Almost every house has a cupboard full of things that are hardly ever used," says one organiser. "We just help them find a second life."

Borrowers say that the libraries are about more (5) just saving money. Many of them come in for a carpet cleaner and leave with a new friend. Volunteers show people how to use the equipment safely, and some libraries organise repair workshops, (6) visitors learn to fix broken items instead of throwing them away.

There are challenges, of course. Some items come back dirty or damaged, and a few are never returned (7) all. Popular objects, such as party speakers, are often booked weeks (8) advance, especially in summer. Finding a suitable building is also difficult, because rents in city centres are high.

Despite these problems, supporters believe that libraries of things could change the (9) we think about owning things. "Our grandparents shared tools with their neighbours (10) the time," says one volunteer. "Somewhere along the way, we forgot how to do it."

Environmental groups agree. Producing a single drill creates as (11) carbon dioxide as driving a car for about fifty kilometres. If ten families share one drill, the savings are obvious. (12) only that, but borrowing also means less clutter at home.

The libraries are now hoping to attract younger members. Several of them have launched apps (13) show which items are available and allow users to book them online. "Young people already share cars, bikes and flats," says one organiser. "Sharing a lawnmower (14) not that different." If he is right, the library of the future may lend you a ladder (15) easily as a novel.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. why
naloge.rezultat:
1. who / that
2. than
3. to
4. have
5. than
6. where
7. at
8. in
9. way
10. all
11. much
12. Not
13. that / which
14. is
15. as
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. who / that
Oziralni zaimek za osebe (three friends) v vlogi osebka: who ali that.
2. than
Primerjava s številom: more than thirty.
3. to
Namen: pay a fee to borrow – nedoločnik z to izraža, zakaj plačajo.
4. have
Present perfect v trpniku (have been donated); osebek je v množini (the objects).
5. than
Zveza »be about more than« – primerjava: gre za več kot le varčevanje.
6. where
Oziralni prislov za kraj ali okoliščino: workshops, where visitors learn … (na delavnicah).
7. at
Stalna zveza »not … at all« = sploh ne.
8. in
Stalna zveza »in advance« = vnaprej.
9. way
Zveza »the way we think about« = način, kako razmišljamo.
10. all
Stalna zveza »all the time« = ves čas, nenehno.
11. much
»as much … as« pri neštevnem samostalniku (carbon dioxide); many bi bil napačen.
12. Not
Zveza »Not only that, but …« = ne le to, ampak … (velika začetnica, ker začne poved).
13. that / which
Oziralni zaimek za stvari (apps) v vlogi osebka.
14. is
Osebek je glagolnik »Sharing a lawnmower« – glagol je v ednini: is.
15. as
Primerjava enakosti »as easily as« = enako lahko kot.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the correct form of the verbs in brackets in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Isabella Bird: the Victorian woman who travelled the world

In the nineteenth century, respectable British women were expected to stay at home. Isabella Bird, however, (0) (SPEND) most of her adult life travelling to some of the most remote places on Earth.

Born in 1831, Isabella (1) (BE) a sickly child who suffered from back pain and headaches. When she was twenty-two, her doctor (2) (ADVISE) her to take a sea voyage for her health. She sailed to America, and the trip (3) (CHANGE) her life. To everyone's surprise, she felt better on the road than she ever had at home.

Over the next fifty years, she (4) (VISIT) Hawaii, Japan, China, Korea, Persia and Tibet. In the Rocky Mountains she rode alone for hundreds of kilometres and (5) (CLIMB) a mountain over four thousand metres high. While she (6) (TRAVEL) through Colorado, she met a one-eyed outlaw called Mountain Jim, who became one of the heroes of her most popular book.

Isabella wrote long letters to her sister Henrietta, who (7) (LIVE) quietly in Scotland. These letters later (8) (PUBLISH) as books, and they made her famous. Readers loved her honest, funny descriptions, and many of them (9) (NEVER / READ) anything like it before.

Not everyone approved. Some critics complained that a lady should not (10) (WEAR) trousers and ride like a man. Isabella was so angry about one newspaper report that she (11) (COMPLAIN) to the editor.

In 1892 she (12) (BECOME) the first woman to be elected a member of the Royal Geographical Society. By then she (13) (TRAVEL) for almost forty years. Even in her seventies she was still planning new trips; shortly before her death in 1904, she (14) (PACK) her bags for another journey to China.

Today Isabella Bird is remembered as one of the great travel writers. If she were alive now, she would probably (15) (WRITE) a blog.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. spent
naloge.rezultat:
1. was
2. advised
3. changed
4. visited
5. climbed
6. was travelling
7. lived / was living
8. were published
9. had never read
10. wear
11. complained
12. became
13. had been travelling / had travelled
14. was packing
15. write
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: glagol v oklepaju napisati v pravilni obliki (čas, trpnik, nedoločnik, -ing, pogojnik).
  • Postopek: poišči časovne izraze (yesterday, since, for, by the time, next week) in osebek (ednina ali množina, ali osebek dejanje opravlja ali ga trpi). Preveri tudi besede pred vrzeljo, ki zahtevajo določeno obliko (enjoy + -ing, decide + to, would rather + nedoločnik).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, kateri časovni izraz ali zgradba zahteva to obliko.
  • Pasti: pozabljen -s v 3. osebi ednine, napačen pomožni glagol v trpniku, past simple namesto present perfect ob since/for.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. was
Opis v preteklosti (Born in 1831 …): past simple glagola be v 3. osebi ednine.
2. advised
Zaključeno dejanje v preteklosti ob točno določenem času (When she was twenty-two): past simple.
3. changed
Zaporedje zaključenih dejanj v preteklosti: She sailed … and the trip changed her life.
4. visited
»Over the next fifty years« je zaključeno obdobje v preteklosti, zato past simple, ne present perfect.
5. climbed
Vzporedno z »rode« – dva zaključena dogodka v preteklosti: past simple.
6. was travelling
»While« + dejanje, ki je trajalo, ko se je zgodilo nekaj drugega (she met …): past continuous.
7. lived / was living
Opis stanja v preteklosti v oziralnem stavku; sprejemljiv je tudi past continuous.
8. were published
Pisma so izdali drugi: trpnik v preteklosti, množina (These letters) → were published.
9. had never read
Pred branjem njenih knjig (dejanje pred drugim preteklim dejanjem + before): past perfect.
10. wear
Za modalnim glagolom should (not) stoji goli nedoločnik.
11. complained
Zaključeno dejanje v preteklosti: past simple pravilnega glagola complain.
12. became
Dogodek v točno določenem letu (In 1892): past simple nepravilnega glagola become.
13. had been travelling / had travelled
»By then … for almost forty years« – trajanje do točke v preteklosti: past perfect continuous (ali past perfect).
14. was packing
Dejanje v teku tik pred drugim dogodkom (shortly before her death): past continuous.
15. write
Za »would« stoji goli nedoločnik (drugi pogojnik: If she were …, she would write).

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Hannah Price, a vet who treats injured wild animals. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Hannah, most vets look after cats and dogs. Why did you choose wild animals?

Hannah: I grew up on a farm in Wales, so I was surrounded by animals from the start. But the moment I remember best is finding a barn owl with a broken wing when I was nine. The local vet said there was nothing he could do, and I spent the whole summer feeding it with my father. It never flew again, but I decided then that somebody should know how to help animals like that.

Interviewer: How did you train?

Hannah: The normal way – five years at veterinary school in Bristol. Wildlife medicine was only a tiny part of the course, so I spent every holiday volunteering at rescue centres. After I qualified, I worked in a small-animal practice for four years, mostly to pay back my student loan.

Interviewer: And now you run your own hospital.

Hannah: Yes, a small one, on the edge of a nature reserve. We treat around three thousand animals a year: hedgehogs, foxes, swans, bats, even the odd seal. Hedgehogs are the most common patients. Many of them are hurt by garden machines, especially by the robot lawnmowers that work at night.

Interviewer: What is the biggest difference between treating a pet and a wild animal?

Hannah: Stress. A dog knows people and trusts them. For a wild animal, a human is a predator, so simply being held can kill it. We keep the lights low, we speak very quietly, and we try to touch them as little as possible. Sometimes the best medicine is a dark box and silence.

Interviewer: Do you get attached to them?

Hannah: You have to be careful. Our aim is always to release them, so we never give them names. If an animal becomes too used to people, it won't survive outside. The volunteers find that hard – they want to cuddle the baby foxes!

Interviewer: Who pays for all this?

Hannah: Mostly the public. We receive no money from the government, so we depend on donations and on a charity shop in town. Our biggest single cost is not medicine, as people expect, but food. A recovering seal eats several kilograms of fish a day.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to young people who want to do your job?

Hannah: Get experience before you apply, because veterinary schools want to see that you understand what the work is really like. And learn to deal with loss. Not every animal can be saved, and you mustn't let the sad days stop you from coming back the next morning.

An interview with a wildlife vet

As you listen to the recording, answer in note form in the spaces below.

  1. 0.Who does Hannah Price treat?
    (Injured) wild animals.
  2. 1.What did Hannah find when she was nine?
  3. 2.What did Hannah do in her holidays at university?
  4. 3.Why did she work in a small-animal practice after qualifying?
  5. 4.Where is Hannah's hospital?
  6. 5.Which animals are her most common patients?
  7. 6.What often injures hedgehogs?
  8. 7.What can kill a wild animal in hospital?
  9. 8.Why don't they name the animals?
  10. 9.What is the hospital's biggest single cost?
naloge.rezultat:
1. A barn owl (with a broken wing).
2. She volunteered at rescue centres.
3. To pay back her student loan.
4. On the edge of a nature reserve.
5. Hedgehogs.
6. (Robot) lawnmowers / garden machines.
7. Stress. / Being held (by people).
8. Their aim is to release them. / So they don't get used to people.
9. Food.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A barn owl (with a broken wing).
»finding a barn owl with a broken wing when I was nine«. Dovolj je »a barn owl«.
2. She volunteered at rescue centres.
Ker je bila divjad le majhen del študija, je med počitnicami prostovoljno delala v zavetiščih.
3. To pay back her student loan.
»mostly to pay back my student loan« – vprašanje »Why« zahteva razlog oziroma namen.
4. On the edge of a nature reserve.
Neposreden podatek: »on the edge of a nature reserve«.
5. Hedgehogs.
»Hedgehogs are the most common patients.« Ostale živali so le naštete.
6. (Robot) lawnmowers / garden machines.
»hurt by garden machines, especially by the robot lawnmowers«.
7. Stress. / Being held (by people).
Glavna razlika je stres: »simply being held can kill it«.
8. Their aim is to release them. / So they don't get used to people.
Imena bi pomenila navezanost; žival, ki se navadi na ljudi, v naravi ne preživi.
9. Food.
»Our biggest single cost is not medicine, as people expect, but food.« Pozor na past: zdravila niso pravilen odgovor.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Marcus Bell, who directs a theatre company for young people. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Marcus, you started acting very young, didn't you?

Marcus: At seven. My grandmother took me to a pantomime in Manchester, and in the second half the actors asked for a child to come on stage. I put my hand up before she could stop me. I forgot my one line, the audience laughed, and I loved every second of it.

Interviewer: But you didn't go to drama school.

Marcus: No. My parents thought acting was not a proper job, so I studied engineering. I was quite good at it, actually. But every evening I was at a small theatre above a pub, painting scenery and selling tickets. When the director fell ill one season, they asked me to take over a play, and I never went back to engineering.

Interviewer: Did your engineering help?

Marcus: Enormously. Theatre is full of practical problems: how to change a whole set in thirty seconds, how to make a ghost appear. Engineers are trained to solve problems step by step, and that's exactly what a director does in rehearsals.

Interviewer: Tell us about your company.

Marcus: We work with teenagers who have never been to a theatre. Every year we choose about forty of them from schools in the poorest parts of the city. They write the play themselves, based on their own lives, and in July we perform it for one week. Last year's play was about a family who lose their flat, and it was so powerful that a television channel filmed it.

Interviewer: What changes do you see in the young people?

Marcus: Confidence, above all. Many of them arrive unable to look an adult in the eye. By the end, they can stand in front of five hundred people. Teachers tell us that their marks often improve too, because they've learned to concentrate and to work in a team.

Interviewer: What is the hardest part of your job?

Marcus: Saying no. We get about three hundred applications for forty places, and choosing is painful. We try to keep in touch with everyone who isn't selected and invite them to free workshops instead.

Interviewer: What's next for you?

Marcus: We're taking our next production to a festival in Edinburgh. For most of the cast, it will be the first time they've ever left Manchester, so I think the train journey will be just as exciting as the performance.

An interview with a theatre director

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Marcus started acting as a child. (T)
  2. 1.Marcus first appeared on stage because his grandmother asked the actors to choose him. T / F
  3. 2.Marcus's parents did not think acting was a serious career. T / F
  4. 3.Marcus was a poor engineering student. T / F
  5. 4.Marcus became a director when someone else could not do the job. T / F
  6. 5.Marcus believes that directors and engineers solve problems in a similar way. T / F
  7. 6.The teenagers in Marcus's company perform plays by famous writers. T / F
  8. 7.Last year's play was shown on television. T / F
  9. 8.According to teachers, the young actors often do better at school. T / F
  10. 9.Young people who are not selected cannot take part in any of the company's activities. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. F
2. T
3. F
4. T
5. T
6. F
7. T
8. T
9. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. F
Sam je dvignil roko, »before she could stop me« – babica ga ni predlagala.
2. T
»My parents thought acting was not a proper job«.
3. F
»I was quite good at it, actually.«
4. T
Režiser je zbolel in Marcus je prevzel predstavo: »When the director fell ill … they asked me to take over a play«.
5. T
»Engineers are trained to solve problems step by step, and that's exactly what a director does«.
6. F
»They write the play themselves, based on their own lives«.
7. T
»a television channel filmed it«.
8. T
»Teachers tell us that their marks often improve too«.
9. F
Vabijo jih na brezplačne delavnice: »invite them to free workshops instead«.
