naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Daniel Okafor, a journalist, about his childhood. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Daniel, you were born in Lagos but grew up in London. How old were you when you moved?

Daniel: Eight. My mother got a job as a nurse in a London hospital, and the rest of us followed her six months later. I remember the flight very clearly, because it was the first time I had seen snow – we landed in the middle of a snowstorm in January.

Interviewer: Was it difficult to settle in?

Daniel: Very. In Lagos I had been the best reader in my class, but in London the teachers thought I didn't understand English, simply because of my accent. They put me in a group for beginners. It took my mother three visits to the school to convince them to move me.

Interviewer: How did you make friends?

Daniel: Through football, like most boys. I wasn't particularly good, but I had a real leather ball that my uncle had sent from Nigeria, and in those days that made you very popular in the playground.

Interviewer: Did you keep in touch with Nigeria?

Daniel: My grandparents wrote to us every month, long letters on thin blue paper. My job was to read them aloud to my younger sisters, who were starting to forget the language. Every second summer we went back to Lagos for six weeks, and I felt like a different person there – more relaxed, louder.

Interviewer: When did you start writing?

Daniel: At thirteen I started a newspaper for our block of flats. It had one page and came out every Friday. I wrote about broken lifts, new babies and arguments about parking. I sold it for ten pence, and the money paid for the photocopies.

Interviewer: What did you learn from those years?

Daniel: That everybody has a story worth telling. The old man downstairs, who never spoke to anyone, turned out to have fought in the Second World War. When I wrote about him, half the building came to his ninetieth birthday.

Interviewer: Do you feel more British or Nigerian today?

Daniel: Both, and I've stopped thinking I have to choose. My children ask me the same question now, and I tell them they are lucky – they have two homes instead of one.

Growing up between two countries

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Daniel was born in Nigeria. (T)
  2. 1.Daniel's father found a job in London first. T / F
  3. 2.The family arrived in London in winter. T / F
  4. 3.Daniel's teachers in London thought his English was weak. T / F
  5. 4.Daniel was one of the best football players at school. T / F
  6. 5.Daniel's sisters were losing their knowledge of their first language. T / F
  7. 6.The family visited Nigeria every summer. T / F
  8. 7.Daniel's newspaper made a large profit. T / F
  9. 8.The old man downstairs had been a soldier. T / F
  10. 9.Daniel tells his children they should choose one country. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. F
2. T
3. T
4. F
5. T
6. F
7. F
8. T
9. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. F
Službo je dobila mati: »My mother got a job as a nurse«.
2. T
Pristali so januarja med snežnim metežem.
3. T
Zaradi naglasa so mislili, da ne razume angleško, in ga dali v skupino za začetnike.
4. F
»I wasn't particularly good«; priljubljen je bil zaradi usnjene žoge.
5. T
»my younger sisters, who were starting to forget the language«.
6. F
»Every second summer« = vsako drugo poletje.
7. F
Denar je pokril le fotokopije.
8. T
»turned out to have fought in the Second World War«.
9. F
Pravi jim, da imajo srečo, ker imajo dva doma.

naloge.besedilo:
E-mail

You have seen the following advertisement on the website of a youth organisation:

Volunteers wanted! We are looking for students to help at our international summer camp for children aged 8–12. For more information, contact Rebecca Smith.

Write an e-mail of 120–150 words to Rebecca Smith, in which you:

  • explain why you are interested in the job,
  • describe your experience of working with children,
  • ask about accommodation and working hours.
naloge.rezultat: Formalno e-pismo s prijavo: nagovor Dear Ms Smith, uvod z namenom, razlogi za zanimanje, izkušnje z otroki, vljudni vprašanji o nastanitvi in delovnem času, formalen konec (Yours sincerely); 120–150 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. E-mail (120–150 words), formal style
  2. explain why you are interested in the job
  3. describe your experience of working with children
  4. ask about accommodation and working hours
Kako napišeš formalno e-pismo
Formalno e-pismo: zgradba
  • Nagovor: »Dear Mr Smith,« / »Dear Ms Novak,« (če poznaš ime) ali »Dear Sir or Madam,« (če ga ne poznaš). Za nagovorom vejica, nato nov odstavek z veliko začetnico.
  • Uvodni odstavek: v eni ali dveh povedih povej, zakaj pišeš (I am writing to complain about … / I am writing to apply for …).
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku, s konkretnimi podatki (datumi, številke, primeri).
  • Sklepni odstavek: kaj pričakuješ (I look forward to hearing from you. / I would be grateful if you could …).
  • Pozdrav: »Yours sincerely,« (če si začel z imenom), »Yours faithfully,« (če si začel z Dear Sir or Madam) ali nevtralno »Kind regards,«. Nato ime in priimek.
E-pismo s pritožbo (complaint)
  • Povej, kaj si kupil ali obiskal in kdaj (I ordered a pair of headphones on 3 May, order number …).
  • Opiši težave stvarno, eno za drugo, s posledicami (As a result, I had to …).
  • Izrazi nezadovoljstvo vljudno, a odločno: I was extremely disappointed … / This is not what your advertisement promised.
  • Zahtevaj rešitev: I would like a full refund / a replacement. I expect … within … days.
E-pismo s prijavo (application)
  • Povej, kje si videl oglas in za kaj se prijavljaš (I am writing to apply for the position of … advertised on your website).
  • Predstavi se in navedi izkušnje in znanja, ki ustrezajo oglasu (I have been volunteering … / I speak English and German fluently).
  • Pojasni, zakaj te delo zanima in kaj lahko ponudiš (I believe I would be a valuable member of your team because …).
  • Postavi vprašanje, če ga navodilo zahteva (I would also like to know whether accommodation is provided).
Uporabne zveze
  • I would be grateful if you could … · Could you please let me know …? · I would appreciate it if …
  • Firstly, … Secondly, … In addition, … Furthermore, … However, … Therefore, …
  • Please find attached my CV. · I am available for an interview at any time.
Pogoste napake
  • Nagovor »Hello« ali »Hi« in pozdrav »Bye« v formalnem pismu.
  • Skrajšane oblike (I'm, don't, can't) in pogovorni izrazi (gonna, stuff, really cool).
  • Ena dolga poved brez odstavkov; ena iztočnica omenjena le v pol povedi.
  • »Yours sincerely« za »Dear Sir or Madam« (pravilno je Yours faithfully).
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba e-pisma s prijavo
Dear Ms Smith,
Ime poznaš, zato »Dear Ms Smith« in na koncu »Yours sincerely«.
I am writing to apply for the position of volunteer at your summer camp, which I saw advertised on your website.
Uvod: zakaj pišeš in kje si videl oglas.
Odstavek 1: zakaj te delo zanima
I would like to improve my English and I enjoy helping children discover new activities.
Iztočnica 1: dva razloga z because / I would like to …
Odstavek 2: izkušnje
For two years I have been helping at the summer school in my town, where I organise games for nine-year-olds.
Iztočnica 2: present perfect continuous za izkušnje, ki trajajo.
Odstavek 3: vprašanja
Could you please let me know whether accommodation is provided and how many hours a day volunteers work?
Iztočnica 3: posredna vprašanja so vljudnejša (Could you tell me whether …).
I look forward to hearing from you. / Yours sincerely, / Ana Kovač
Formalen konec in polno ime.
Preštej besede (120–150). Brez skrajšanih oblik in pogovornih izrazov.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Dear Ms Smith,

I am writing to apply for the position of volunteer at your international summer camp, which I saw advertised on your website.

I am interested in this job because I enjoy working with children and I would like to improve my English by using it every day. I also believe that an international camp is a great opportunity to meet people from different cultures.

For the past two years, I have been helping at a summer school in my town, where I organise games and craft activities for children aged eight to ten. I am patient and responsible, and I also have a first aid certificate.

Could you please let me know whether accommodation is provided for volunteers? I would also like to know how many hours a day we would be expected to work.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
Ana Kovač

Število besed: 149 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Social media brings people closer together.
  2. Every young person should learn to cook at school.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in jasno povej stališče (I only partly agree that social media brings people closer).
Teza v uvodu; ne prepiši naslova dobesedno.
Jedro 1: argument za + primer (keeping in touch with relatives abroad, video calls).
Temeljna poved, razlaga, primer.
Jedro 2: argument proti + primer (people at the same table looking at their phones; superficial 'friends').
Povezovalci: However, On the other hand.
Jedro 3: tvoje uravnoteženo mnenje (it depends on how we use it).
Pokaži, da razumeš obe strani.
Sklep: povzemi stališče brez novih argumentov.
Odgovori na »How far do you agree?«.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: healthy eating, independence, saving money, less food waste. Against: the curriculum is already full, parents can teach cooking at home.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Social media brings people closer together.

Today almost every teenager has at least one social media account, and many adults spend hours a day online. Some people believe that social media brings us closer together, while others think it does the opposite. In my opinion, the statement is only partly true.

On the one hand, social media makes it easy to keep in touch with people who live far away. My aunt moved to Germany five years ago, but thanks to video calls and photos we still feel part of each other's lives. Social networks also help people with similar interests find each other, for example fans of a rare hobby or patients with the same illness.

On the other hand, social media can push people apart. It is common to see a family sitting at the same table while everybody is looking at their phone. Online "friends" are often not real friends at all, and many young people feel lonely even though they have hundreds of followers. Constant comparison with others can also lead to jealousy and low self-esteem.

In my view, social media itself is neither good nor bad. It brings people closer when we use it to support real relationships, but it separates us when it replaces them.

To sum up, I agree that social media can bring people together, but only if we remember to put our phones away from time to time and talk to the people next to us.

Število besed: 245 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Ghost Ship

On 4 December 1872, the crew of the British ship Dei Gratia noticed a vessel drifting strangely in the Atlantic Ocean, about seven hundred kilometres east of the Azores. Her sails were partly torn, and she was moving in a zigzag, as if nobody were steering. Captain David Morehouse recognised her at once: she was the Mary Celeste, an American cargo ship that had left New York about a week before his own ship.

Morehouse sent three men across in a small boat. What they found has fascinated people ever since. There was nobody on board. The ship was in reasonably good condition, with enough food and water for six months. The cargo – 1,701 barrels of industrial alcohol – was almost untouched. The crew's personal belongings, including their pipes and oilskin coats, were still in their cabins. The only lifeboat, however, was missing, and the ship's last log entry, made nine days earlier, recorded nothing unusual.

The ten people who had sailed on the Mary Celeste – Captain Benjamin Briggs, his wife, their two-year-old daughter and seven crew members – were never seen again.

The crew of the Dei Gratia sailed the Mary Celeste to Gibraltar, hoping to receive a reward for saving her. Instead, they found themselves suspected of a crime. The official in charge of the inquiry, Frederick Solly-Flood, was convinced that the sailors had murdered everyone on board to claim the reward. He pointed to marks on the ship's rail that he believed were caused by an axe, and to stains that he thought were blood. Scientific tests later showed that the stains were not blood at all, and the men were eventually paid, although far less than they had hoped.

Over the years, dozens of theories have been suggested: pirates, a sea monster, a mutiny, even an attack by giant squid. The story became famous in 1884, when a young doctor called Arthur Conan Doyle published a short story about the ship, adding so many invented details that many readers believed it was a true account.

Most historians now favour a simpler explanation. Nine of the alcohol barrels were found to be empty. Alcohol vapour may have leaked and frightened Briggs into thinking the ship was about to explode. He may have ordered everyone into the lifeboat, intending to wait at a safe distance, attached to the ship by a rope. If the rope broke, the small boat would have been left alone in the middle of the ocean.

Nobody will ever know for certain. The Mary Celeste herself had an unlucky career: in 1885 her last captain deliberately ran her onto a reef near Haiti in an attempt to cheat an insurance company. He was caught, and the ship that had survived the ocean empty was finally destroyed by human greed.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.Where was the Mary Celeste found?
    In the Atlantic (east of the Azores).
  2. 1.What suggested to the Dei Gratia's crew that the ship was not being controlled?
  3. 2.Why did Captain Morehouse recognise the ship?
  4. 3.How long could the supplies on board have lasted?
  5. 4.What showed that the crew had left in a hurry?
  6. 5.What was missing from the ship?
  7. 6.What did Solly-Flood suspect the Dei Gratia's crew of?
  8. 7.What did the scientific tests prove?
  9. 8.Why did many readers think Conan Doyle's story was true?
  10. 9.What may have made Briggs think the ship would explode?
  11. 10.Why was the ship finally wrecked?
naloge.rezultat:
1. It was moving in a zigzag.
2. She had left New York shortly before his ship. / He had seen her in New York.
3. (For) six months.
4. Their personal belongings were still there. / They left their pipes and coats.
5. The (only) lifeboat.
6. Murder (to get the reward).
7. The stains were not blood.
8. He added many (invented) details.
9. (Leaking) alcohol vapour.
10. To cheat an insurance company. / For insurance money.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. It was moving in a zigzag.
»she was moving in a zigzag, as if nobody were steering«. Strgana jadra sama po sebi ne pomenijo, da ladje nihče ne krmari.
2. She had left New York shortly before his ship. / He had seen her in New York.
Ladja je odplula iz New Yorka približno teden dni pred njegovo; zato jo je poznal.
3. (For) six months.
»enough food and water for six months«.
4. Their personal belongings were still there. / They left their pipes and coats.
Mornarji ne bi pustili pip in oljnatih plaščev, če bi imeli čas; to je implicitni sklep iz besedila.
5. The (only) lifeboat.
»The only lifeboat, however, was missing«.
6. Murder (to get the reward).
Prepričan je bil, da so mornarji pobili posadko, da bi dobili nagrado.
7. The stains were not blood.
»the stains were not blood at all«.
8. He added many (invented) details.
»adding so many invented details that many readers believed it was a true account«.
9. (Leaking) alcohol vapour.
Prazni sodi kažejo na puščanje; hlapi so ga lahko prestrašili.
10. To cheat an insurance company. / For insurance money.
Kapitan jo je namenoma nasedel, da bi ogoljufal zavarovalnico (human greed).

Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (C).

Can plants hear us?

New research suggests that the green world is far more sensitive than we ever imagined.

For centuries, gardeners have claimed that plants grow better if you talk to them. Scientists usually smiled politely at such stories. [0] Today, however, a growing number of researchers are taking the idea of plant sensitivity seriously.

Plants have no ears, no brain and no nervous system. [1] A team at Tel Aviv University recently recorded tomato and tobacco plants with ultrasonic microphones. When the plants were short of water or had their stems cut, they produced clicking sounds, far too high for human ears.

The researchers were even able to train a computer to recognise the different sounds. [2] In other words, a farmer with the right equipment might one day know exactly when a field needs water.

Other experiments suggest that plants can also respond to sounds around them. In one study, a type of cress was exposed to the recording of a caterpillar eating leaves. [3] The plants that had "heard" the danger produced more of the chemicals that make their leaves taste bitter.

Some flowers seem to react to the buzzing of bees. When evening primroses were played the sound of a flying bee, they made their nectar sweeter within three minutes. [4] Producing sugar costs a plant a lot of energy, so it makes sense to do it only when a customer is close.

None of this means that plants think or feel in the way animals do. [5] They argue that words such as "hear" and "communicate" give the wrong impression, because plants are simply reacting to vibrations, as they react to light or gravity.

The debate is partly about language. [6] For supporters of the new research, the important point is that plants are not passive objects but living organisms that constantly gather information about their environment.

The research may also have practical uses. If farmers can "listen" to their crops, they could water them only when necessary and use fewer pesticides. [7] Engineers are already designing cheap microphones that could be placed in greenhouses.

As for talking to your houseplants, there is still no evidence that they enjoy conversation. [8] But if it makes you water them more regularly, they will certainly be grateful. [9] Perhaps the old gardeners were not entirely wrong after all. [10]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. ASome critics are careful to point out the limits of these findings.
  2. BIn a world that is short of water, this could save huge amounts of it.
  3. CTalking to plants, they said, was a pleasant habit but nothing more.
  4. DYet some of them seem to be able to produce sounds.
  5. EIt could tell, for example, whether a plant was thirsty or injured.
  6. FAfterwards, the scientists tested the chemistry of its leaves.
  7. GPerhaps it is the carbon dioxide in your breath that they appreciate.
  8. HThe same thing did not happen when other sounds were played.
  9. IWhat one scientist calls listening, another calls a mechanical response.
  10. JIn the end, a well-watered plant is a happy plant, whatever you say to it.
  11. KUnfortunately, the experiment could not be repeated.
  12. LTheir belief that plants respond to us may simply have been ahead of its time.
  13. MThis shows that plants are much more intelligent than animals.
naloge.rezultat:
1. D
2. E
3. F
4. H
5. A
6. I
7. B
8. G
9. J
10. L
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. D
Prejšnja poved našteje, česa rastline nimajo (ušes, možganov); »Yet« uvede nasprotje: kljub temu oddajajo zvoke. Naslednja poved te zvoke opiše.
2. E
»It« se nanaša na računalnik iz prejšnje povedi; »for example, whether a plant was thirsty or injured« ustreza poskusu s pomanjkanjem vode in rezanjem stebel.
3. F
Dogodek si sledi: rastlinam predvajajo posnetek, nato (Afterwards) preverijo kemijo listov; naslednja poved poroča o rezultatu.
4. H
Kontrolni poskus: z drugimi zvoki se nektar ni spremenil. Za tem sledi razlaga, zakaj se rastlini to splača.
5. A
Za »None of this means …« sledi »They argue …«, zato mora vrzel predstaviti osebek »they« – kritike (Some critics …).
6. I
»The debate is partly about language« – vrzel to pojasni s primerom: kar eden imenuje poslušanje, drugi imenuje mehanski odziv.
7. B
Zalivanje le, ko je potrebno: »this could save huge amounts of it« (it = water).
8. G
Šaljiva razlaga, zakaj rastline morda uspevajo, ko govorimo z njimi: ogljikov dioksid v dahu.
9. J
Nadaljuje misel o rednejšem zalivanju: ne glede na to, kaj rečeš, je zalita rastlina srečna rastlina.
10. L
Zadnja vrzel poveže konec s prvim odstavkom: vrtnarji so morda le prehiteli znanost (ahead of its time).

Is it time for a four-day working week?

Imagine finishing work on Thursday afternoon and not returning (0) Monday morning – without losing any of your salary. For thousands of employees in Britain, this is no longer a dream.

In 2022, more than sixty British companies took part (1) the world's largest trial of the four-day week. The rules were simple: employees worked eighty per cent of their usual hours, received one hundred per cent of their pay and promised to keep productivity at the same level. The companies ranged from banks and software firms (2) a fish and chip shop.

The results were striking. Most companies reported that productivity stayed the same (3) even improved. Sick days fell by about two thirds, and far fewer people left their jobs. At the end of the six-month trial, the vast majority of the companies decided to continue with the shorter week, and some made it permanent.

Employees said the extra day off changed their lives. Many used it for errands that they would otherwise have done at the weekend, (4) left Saturday and Sunday free for rest and family. Others took up new hobbies, studied or spent more time with elderly parents. "I (5) to be exhausted every Friday," said one office worker. "Now I actually have energy for my children."

How is it possible to do the same work in less time? Managers said that the trial forced them to look carefully at how time was used. Many meetings were shortened or cancelled altogether, and employees were encouraged to switch (6) email notifications for part of the day so that they could concentrate. "We discovered how much time we had been wasting," said one director.

(7), the four-day week is not suitable for every business. Hospitals, schools and shops cannot simply close for a day, and some companies in the trial struggled (8) arrange cover for their customers. Critics also warn that squeezing five days of work into four could increase stress rather than reduce (9).

Others point out that the five-day week (10) itself an invention of the twentieth century. A hundred years ago, many people worked six days a week, and the same arguments (11) used against the change.

Example: 0. until / till
naloge.rezultat:
1. in
2. to
3. or
4. which
5. used
6. off
7. However
8. to
9. it
10. is / was
11. were
12. their
13. about / on
14. to
15. to
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. in
Stalna zveza »take part in« = sodelovati v.
2. to
Zveza »range from … to …« = segati od … do …
3. or
Dve možnosti: ostala enaka ali (or) se celo izboljšala.
4. which
Nedoločilni oziralni stavek se nanaša na vso prejšnjo misel (opravki ob prostem dnevu, kar je sprostilo vikend).
5. used
»used to + nedoločnik« = navada v preteklosti, ki je ni več.
6. off
Frazni glagol »switch off« = izklopiti.
7. However
Prislov za nasprotje na začetku povedi, z vejico.
8. to
Glagol »struggle« + to + nedoločnik = s težavo nekaj narediti.
9. it
Zaimek nadomešča »stress«: increase stress rather than reduce it.
10. is / was
Petdnevni teden je še vedno izum 20. stoletja: is (dejstvo).
11. were
Trpnik v pretekliku, množina (the same arguments were used).
12. their
Svojilni zaimek za države: their own experiments.
13. about / on
»a debate about / on« = razprava o.
14. to
Namen: It took a weekend to remind me (da me je spomnil).
15. to
»have to« = morati; »may soon have to learn«.

Why do we laugh?

Laughter is one of the most (0) (MYSTERY) human behaviours. We all do it, usually many times a day, yet scientists are still not sure exactly why.

One thing is clear: laughter is much older than language. Chimpanzees, gorillas and even rats produce sounds that are similar to laughter when they play, which suggests that our (1) (ANCESTRY) were laughing millions of years before they could speak.

Surprisingly, most laughter has very little to do with jokes. The psychologist Robert Provine spent years listening to people's (2) (CONVERSE) in shopping centres and on university campuses. He found that only about one laugh in five followed anything that was (3) (REMOTE) funny. Most laughter followed ordinary comments such as "I'll see you later" or "Look, there's Andrew."

According to Provine, laughter is above all a social signal. We are thirty times more likely to laugh when we are with other people than when we are alone. It shows (4) (FRIEND), reduces tension and tells others that we belong to the same group. That is why laughter is so (5) (INFECT): when one person starts, others often find it (6) (POSSIBLE) to stop.

Laughter also seems to have real health benefits. Researchers have found that it releases endorphins, chemicals that make us feel good and increase our (7) (TOLERATE) of pain. In one experiment, volunteers who had watched a comedy could keep their hands in ice-cold water for longer than those who had watched a (8) (DOCUMENT) about golf.

Some hospitals have taken this (9) (SERIOUS). Clowns visit children's wards to help young patients relax before operations, and studies show that their presence can reduce (10) (ANXIOUS) as effectively as some medicines. In India, thousands of people meet in parks every morning for "laughter yoga", in which they laugh on purpose, without any reason. At first it feels (11) (COMFORT), they say, but the fake laughter soon becomes real.

There is, however, a darker side. Laughter can be used to exclude people, and being laughed at is one of the most (12) (PAIN) experiences a child can have. Our brains are very good at telling the difference between a warm laugh and a cruel one, even in (13) (STRANGE).

Perhaps the most (14) (REMARK) fact about laughter is how little control we have over it. Try to laugh on command and you will find it surprisingly difficult; try not to laugh at a funeral, and you may find it (15) (BEAR) hard.

naloge.rezultat:
1. ancestors
2. conversations
3. remotely

5. infectious

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. ancestors
Za svojilnim zaimkom »our« samostalnik; glagol »were« zahteva množino: ancestors.
2. conversations
Za »people's« samostalnik v množini (mnogo pogovorov).
3. remotely
Prislov pred pridevnikom (funny): remotely funny = vsaj malo smešno.
4. friendliness / friendship
Za glagolom shows stoji samostalnik: friendliness (prijaznost) ali friendship.
5. infectious
Za »so« stoji pridevnik: infect → infectious = nalezljiv.
6. impossible
Pomen: drugi se ne morejo ustaviti → nikalna predpona im-.
7. tolerance
Za svojilnim zaimkom samostalnik: tolerate → tolerance.
8. documentary
Za nedoločnim členom »a« samostalnik: dokumentarni film.
9. seriously
Prislov ob glagolu »take«: take something seriously.
10. anxiety
Za glagolom reduce stoji samostalnik: anxious → anxiety.
11. uncomfortable
Za »feels« pridevnik; pomen je negativen (sprva je neprijetno) → un- + comfortable.
12. painful
Pred samostalnikom »experiences« pridevnik v presežniku: the most painful.
13. strangers
Za predlogom »in« samostalnik v množini: celo pri neznancih.
14. remarkable
Presežnik pridevnika pred samostalnikom »fact«: the most remarkable.
15. unbearably
Prislov pred pridevnikom (hard); pomen je skoraj neznosno → un- + bear + -able + -ly.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Rosa Fenton, a chef, about her childhood. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Rosa, you grew up in a fishing village in Cornwall. What was it like?

Rosa: Small and windy! There were about four hundred people, one shop and a pub. My father was a fisherman and my mother ran a café on the harbour, so I spent most of my childhood either on a boat or behind a counter.

Interviewer: Is that where you learned to cook?

Rosa: Not exactly. My mother's café served tea and sandwiches – nothing exciting. The real cook in the family was my grandmother. She lived with us, and every Sunday she made fish stew for the whole street. I was allowed to help from the age of six, but only if I cleaned the fish first. I hated that job, but it taught me that good food starts with good ingredients.

Interviewer: Were you a good pupil at school?

Rosa: Terrible! The school was in the next town, and the bus took forty minutes. I used to look out of the window and plan menus instead of doing my homework. My teachers thought I was lazy. Only my art teacher understood me. She said that cooking was a kind of art, and she let me design the posters for the school's Christmas fair.

Interviewer: When did you decide to become a chef?

Rosa: When I was fifteen, a famous chef came to the village to film a television programme. He needed somebody to carry boxes, and my mother sent me. At the end of the day he tasted my grandmother's stew – I had brought some in a flask – and said it was better than anything in his restaurant. That evening I told my parents I was leaving school.

Interviewer: How did they react?

Interviewer: Do you still go back to the village?

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Daniel Okafor, a journalist, about his childhood. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Daniel, you were born in Lagos but grew up in London. How old were you when you moved?

Daniel: Eight. My mother got a job as a nurse in a London hospital, and the rest of us followed her six months later. I remember the flight very clearly, because it was the first time I had seen snow – we landed in the middle of a snowstorm in January.

Interviewer: Was it difficult to settle in?

Daniel: Very. In Lagos I had been the best reader in my class, but in London the teachers thought I didn't understand English, simply because of my accent. They put me in a group for beginners. It took my mother three visits to the school to convince them to move me.

Interviewer: How did you make friends?

Daniel: Through football, like most boys. I wasn't particularly good, but I had a real leather ball that my uncle had sent from Nigeria, and in those days that made you very popular in the playground.

Interviewer: Did you keep in touch with Nigeria?

Daniel: My grandparents wrote to us every month, long letters on thin blue paper. My job was to read them aloud to my younger sisters, who were starting to forget the language. Every second summer we went back to Lagos for six weeks, and I felt like a different person there – more relaxed, louder.

Interviewer: When did you start writing?

Daniel: At thirteen I started a newspaper for our block of flats. It had one page and came out every Friday. I wrote about broken lifts, new babies and arguments about parking. I sold it for ten pence, and the money paid for the photocopies.

Interviewer: What did you learn from those years?

Daniel: That everybody has a story worth telling. The old man downstairs, who never spoke to anyone, turned out to have fought in the Second World War. When I wrote about him, half the building came to his ninetieth birthday.

Interviewer: Do you feel more British or Nigerian today?

Daniel: Both, and I've stopped thinking I have to choose. My children ask me the same question now, and I tell them they are lucky – they have two homes instead of one.

Growing up between two countries

naloge.besedilo:
Report

You recently attended a three-day international youth festival on sustainable living, where you took part in one of three workshops: Zero-Waste Cooking, Upcycling Clothes or Green Energy at Home.

Write a report of 150–180 words to the organisers, in which you:

  • explain which workshop you attended and why you chose it,
  • evaluate what you learned and how you will use it,
  • comment on the organisation of the festival and suggest one improvement.
To: Festival Organisers
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Sustainable Living Festival
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi (izbrana delavnica in razlog, kaj si se naučil in kako boš to uporabil, ocena organizacije s predlogom) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain which workshop you attended and why you chose it
  3. evaluate what you learned and how you will use it
  4. comment on the organisation of the festival and suggest one improvement
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: Festival Organisers / From: Ana Kovač / Subject: Sustainable Living Festival
Glava, nato uvod z namenom (The purpose of this report is to …).
Workshop attended
I chose the Upcycling Clothes workshop because fast fashion is one of the biggest sources of waste among young people.
Iztočnica 1: izbira + utemeljitev.
What I learned
We learned to repair, dye and redesign old garments; I have already turned two old shirts into a bag and plan to run a swap event at school.
Iztočnica 2: ocena in uporaba (I intend to …, which will …).
Organisation and recommendation
The workshops were well prepared; however, the timetable overlapped, so participants could not attend more than one. I would suggest repeating each workshop twice a day.
Iztočnica 3: uravnotežena ocena + konkreten predlog.
Conclusion: Overall, the festival was inspiring and highly practical.
Kratek sklep, formalen slog.
Višja raven: 150–180 besed, pestrejše strukture (trpnik, neosebni izrazi: It was felt that …).
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: Festival Organisers
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Sustainable Living Festival

Introduction

The purpose of this report is to evaluate the three-day Sustainable Living Festival, which I attended last month.

Workshop attended

I chose the Upcycling Clothes workshop, as fast fashion is one of the biggest sources of waste among young people and I wanted to find practical alternatives.

What I learned

We were taught how to repair, dye and redesign old garments. I have already turned two worn-out shirts into a shopping bag, and I intend to organise a clothes swap at my school, which will hopefully encourage other students to buy less.

Organisation

The workshops were well prepared and the leaders were enthusiastic. However, all three workshops took place at the same time, so participants could not attend more than one. I would therefore suggest repeating each workshop twice a day.

Conclusion

Overall, the festival was inspiring and highly practical, and I would recommend it to anyone interested in sustainability.

  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – in a world that takes almost everything from them, friendship is the only thing the clones can truly own, although it is complicated by jealousy and fear.
Teza že v uvodu; brez življenjepisa avtorja in obnove.
Jedro 1 – Kathy and Ruth at Hailsham: Ruth's lies about the pencil case and the 'secret guard'; Kathy plays along out of loyalty.
Konkretni prizori iz Hailshama.
Jedro 2 – the Cottages: Ruth separates Kathy and Tommy, copies the veterans' behaviour; the trip to Norfolk and the 'possible'.
Pokaži, kako ljubosumje rani prijateljstvo.
Jedro 3 – reconciliation: the boat trip, Ruth's apology and the address of Madame; Kathy becomes Ruth's carer.
Vrhunec: prijateljstvo kot odpuščanje pred smrtjo.
Sklep: friendship gives their short lives meaning, even if it cannot save them.
Sklep se vrne k tezi.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed. Podpri trditve s prizori.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Friendship in Never Let Me Go

In Kazuo Ishiguro's Never Let Me Go, the students of Hailsham are raised as clones whose organs will be donated until they "complete". They cannot choose their future, their work or the length of their lives. In such a world, I believe, friendship is the only thing they can truly own, although it is constantly threatened by jealousy and fear.

At Hailsham, the friendship between Kathy and Ruth is already complicated. Ruth pretends that her pencil case was a present from Miss Geraldine and invents a "secret guard" to protect their favourite teacher. Kathy sees through these lies, yet she usually plays along. Her loyalty shows that, for her, belonging to the group matters more than being right.

At the Cottages, the friendship becomes painful. Ruth copies the behaviour of the older veterans and deliberately keeps Kathy and Tommy apart, although she knows they are meant for each other. During the trip to Norfolk to find Ruth's "possible", her disappointment turns into cruelty, and the three friends drift apart.

However, the novel suggests that true friendship includes forgiveness. Years later, the three of them visit a stranded boat in the marshes. Ruth, now weak after her donations, apologises for separating Kathy and Tommy and gives them Madame's address, hoping they can ask for a deferral. Kathy becomes her carer and stays with her until the end.

In conclusion, the friendship between the characters is far from perfect, but it gives their short lives meaning and dignity. It cannot save them from their fate, yet it allows them to face it together, which is perhaps the most human thing they can do.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Boy Who Mapped the Stars

Benjamin Banneker was born in 1731 on a small tobacco farm in Maryland, in what was then a British colony in North America. His grandmother, an Englishwoman who had come to America as a servant, taught him to read using the family Bible. Apart from a few months at a small country school, this was almost all the education he ever received.

As a young man, Benjamin worked on the farm, but in his free time he was fascinated by machines. When he was about twenty-two, he borrowed a pocket watch from a travelling salesman. He took it apart, studied every piece and returned it. Then, using only a knife and pieces of wood, he built a clock of his own. Every part, including the gears, was carved by hand. The clock struck every hour and kept almost perfect time for more than forty years.

News of the wooden clock spread, and people came from miles away to see it. One of the visitors was George Ellicott, the son of a wealthy family of mill owners, who lived nearby. Ellicott was an amateur astronomer, and he lent Benjamin books on astronomy and a telescope. Benjamin, by then nearly sixty, taught himself the mathematics needed to calculate the movements of the planets.

In 1789 he correctly predicted a solar eclipse, although some well-known astronomers had calculated a different date. Encouraged by this success, he began to produce an almanac, a yearly book that contained information about the weather, the tides and the positions of the sun, moon and stars. Farmers and sailors depended on such books, and Banneker's almanac sold well in several cities for six years.

Benjamin also helped to survey the land for the new capital city, Washington. For three months he lived in a tent, recording the positions of the stars every night so that the city's borders could be measured accurately. He was one of very few African Americans who were free at that time, and his work made him famous.

In 1791 he sent a copy of his almanac to Thomas Jefferson, who later became President. In a long letter, he asked Jefferson how he could support freedom for all men while millions of Black people were still slaves. Jefferson replied politely and sent the almanac to scientists in Paris, but he did nothing to change the law.

Benjamin Banneker died in 1806. On the day of his funeral, his house caught fire and burned to the ground. Almost all his papers were lost, and so was the famous wooden clock. Today, a park and a museum near his farm keep his memory alive.

  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. His grandmother.
»His grandmother … taught him to read using the family Bible.«
2. He took it apart (and studied it).
»He took it apart, studied every piece and returned it.« Pozor: ure ni obdržal.
3. Wood.
Uro je izdelal le z nožem in koščki lesa: »every part … was carved by hand«.
4. (For) more than forty years.
»kept almost perfect time for more than forty years«.
5. Books on astronomy and a telescope.
Dovolj je navesti obe stvari: knjige in teleskop.
6. A solar eclipse.
»he correctly predicted a solar eclipse«.
7. Farmers and sailors.
»Farmers and sailors depended on such books«.
8. To measure the city's borders (accurately).
Namen: »so that the city's borders could be measured accurately«.
9. (About) slavery / freedom for Black people.
Vprašal ga je, kako lahko podpira svobodo vseh ljudi, medtem ko so milijoni temnopoltih sužnji.
10. They were lost (in a fire).
Hiša je zgorela na dan pogreba in »Almost all his papers were lost«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and match the statements with the paragraphs. More than one statement may refer to the same paragraph. There is an example at the beginning: Example 0.

Holidays without a car

Five travellers explain how they explored Europe without driving.

A Marta, by night train

I travelled from Vienna to Rome on a night train with my two children. We had our own compartment with four beds, and the children thought it was the best adventure of their lives. We fell asleep in the Alps and woke up in Italy, which saved us the cost of a hotel. The only problem was the price: booking at the last minute, the tickets cost almost as much as flying. Next time I'll book three months in advance.

B Joe, by bicycle

I cycled along the Danube from Germany to Hungary, about a thousand kilometres in three weeks. The route is almost completely flat, so you don't need to be very fit. I carried a tent, but in the end I used it only twice, because the guesthouses along the river were so cheap. The best part was the freedom: whenever I saw a nice village or a beach, I simply stopped. I lost five kilos, although I ate more cake than ever before.

C Ingrid, on foot

My husband and I walked part of the Camino de Santiago in Spain. We walked twenty-five kilometres a day and slept in pilgrims' hostels, sometimes in rooms with forty other people. It is not a holiday for light sleepers! But we met people from all over the world, and some of them are still our friends. My feet suffered for the first week, and I would advise anyone to buy their boots at least a month before they go.

D Tomás, by ferry

Instead of flying to Greece, I took ferries from Italy and then from island to island. Some journeys lasted ten hours, but I didn't mind. I read, slept on the deck under the stars and watched dolphins following the boat. Ferry timetables in Greece change all the time, so you need to be flexible – once I waited two days for a boat. If you are in a hurry, this is not the holiday for you.

E Hannah, by bus

I'm a student, so I travelled around Central Europe on long-distance buses. They are by far the cheapest way to travel; I once went from Prague to Berlin for nine euros. The buses have Wi-Fi and plugs, so I could work on my laptop. On the other hand, the seats are not very comfortable, and on one trip the toilet was broken for six hours. I planned the whole trip with an app, which made it very easy.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Who travelled with children? (A)
  2. 1.Who saved money on accommodation by travelling at night?
  3. 2.Who did not use some equipment as much as expected?
  4. 3.Who made friendships that have lasted?
  5. 4.Who gives advice about preparing equipment?
  6. 5.Who had to change their plans because of transport?
  7. 6.Who could continue studying or working while travelling?
  8. 7.Who was disappointed by the cost of the journey?
  9. 8.Who says the holiday is unsuitable for people with little time?
  10. 9.Who mentions an unexpected effect on their health?
  11. 10.Who used technology to organise the journey?
naloge.rezultat:
1. A
2. B
3. C
4. C
5. D
6. E
7. A
8. D
9. B
10. E
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: vsako trditev poveži z odstavkom, v katerem je ta informacija. En odstavek je lahko odgovor za več trditev.
  • Postopek: preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede; nato preberi odstavke enega za drugim in ob vsakem preveri, katere trditve se nanj nanašajo.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del odstavka, ki pove isto kot trditev. Pozor: trditev je skoraj vedno parafraza, ne dobesedni prepis.
  • Pasti: ista beseda se pojavi v več odstavkih; pravilen je tisti, ki pove celo trditev, ne le del.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A
Na nočnem vlaku so spali, »which saved us the cost of a hotel«.
2. B
Šotor je uporabil le dvakrat, ker so bili penzioni poceni.
3. C
»some of them are still our friends«.
4. C
Svetuje nakup čevljev vsaj mesec dni prej.
5. D
Enkrat je na ladjo čakal dva dni; vozni redi se pogosto spreminjajo.
6. E
Avtobusi imajo Wi-Fi in vtičnice, zato je lahko delala na prenosniku.
7. A
Vozovnice so stale skoraj toliko kot letalske, ker so rezervirali v zadnjem trenutku.
8. D
»If you are in a hurry, this is not the holiday for you.«
9. B
Izgubil je pet kilogramov, čeprav je jedel več peciva kot kdajkoli.
10. E
»I planned the whole trip with an app«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

The fight to save Britain's libraries

Since 2010, almost eight hundred public libraries in Britain have closed, and many others have reduced (0) opening hours. Local councils, which pay for libraries, say they have no choice: their budgets have been cut, and they must spend (1) money they have left on care for the elderly and on children's services.

For many people, (2), the loss of a library is much more than the loss of a building full of books. Libraries are one of the few places where anyone can spend the day without paying. They offer free computers and internet, help with job applications, reading groups for parents and babies, and a warm, quiet place (3) students can do their homework.

"People think libraries are only about books," says Anna Collins, a librarian in Manchester. "But on a typical day I help someone apply (4) a passport, show an elderly man how to use video calls (5) that he can see his grandchildren, and find a quiet corner for a teenager who has nowhere to study at home."

In some towns, local people have refused to accept closures. In the village of Kensal Rise in London, residents campaigned (6) six years to reopen their library after the council closed it. They raised money, organised concerts and (7) took the council to court. The library finally reopened in 2020, run entirely (8) volunteers.

Other libraries have found creative ways to survive. Some have opened cafés or rent rooms to small businesses. Others lend things (9) than books, such as tools, games and even musical instruments. A library in Devon has a "repair café" where volunteers fix broken toasters and lamps.

Critics say that volunteers cannot replace trained librarians, and that (10) is wrong to expect unpaid people to provide a public service. They also point out that libraries in poor areas are the most likely to close, even (11) the people there need them the most.

Despite the closures, libraries remain popular. More than half of British adults visited one last year, and the number of children (12) borrow books has actually increased. During the pandemic, many libraries offered e-books and online story times, and the number of digital loans rose (13) almost fifty per cent.

"A library is a promise," Anna Collins says. "It tells every child that knowledge belongs to them, (14) matter how much money their parents have." It is a promise that many people are determined (15) keep.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. their
naloge.rezultat:
1. the
2. however
3. where
4. for
5. so
6. for
7. even
8. by
9. other
10. it
11. though / if
12. who / that
13. by
14. no
15. to
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. the
Določni člen pred samostalnikom, ki ga določa oziralni stavek: the money (that) they have left.
2. however
Vezniški prislov za nasprotje med vejicama: For many people, however, …
3. where
Oziralni prislov za kraj: a place where students can do their homework.
4. for
Glagol »apply for« = zaprositi za (potni list, službo).
5. so
Namen: »so that« = da bi.
6. for
Trajanje: for six years.
7. even
Prislov »even« poudari presenetljivo dejanje: celo so tožili občino.
8. by
Trpnik: run by volunteers = ki jo vodijo prostovoljci.
9. other
Zveza »other than« = razen, poleg (druge stvari kot knjige).
10. it
Formalni osebek: it is wrong to expect …
11. though / if
Dopustni veznik »even though« = čeprav.
12. who / that
Oziralni zaimek za osebe (children) v vlogi osebka.
13. by
Sprememba količine: rose by fifty per cent.
14. no
Stalna zveza »no matter how« = ne glede na to, koliko.
15. to
»be determined to + nedoločnik« = biti odločen nekaj narediti.

Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

From bitter drink to sweet bar: the story of chocolate

For most of its history, chocolate was not eaten at all. It was a (0) (BITTER) drink.

The Olmecs, who lived in what is now Mexico more than three thousand years ago, were probably the first to grow cacao trees. Later, the Maya and the Aztecs mixed ground cacao beans with water, chilli and spices to make a foamy drink. For the Aztecs, cacao was so (1) (VALUE) that the beans were used as money: a rabbit cost about thirty beans, and a slave about a hundred.

When the Spanish arrived in the sixteenth century, they found the drink (2) (PLEASANT) at first. Soon, however, they started adding sugar and cinnamon, and chocolate became extremely (3) (POPULARITY) at the royal court in Madrid. For almost a century the Spanish kept the recipe a secret, and it was only in the 1600s that chocolate spread to the rest of Europe.

Because cacao and sugar were expensive, drinking chocolate was a sign of (4) (WEALTHY). In London, special "chocolate houses" opened, where rich men met to drink, gamble and discuss politics. Doctors recommended it as a medicine for many (5) (ILL), from stomach problems to tiredness.

The real (6) (REVOLUTIONARY) came in the nineteenth century. In 1828, a Dutch chemist named Coenraad van Houten invented a machine that separated cocoa butter from the beans, producing a fine powder that was much easier to mix. A few years later, a British company called Fry's used this (7) (DISCOVER) to make the first solid chocolate bar.

Swiss chocolate makers then added milk, creating a softer and (8) (SWEETNESS) taste. Rodolphe Lindt invented a process that made chocolate melt (9) (SMOOTH) in the mouth. Thanks to new factories, chocolate was no longer a luxury but something that ordinary people could (10) (AFFORDABLE).

Today, the world eats more than seven million tonnes of chocolate every year. However, the industry has a dark side. Most cacao is grown by small farmers in West Africa, many of whom live in (11) (POOR), and child labour on cacao farms remains a serious problem. Campaigners are calling for (12) (FAIRLY) prices and for chocolate companies to take more (13) (RESPONSIBLE) for the way their beans are produced.

Climate change is a further threat. Cacao trees need a hot, wet climate, and scientists warn that by 2050 many of today's growing areas may become too dry. Researchers are now developing new, more (14) (RESIST) types of cacao. Without them, our favourite treat could become as rare and expensive as it was for the Aztecs, a truly (15) (WORRY) thought for chocolate lovers.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

1. valuable
2. unpleasant
3. popular
4. wealth
5. illnesses
6. revolution
7. discovery
8. sweeter
9. smoothly
10. afford

13. responsibility

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. valuable
Za »so« stoji pridevnik: value → valuable (dragocen).
2. unpleasant
Španci so pijačo sprva težko sprejeli (at first … Soon, however …) → nikalni pridevnik unpleasant.
3. popular
Za »became extremely« stoji pridevnik: popularity → popular.
4. wealth
Za »a sign of« stoji samostalnik: wealthy → wealth.
5. illnesses
Za »many« stoji samostalnik v množini: ill → illnesses.
6. revolution
Za »The real« stoji samostalnik: revolutionary → revolution.
7. discovery
Za »this« stoji samostalnik: discover → discovery.
8. sweeter
Vzporedno s »softer«: primernik pridevnika sweet.
9. smoothly
Prislov opisuje glagol »melt«: smooth → smoothly.
10. afford
Za modalnim »could« stoji glagol: affordable → afford.
11. poverty
Za »live in« stoji samostalnik: poor → poverty.
12. fair / fairer
Pred samostalnikom »prices« stoji pridevnik: fair prices (pravične cene); sprejemljiv je primernik fairer.
13. responsibility
»take responsibility for« = prevzeti odgovornost; za »more« samostalnik.
14. resistant
Za »more« pred samostalnikom »types« stoji pridevnik: resist → resistant (odporen).
15. worrying
Pridevnik na -ing opisuje stvar, ki povzroča občutek: a worrying thought.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Dr Leila Hart, a scientist who studies the planet Saturn. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Hart, when did you first become interested in space?

Leila: When I was ten, my grandfather gave me an old pair of binoculars. One clear night in August, we lay on the grass in his garden and he showed me the moons of Jupiter. They were just four tiny dots, but I couldn't believe that I was looking at other worlds. I asked for a telescope for every birthday after that.

Interviewer: Were you good at science at school?

Leila: Not at first. I actually failed my first physics exam, because I didn't see the point of all the formulas. Then I had a teacher who connected everything to real problems – how to land on Mars, how fast a rocket has to go – and suddenly it all made sense.

Interviewer: What exactly do you study?

Leila: Mainly Saturn's rings. People think they are solid, like a vinyl record, but they are made of billions of pieces of ice, some as small as a grain of sand, others as big as a house. We are trying to understand how old they are. Some scientists think they are as old as the planet itself; others believe they are much younger, perhaps only a hundred million years old.

Interviewer: How do you get your information?

Leila: Mostly from spacecraft. I worked for twelve years on data from the Cassini mission, which orbited Saturn until 2017. At the end of the mission, the spacecraft was deliberately flown into the planet, so that it would not crash into one of the moons and contaminate it with bacteria from Earth.

Interviewer: That must have been an emotional moment.

Leila: Very. About two hundred of us gathered in a control room in California at four in the morning. When the signal stopped, there was complete silence, and then everyone started to clap. Some people had worked on Cassini for thirty years – longer than I had been alive when it was launched.

Interviewer: What is the most exciting discovery you have been part of?

Leila: Probably the water on Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons. Cassini flew through jets of water coming out of cracks in its surface. There is an ocean under the ice, and it may contain the right chemistry for life.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to girls who want to work in science?

Leila: Don't let a bad mark decide your future. And find people who believe in you – for me, that was my grandfather and that physics teacher.

An interview with a space scientist

  8. 7.Why was Cassini flown into Saturn?
  9. 8.How did the scientists react when the signal stopped?

  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

»my grandfather gave me an old pair of binoculars«.

»he showed me the moons of Jupiter«.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Sam Reed, a British explorer and television presenter, about his work. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Sam, you have filmed in more than a hundred countries. Where did it all start?

Sam: In a very ordinary suburb outside London. My parents weren't adventurers at all – my father sold insurance. But we had a big garden that backed onto a wood, and I spent every afternoon there catching frogs, lizards and grass snakes. By the age of eleven I had a collection of thirty animals in my bedroom, which my mother was not happy about.

Interviewer: How did you get into television?

Sam: By writing letters. After university I sent letters to every production company I could find, offering to work for nothing. Only one replied. They needed someone to carry equipment on a trip to Borneo. On the last day, the presenter fell ill, and the director asked me to speak to the camera instead. That was my first programme.

Interviewer: What is the most dangerous situation you have been in?

Sam: People expect me to say sharks or crocodiles, but the real danger is usually the weather. In Alaska, our helicopter couldn't land for three days because of a storm, and we ran out of food. We survived on the fish we caught through a hole in the ice.

Interviewer: Your programmes often show animals that most people find frightening.

Sam: That's deliberate. Everyone loves pandas and dolphins, and they get most of the money for conservation. But spiders, bats and snakes are just as important for the planet, and they are disappearing much faster. If I can make a child think a spider is beautiful, I've done my job.

Interviewer: Has your job changed over the years?

Sam: Enormously. When I started, we went to remote places to film animals nobody had seen before. Now, sadly, many programmes are about animals that are about to disappear. I used to film coral reefs full of colour; on my last trip to the same reef, it was almost completely white.

Interviewer: Is there anything that gives you hope?

Sam: Young people. Wherever I go, I meet teenagers who are organising beach clean-ups, planting trees or protesting outside parliament. They know much more about the environment than my generation did at their age.

Interviewer: And what's next?

Sam: Next year I'm kayaking the length of the Amazon – about six thousand kilometres. It will take about five months. My mother still isn't happy about it.

An interview with a wildlife presenter

  1. 0.Sam grew up near London. (T)
  2. 1.Sam's parents had adventurous jobs. T / F
  3. 2.Sam's mother was pleased about his animal collection. T / F
  4. 3.Many production companies answered Sam's letters. T / F
  5. 4.Sam got his first chance to present because someone was ill. T / F
  6. 5.Sam thinks dangerous animals are the biggest risk of his job. T / F
  7. 6.In Alaska, the team caught their own food. T / F
  8. 7.Sam believes that unpopular animals receive less money for protection. T / F
  9. 8.The coral reef Sam visited recently was more colourful than before. T / F
  10. 9.Sam's next journey will take about five months. T / F

1. F
2. F
3. F
4. T
5. F
6. T
7. T
8. F
9. T
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

Preživeli so z ribami, ki so jih ujeli skozi luknjo v ledu.
