deli.A: A) PISNI SESTAVEK (V ENI OD STALNIH SPOROČANJSKIH OBLIK)

naloge.besedilo:
Article

The online magazine Young Europe is preparing an issue on transport in European cities. Students have been invited to write about their own town.

Write an article of 120–150 words for the next issue, in which you:

  • describe how most people travel around your town,
  • explain what problems cars cause there,
  • suggest one change that would make your town better for pedestrians and cyclists.
naloge.rezultat: Članek z naslovom, pritegnitvenim uvodom, odstavki o tem, kako ljudje potujejo, o težavah zaradi avtomobilov in o enem predlogu za pešce in kolesarje, ter sklep z nagovorom; 120–150 besed, polformalni slog.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Article (120–150 words), semi-formal style, with a title
  2. describe how most people travel around your town
  3. explain what problems cars cause there
  4. suggest one change that would make your town better for pedestrians and cyclists
Kako napišeš članek (article)
Članek (article): zgradba
  • Naslov: kratek in zanimiv; če navodilo ponuja naslove (headings), izberi enega in ga prepiši natančno.
  • Uvod: pritegni bralca (vprašanje, presenetljiv podatek, kratka zgodba) in v eni povedi povej, o čem bo članek.
  • Jedro: vsaka iztočnica v svojem odstavku; vsak odstavek začni s temeljno povedjo in jo podpri s primerom ali podatkom.
  • Sklep: povzemi svoje stališče ali nagovori bralce (So next time you …, why not …?). Nagovora »Dear …« in pozdrava ni.
Slog članka
  • Članek je namenjen širši javnosti (bralcem revije, šolskega časopisa, spletne strani), zato je slog polformalen: živahen, a ne pogovoren.
  • Uporabi retorična vprašanja (Have you ever wondered …?), neposreden nagovor bralca (you) in konkretne primere iz izkušenj.
  • Pri članku z mnenjem (opinion article) jasno povej svoje stališče in ga utemelji, upoštevaj tudi nasprotno mnenje.
  • Tudi v polformalnem slogu se izogibaj slengu (gonna, stuff, super cool) in pretiranim klicajem.
Uporabne zveze
  • Have you ever thought about …? · Imagine a school where … · According to a recent survey, …
  • On the one hand, … On the other hand, … · What is more, … · Not only … but also …
  • All in all, … · It is high time we … · The choice is yours.
Pogoste napake
  • Članek napisan kot pismo (Dear readers, … Yours sincerely).
  • Manjka naslov ali je naslov drugačen od ponujenega.
  • Iztočnice so le naštete, niso razvite s primeri in razlogi.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba članka
Naslov: kratek in zanimiv (Is it time to park the car?).
Članek potrebuje naslov; nagovora in pozdrava ni.
Uvod: vprašanje bralcem (How do you get to school every morning?).
Pritegni bralca in povej, o čem boš pisal.
Odstavek 1: kako ljudje potujejo
Most people in my town drive, even for short distances, because buses run only once an hour.
Iztočnica 1: opis z razlogom.
Odstavek 2: težave
Traffic jams in the centre, noise, pollution and a lack of parking spaces.
Iztočnica 2: dve ali tri težave z razlago posledic.
Odstavek 3: predlog
The town should build a safe cycle lane from the station to the schools.
Iztočnica 3: en konkreten predlog z utemeljitvijo.
Sklep: nagovor bralcev (Why not leave your car at home for one day?).
Polformalni slog, brez slenga.
Preštej besede (120–150). Naslov šteje.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Is it time to park the car?

How do you get to school every morning? In my town, the answer for most people is simple: by car.

Although our town is small, almost everyone drives, even for distances of less than two kilometres. Buses run only once an hour, and there are very few safe cycle paths, so many parents drive their children to school.

This causes several problems. Every morning there are traffic jams in the centre, and the air near the main road is full of fumes. Cars are also parked on pavements, which makes walking dangerous for children and older people.

In my opinion, the town should build a safe cycle lane from the railway station to the schools. If students could cycle without fear, hundreds of cars would disappear from the streets.

Why not leave your car at home for a day?

Število besed: 146 (zahtevanih 120–150). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

naloge.besedilo:
Choose ONE essay title.

  1. Exams are the best way to measure what students know.
  2. Famous people should be role models for the young.

Underline the essay title you have chosen. How far do you agree or disagree with the statement? Support your opinion in 220–250 words.
naloge.rezultat: Argumentativni esej z jasnim stališčem, argumenti s primeri, protiargumentom in sklepom; 220–250 besed, en izbrani naslov.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Choose ONE title and underline it.
  2. State clearly how far you agree or disagree.
  3. Support your opinion with arguments and examples.
  4. Write 220–250 words.
Kako napišeš argumentativni esej
Argumentativni esej: zgradba
  • Uvod (2–3 povedi): uvedi temo s splošno mislijo, trditev iz naslova povej s svojimi besedami in jasno zavzemi stališče (I largely agree that … / I am not convinced that …).
  • Jedro (2–3 odstavki): vsak odstavek ima en argument. Zgradba odstavka: temeljna poved (argument) → razlaga (zakaj drži) → konkreten primer (izkušnja, podatek, primer iz Slovenije).
  • Protiargument: v enem odstavku predstavi nasprotno mnenje in ga ovrzi (Critics argue that … However, …). To pokaže zrelost razmišljanja.
  • Sklep (2–3 povedi): povzemi stališče in odgovori na vprašanje »How far do you agree?«. Brez novih argumentov.
Kako dobiš točke za vsebino
  • Odgovori na naslov, ki si ga izbral, in ga podčrtaj. Ne piši o drugem naslovu.
  • Stališče naj bo jasno in dosledno od uvoda do sklepa. »Deloma se strinjam« je dovoljeno, če pojasniš, v čem da in v čem ne.
  • Primeri morajo biti konkretni: »My cousin spent a year in Ghana …« je boljše kot »Many people do it«.
Uporabne zveze
  • Mnenje: In my opinion, … · I firmly believe that … · It seems to me that …
  • Dodajanje: Furthermore, … · What is more, … · In addition, …
  • Nasprotje: However, … · On the other hand, … · Although …, … · Critics argue that …
  • Primer: For example, … · For instance, … · A good example of this is …
  • Sklep: All things considered, … · To sum up, … · In conclusion, …
Pogoste napake
  • Uvod, ki dobesedno prepiše naslov.
  • Argument brez primera ali primer brez povezave z argumentom.
  • Neformalen slog: you know, a lot of, kids, skrajšane oblike.
  • Prekratko jedro in predolg uvod.
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt (velja za oba naslova)
Uvod: preoblikuj trditev in povej stališče (I do not believe that exams are the best way …).
Jasna teza v uvodu.
Jedro 1: argument + primer (exams test memory and nerves, not understanding).
Temeljna poved, razlaga, primer.
Jedro 2: argument + primer (projects and presentations show skills that exams cannot).
Povezovalci: Moreover, In addition.
Jedro 3: protiargument (exams are fair and objective because everybody answers the same questions … However …).
Upoštevaj nasprotno mnenje.
Sklep: povzemi (a combination of exams and continuous assessment).
Brez novih argumentov.
Ideje za 2. naslov
For: they have influence, they are watched by millions. Against: they did not choose to be role models, parents and teachers are better examples.
Izberi en naslov in ga podčrtaj.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
Exams are the best way to measure what students know.

For most students, exams are the most stressful part of school life. Many people believe that they are the fairest way to find out what we have learned. I do not fully agree, because exams measure only part of our knowledge.

Firstly, exams often test memory rather than understanding. Before a test, many students learn facts by heart and forget them a week later. A good mark therefore does not always mean that a student understands the subject or can use the knowledge in real life.

Secondly, some important skills cannot be tested in a written exam. Projects, presentations and practical work show whether students can cooperate, solve problems and express their ideas. For example, a student who is nervous in exams may give an excellent presentation about a topic he really understands.

On the other hand, exams have one clear advantage: they are objective. Everybody answers the same questions in the same time, and the results can be compared. This is why exams such as the matura are important for university entrance.

In conclusion, I believe that exams are useful, but they are not the best way to measure knowledge on their own. Schools should combine them with projects and continuous assessment, so that every student has a chance to show what they really know.

Število besed: 226 (zahtevanih 220–250). Zgled je eden od mogočih odgovorov; tvoje besedilo je lahko drugačno, a mora izpolniti vse zahteve iz navodila.

Read the text and answer the questions in note form in the spaces below. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Answer 0.

The Language Detective

When Dr Elena Marsh is called to a police station, it is usually because somebody has written something they wish they hadn't. Dr Marsh is a forensic linguist: she studies language to help solve crimes. "Everyone has a linguistic fingerprint," she explains. "The words we choose, the way we spell, even where we put our commas – it is all surprisingly personal."

Her first case came almost by accident. Fifteen years ago, she was teaching English at a university when a detective asked her to look at a series of anonymous letters sent to a local politician. The police had three suspects, but no evidence. Dr Marsh noticed that the writer always used the word "whilst" instead of "while" and wrote "alright" as one word. Only one of the three suspects did the same in his emails. When he was shown her report, he confessed.

Since then she has worked on more than two hundred cases, from threatening text messages to fake wills. In one case, a woman was accused of writing a suicide note for her husband. Dr Marsh compared the note with dozens of the husband's emails and found that he regularly made a spelling mistake that also appeared in the note. The woman was released.

Text messages are a particular challenge. They are short, and people write them quickly, often without punctuation. "Paradoxically, that can make them easier to analyse," she says. "When we write fast, we don't try to sound clever. We just write the way we always do." She is especially interested in abbreviations and emojis, which differ greatly between generations and regions.

Not everyone trusts the method. Critics point out that forensic linguistics is not as precise as DNA testing. A person's style changes depending on who they are writing to, and a clever criminal could deliberately copy someone else's style. Dr Marsh agrees that her evidence should never be used alone. "I can tell a court that two texts are very likely to be by the same person," she says, "but I can't say it is certain."

Recently, she has started to work on a new problem: texts written with the help of artificial intelligence. When a computer helps to write a message, many of the personal features disappear. "It's like a criminal wearing gloves," she says. "The fingerprints are still there, but they are much harder to find."

Despite the difficulties, she loves her job. "Language is the most human thing we have," she says. "Even when people lie, their words tell the truth about them."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. 0.What does a forensic linguist do?
    Studies language to help solve crimes.
  2. 1.What does Dr Marsh compare a person's way of writing to?
  3. 2.What was Dr Marsh's job when she got her first case?
  4. 3.What two features of the letters helped to identify the writer?
  5. 4.What did the police lack in the case of the anonymous letters?
  6. 5.How did the suspect react to her report?
  7. 6.What showed that the husband had written the suicide note?
  8. 7.Why can text messages be easier to analyse, according to Dr Marsh?
  9. 8.What two features of text messages particularly interest her?
  10. 9.What could a clever criminal do to avoid detection?
  11. 10.What happens to personal features when AI helps to write a text?
  12. 11.What does Dr Marsh believe words reveal even when people lie?

1. A (linguistic) fingerprint.
2. She was an English teacher at a university.
3. Using 'whilst' and writing 'alright' as one word.
4. Evidence.
5. He confessed.
6. A spelling mistake he often made.
7. People write them fast, in their usual way.
8. Abbreviations and emojis.
9. Copy someone else's style.
10. Many of them disappear.
11. The truth about them.
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: kratek odgovor (1–5 besed) na vprašanje. Ne pišeš celih povedi, ampak bistvo (note form).
  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: v razlagi spodaj je navedek iz besedila (v narekovajih), na katerem temelji odgovor. Odgovor je pravilen, če pove isto kot navedek, tudi s svojimi besedami.
  • Pasti: odgovor ima preveč besed (več kot 5 ni sprejemljivo); odgovor vsebuje dodatno napačno informacijo; prepišeš del besedila, ki ne odgovarja na vprašanje.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. A (linguistic) fingerprint.
»Everyone has a linguistic fingerprint«.
2. She was an English teacher at a university.
»she was teaching English at a university«.
3. Using 'whilst' and writing 'alright' as one word.
Ločevalni lastnosti sta bili raba »whilst« in zapis »alright« kot ene besede.
4. Evidence.
»The police had three suspects, but no evidence.« Vprašanje sprašuje, česa niso imeli, ne koliko osumljencev so imeli.
5. He confessed.
»When he was shown her report, he confessed.«
6. A spelling mistake he often made.
Ista pravopisna napaka je bila v njegovih e-pismih in v sporočilu.
7. People write them fast, in their usual way.
Pri hitrem pisanju ne poskušamo zveneti pametno, zato pišemo kot vedno.
8. Abbreviations and emojis.
»She is especially interested in abbreviations and emojis«.
9. Copy someone else's style.
»a clever criminal could deliberately copy someone else's style«.
10. Many of them disappear.
»many of the personal features disappear«; primerjava z rokavicami.
11. The truth about them.
»their words tell the truth about them«.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text and choose from the sentences below the one that fits each gap. Each sentence can be used only once. There are two extra sentences which you do not need to use. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0 (C).

Why being bored is good for you

We do everything we can to avoid boredom. Psychologists say we should start welcoming it instead.

Think back to the last time you were bored. If you are like most people, you probably reached for your phone within seconds. [0] Yet a growing body of research suggests that by escaping boredom so quickly, we may be losing something valuable.

Boredom is not the same as having nothing to do. It is the uncomfortable feeling that what we are doing has no meaning or interest. [1] In this sense, psychologists describe it as an emotion that pushes us to change our situation.

In one well-known experiment, two groups of volunteers were asked to think of creative uses for a pair of plastic cups. [2] The bored group produced far more original ideas.

Researchers believe this happens because boredom allows the mind to wander. When we stop focusing on the outside world, the brain starts making unexpected connections between memories and ideas. [3] Many famous writers and scientists have described having their best ideas while walking, washing up or staring out of a train window.

The problem is that today we almost never let this happen. [4] One study found that many people would rather give themselves a small electric shock than sit alone with their thoughts for fifteen minutes.

This constant stimulation may have a price. Some psychologists believe that children who are never bored find it harder to entertain themselves and to develop their own interests. [5] Without the boring hours of a long summer, they say, many of today's adults would never have discovered painting, music or reading.

Of course, not all boredom is helpful. [6] Chronic boredom at school or at work has been linked to stress, poor performance and even depression. The key, researchers say, is the difference between short periods of boredom and a life without meaning.

So what can we do? Experts suggest small changes, such as leaving our phones in another room for an hour or going for a walk without headphones. [7] Teachers and parents, too, might resist the urge to fill every free minute of a child's day with activities.

It may feel strange at first. [8] But if the research is right, a few minutes of doing nothing could be the most productive part of your day. [9]

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  1. AFeeling restless and empty for months is quite different from a quiet afternoon.
  2. BBefore the task, one of the groups had to spend fifteen minutes copying numbers from a phone book.
  3. CScrolling through messages or news is the easiest way to make the feeling disappear.
  4. DIt tells us that we need something more.
  5. EEvery queue, every bus journey and every break is filled with a screen.
  6. FThis is often the moment when creative solutions appear.
  7. GOthers point to their own childhood memories.
  8. HThe aim is not to be bored for its own sake, but to give the mind space.
  9. IMost of us are used to being entertained every second.
  10. JNext time you feel bored, try to stay with the feeling instead of escaping it.
  11. KAs a result, the volunteers decided to stop the experiment.
  12. LBoredom, in fact, is a modern invention.

1. D
2. B
3. F
4. E
5. G
6. A
7. H
8. I
9. J
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel vstaviti en del povedi (ali poved). Dva dela sta odveč.
  • Postopek: preberi besedilo pred vrzeljo in za njo. Ugotovi, kaj mora slediti slovnično (oziralni zaimek, nedoločnik, veznik) in pomensko (razlog, nasprotje, posledica).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: pravilen del se slovnično nadaljuje (npr. za samostalnikom kraja sledi »where …«, za »so« pa »that …«) in pomensko poveže misel pred vrzeljo in za njo.
  • Preverjanje: ko vstaviš vse dele, preberi celo besedilo; ostala dva dela ne smeta pasati nikamor.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. D
Prejšnja poved opiše dolgčas kot občutek, da delo nima smisla; »It tells us that we need something more« pojasni, zakaj ga psihologi imenujejo čustvo, ki nas spodbudi k spremembi (In this sense).
2. B
Opis poskusa: eni skupini so najprej dali dolgočasno nalogo; naslednja poved poroča o »the bored group«, ki brez B ne bi imela pomena.
3. F
Ko možgani povezujejo spomine in ideje, se pojavijo ustvarjalne rešitve; naslednja poved da primere pisateljev in znanstvenikov.
4. E
»we almost never let this happen« – vrzel da primere: vsaka vrsta, vožnja in odmor je zapolnjena z zaslonom.
5. G
Prejšnja poved navaja psihologe (Some psychologists believe …), G doda druge, ki se sklicujejo na otroške spomine; naslednja poved (they say) jih citira.
6. A
»not all boredom is helpful« – vrzel loči kratek dolgčas od mesecev praznine; nadaljuje »Chronic boredom …«.
7. H
Predlogi (telefon v drugi sobi, sprehod brez slušalk) – vrzel pove namen: ne dolgčas zaradi dolgčasa, ampak prostor za misli.
8. I
»It may feel strange at first« – razlog: navajeni smo, da nas nekaj nenehno zabava.
9. J
Sklepni nasvet bralcu: ostani pri občutku, namesto da pobegneš.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and write the missing words in the spaces provided. There is one word missing in each gap. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

When brands get lost in translation

Choosing a name for a new product is never easy. Choosing one that works in every language is (0) harder. Over the years, many international companies have discovered, often too late, that a name that sounds perfect in one country can be embarrassing, or even offensive, in (1).

One of the most famous examples comes from the car industry. When a car manufacturer launched a model called the Nova in Latin America, sales were disappointing. Some people claimed that this was (2) "no va" means "it doesn't go" in Spanish. The story is probably a myth – Spanish speakers would not normally think of the two words together – but it is still taught in business schools (3) a warning.

Other cases are real. A Swedish company once sold a vacuum cleaner in the United States with the slogan "Nothing sucks like an Electrolux". In Sweden the sentence sounded technical; in American English it suggested that the product was terrible. A soft drink company had to change (4) slogan in China after discovering that "brings you back to life" had been translated (5) "brings your ancestors back from the grave".

Food names cause particular problems. A sweet brand that is popular in one European country sounds (6) like the local word for "rubbish" in another, and a popular snack in Japan has a name that English speakers often find amusing. Some companies decide to keep the name anyway, hoping that customers will find it funny (7) than offensive.

To avoid such mistakes, large companies now employ specialists (8) job is to test names in dozens of languages before a product is launched. They check not only the meaning but also the sound, because a name that is difficult to pronounce may be forgotten quickly. Colours and numbers are checked too. In some Asian countries, the number four is associated (9) death, and white is the colour of funerals.

Even with careful research, mistakes happen. When a coffee chain opened its first shops in Australia, it assumed that Australians would love its sweet, milky drinks. (10) did not realise was that Australia already had a strong coffee culture of its own. Within a few years, most of the shops had closed.

The lesson, experts say, is that language is never just a matter (11) words. It carries history, humour and expectations. "A name is the first conversation a company has (12) a customer," says one brand consultant. "If that conversation goes wrong, there may not be a second one."

Interestingly, some brands have turned their mistakes (13) an advantage. A drink with an unfortunate name became a cult product among tourists, (14) bought it as a souvenir simply to photograph the label. Sometimes, it seems, being memorable is (15) important than being perfect.

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. even / much / far
naloge.rezultat:
1. another
2. because
3. as
4. its
5. as
6. almost / exactly / just
7. rather
8. whose
9. with
10. What
11. of
12. with
13. into
14. who
15. more
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. another
»in another (country / language)« = v drugi državi; one … another.
2. because
Vzrok: this was because …
3. as
»as a warning« = kot opozorilo.
4. its
Svojilni zaimek za podjetje (it): its slogan.
5. as
»be translated as« = biti preveden kot.
6. almost / exactly / just
Prislov pred »like«: sounds almost like … (zveni skoraj kot).
7. rather
Zveza »rather than« = namesto, bolj kot.
8. whose
Svojilni oziralni zaimek: specialists whose job is … (katerih delo je).
9. with
»be associated with« = biti povezan s.
10. What
Oziralni zaimek na začetku povedi: What it did not realise was that … (Česar se ni zavedalo, je bilo …).
11. of
Stalna zveza »a matter of« = stvar (česa).
12. with
»have a conversation with« = pogovarjati se z.
13. into
»turn something into« = spremeniti v.
14. who
Nedoločilni oziralni stavek za osebe (tourists): who bought it …
15. more
Primerjava: more important than.

naloge.besedilo:
Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Fake news is nothing new

We often think of fake news as a modern (0) (INVENT), a product of social media and the internet. In fact, false stories have been spreading for as long as people have been able to communicate.

In ancient Rome, Octavian, who later became the emperor Augustus, ran a (1) (SUCCESS) campaign of lies against his rival Mark Antony. He spread rumours that Antony was a drunk who had been (2) (COMPLETE) controlled by the Egyptian queen Cleopatra. To reach as many people as possible, he even had short slogans printed on coins – an early version of the tweet.

The invention of the printing press in the fifteenth century made false information much easier to (3) (DISTRIBUTION). Pamphlets full of (4) (SENSATION) stories about witches, monsters and miracles were sold in markets across Europe. Many of them led to real violence against people who were (5) (FAIR) accused.

One of the most famous hoaxes took place in 1835, when a New York newspaper published a series of articles claiming that a British astronomer had discovered life on the Moon. The articles described bat-like humans, blue unicorns and (6) (BEAUTY) temples. Readers were fascinated, and the newspaper's (7) (CIRCULATE) rose dramatically. When the hoax was revealed, most readers were more amused than angry.

Fake news has not always been so (8) (HARM). In wartime, governments have often used false stories as a weapon. During the First World War, British newspapers reported that German soldiers were using the bodies of dead soldiers to make soap. The story was untrue, but it created such deep (9) (TRUST) that, years later, many people refused to believe the first reports about the Holocaust.

What makes modern fake news (10) (DIFFER) is speed. A false story can now reach millions of people within hours, long before anyone has had a chance to check it. Studies show that false news spreads faster than the truth, partly because it is often more (11) (SURPRISE) and emotional.

Experts say that the best protection is (12) (EDUCATE). Schools in Finland, for example, teach pupils from an early age how to recognise (13) (RELY) sources, check facts and think critically about what they read. Finland now regularly comes first in European rankings of media (14) (LITERATE).

History shows that people have always been willing to believe stories that confirm what they already think. Perhaps the most important skill today is not technology but healthy (15) (SCEPTIC).

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. invention
naloge.rezultat:
1. successful
2. completely
3. distribute
4. sensational
5. unfairly
6. beautiful
7. circulation
8. harmless
9. distrust / mistrust
10. different
11. surprising
12. education
13. reliable
14. literacy
15. scepticism
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. successful
Pred samostalnikom »campaign« stoji pridevnik: success → successful.
2. completely
Prislov opisuje deležnik »controlled«: complete → completely.
3. distribute
Za »easier to« stoji nedoločnik: distribution → distribute.
4. sensational
Pred samostalnikom »stories« pridevnik: sensation → sensational.
5. unfairly
Prislov ob »accused«; pomen je negativen (krivično obtoženi) → unfairly.
6. beautiful
Pred samostalnikom »temples« pridevnik: beauty → beautiful.
7. circulation
Za »the newspaper's« samostalnik: naklada (circulation).
8. harmless
Prejšnji primer (prevara z Luno) je bil zabaven, zato: ni bilo vedno tako nenevarno → harmless.
9. distrust / mistrust
Za »such deep« samostalnik; pomen je negativen (nezaupanje) → distrust ali mistrust.
10. different
»make something different« – za predmetom stoji pridevnik.
11. surprising
Pridevnik na -ing opisuje lastnost novice: surprising (presenetljiv).
12. education
Za »is« stoji samostalnik: educate → education.
13. reliable
Pred samostalnikom »sources« pridevnik: rely → reliable.
14. literacy
Zveza »media literacy« = medijska pismenost; literate → literacy.
15. scepticism
Za pridevnikom »healthy« samostalnik: sceptic → scepticism.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Dr Leila Hart, a scientist who studies the planet Saturn. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Dr Hart, when did you first become interested in space?

Leila: When I was ten, my grandfather gave me an old pair of binoculars. One clear night in August, we lay on the grass in his garden and he showed me the moons of Jupiter. They were just four tiny dots, but I couldn't believe that I was looking at other worlds. I asked for a telescope for every birthday after that.

Interviewer: Were you good at science at school?

Leila: Not at first. I actually failed my first physics exam, because I didn't see the point of all the formulas. Then I had a teacher who connected everything to real problems – how to land on Mars, how fast a rocket has to go – and suddenly it all made sense.

Interviewer: What exactly do you study?

Leila: Mainly Saturn's rings. People think they are solid, like a vinyl record, but they are made of billions of pieces of ice, some as small as a grain of sand, others as big as a house. We are trying to understand how old they are. Some scientists think they are as old as the planet itself; others believe they are much younger, perhaps only a hundred million years old.

Interviewer: How do you get your information?

Leila: Mostly from spacecraft. I worked for twelve years on data from the Cassini mission, which orbited Saturn until 2017. At the end of the mission, the spacecraft was deliberately flown into the planet, so that it would not crash into one of the moons and contaminate it with bacteria from Earth.

Interviewer: That must have been an emotional moment.

Leila: Very. About two hundred of us gathered in a control room in California at four in the morning. When the signal stopped, there was complete silence, and then everyone started to clap. Some people had worked on Cassini for thirty years – longer than I had been alive when it was launched.

Interviewer: What is the most exciting discovery you have been part of?

Leila: Probably the water on Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons. Cassini flew through jets of water coming out of cracks in its surface. There is an ocean under the ice, and it may contain the right chemistry for life.

Interviewer: What advice would you give to girls who want to work in science?

Leila: Don't let a bad mark decide your future. And find people who believe in you – for me, that was my grandfather and that physics teacher.

An interview with a space scientist

As you listen to the recording, complete the sentences. Use 1–5 words for each answer. All contracted forms with the exception of can’t count as two words.

    ten
  2. 1.Leila first looked at the sky with her grandfather in ____.
  3. 2.Through the binoculars, the moons of Jupiter looked like ____.
  4. 3.Physics became interesting when a teacher connected it to ____.
  5. 4.The smallest pieces of Saturn's rings are as small as ____.
  6. 5.Some scientists think the rings may be only ____ years old.
  7. 6.Cassini orbited Saturn until ____.
  8. 7.When the mission ended, about ____ people were in the control room.
  9. 8.Cassini flew through ____ coming from Enceladus.
  10. 9.Leila advises girls not to let ____ decide their future.

1. August / his garden
2. (four) tiny dots
3. real problems
4. a grain of sand
5. a hundred million / 100 million
6. 2017
7. two hundred / 200
8. jets of water
9. a bad mark
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem dopolniti poved z 1–5 besedami.
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem predvidi, kaj manjka (število, kraj, samostalnik). Med poslušanjem zapiši ključno besedo, pri drugem poslušanju preveri.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede del posnetka. Dopolnjena poved mora biti slovnično pravilna.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. August / his garden
»One clear night in August, we lay on the grass in his garden« – sprejemljiva sta oba podatka.
2. (four) tiny dots
»They were just four tiny dots«.
3. real problems
»a teacher who connected everything to real problems«.
4. a grain of sand
»some as small as a grain of sand«.
5. a hundred million / 100 million
»perhaps only a hundred million years old«.

»which orbited Saturn until 2017«.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Sam Reed, a British explorer and television presenter, about his work. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Sam, you have filmed in more than a hundred countries. Where did it all start?

Sam: In a very ordinary suburb outside London. My parents weren't adventurers at all – my father sold insurance. But we had a big garden that backed onto a wood, and I spent every afternoon there catching frogs, lizards and grass snakes. By the age of eleven I had a collection of thirty animals in my bedroom, which my mother was not happy about.

Interviewer: How did you get into television?

Sam: By writing letters. After university I sent letters to every production company I could find, offering to work for nothing. Only one replied. They needed someone to carry equipment on a trip to Borneo. On the last day, the presenter fell ill, and the director asked me to speak to the camera instead. That was my first programme.

Interviewer: What is the most dangerous situation you have been in?

Sam: People expect me to say sharks or crocodiles, but the real danger is usually the weather. In Alaska, our helicopter couldn't land for three days because of a storm, and we ran out of food. We survived on the fish we caught through a hole in the ice.

Interviewer: Your programmes often show animals that most people find frightening.

Sam: That's deliberate. Everyone loves pandas and dolphins, and they get most of the money for conservation. But spiders, bats and snakes are just as important for the planet, and they are disappearing much faster. If I can make a child think a spider is beautiful, I've done my job.

Interviewer: Has your job changed over the years?

Sam: Enormously. When I started, we went to remote places to film animals nobody had seen before. Now, sadly, many programmes are about animals that are about to disappear. I used to film coral reefs full of colour; on my last trip to the same reef, it was almost completely white.

Interviewer: Is there anything that gives you hope?

Sam: Young people. Wherever I go, I meet teenagers who are organising beach clean-ups, planting trees or protesting outside parliament. They know much more about the environment than my generation did at their age.

Interviewer: And what's next?

Sam: Next year I'm kayaking the length of the Amazon – about six thousand kilometres. It will take about five months. My mother still isn't happy about it.

An interview with a wildlife presenter

    More than a hundred.
  2. 1.What did Sam's father do?
  3. 2.How many animals did Sam keep in his bedroom?
  4. 3.What did Sam offer production companies?
  5. 4.What was Sam's job on the trip to Borneo?
  6. 5.Why couldn't the helicopter land in Alaska?
  7. 6.Which animals get most of the money for conservation?
  8. 7.What are many programmes about now?
  9. 8.What gives Sam hope?
  10. 9.How will Sam travel along the Amazon?

2. Thirty.
3. To work for nothing.
4. Carrying equipment.
5. Because of a storm.
6. Pandas and dolphins.
7. Animals that are about to disappear.
8. Young people.
9. By kayak.

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem kratko odgovoriti na vprašanja (note form).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

»my father sold insurance«.
2. Thirty.
»a collection of thirty animals in my bedroom«.
3. To work for nothing.
»offering to work for nothing«.

»They needed someone to carry equipment«.

»our helicopter couldn't land for three days because of a storm«.

naloge.besedilo:
Report

You and your classmates made a short documentary film with the help of a grant from the ScreenCraft Short Film Production Fund. The fund now asks all grant holders to report on their projects.

Write a report of 150–180 words to the ScreenCraft Short Film Production Fund in which you:

  • explain what your film was about and how the money was spent,
  • evaluate the success of the film,
  • describe one difficulty you faced and how you solved it.
To: ScreenCraft Short Film Production Fund
From: Ana Kovač
Subject: Report on our documentary
naloge.rezultat: Formalno poročilo z glavo, namenom, odstavki s podnaslovi (vsebina filma in poraba sredstev, ocena uspeha, težava in rešitev) in sklepom; 150–180 besed.
naloge.razlaga:
Kaj zahteva navodilo: kontrolni seznam

Vsaka vrstica je ena zahteva. Vsaka mora biti v tvojem besedilu jasno vidna (najbolje v svojem odstavku); ko jo napišeš, jo odkljukaj.

  1. Report (150–180 words), formal style
  2. explain what your film was about and how the money was spent
  3. evaluate the success of the film
  4. describe one difficulty you faced and how you solved it
Kako napišeš poročilo (report)
Poročilo (report): zgradba
  • Glava: To: (komu) / From: (od koga) / Subject: (zadeva) / Date: (po želji). Nagovora »Dear …« ni.
  • Naslov ali kratek uvod z namenom: The aim/purpose of this report is to … / This report summarises …
  • Odstavki s podnaslovi: vsaka iztočnica dobi svoj odstavek z jasnim podnaslovom (Host family, School, Recommendations).
  • Sklep ali priporočila: Overall, … / I would recommend … / It would be a good idea to …
Slog poročila
  • Formalen, stvaren, jedrnat: dejstva, številke, ocene z utemeljitvijo.
  • Pogosti so trpnik in neosebni izrazi: The event was attended by … / It was felt that … / Most participants agreed that …
  • Ocena naj bo uravnotežena: pohvala in kritika (The timetable was well organised; however, …).
  • Ni skrajšanih oblik, ni čustvenih vzklikov. Prva oseba (I, we) je dovoljena, a besedilo naj ne zveni kot dnevnik.
Uporabne zveze
  • The aim of this report is to … · This report is based on …
  • The most successful part was … because … · One drawback was …
  • I would strongly recommend … · In conclusion, … · To sum up, …
Ocenjevanje in postopek pisanja
Kako ocenjujejo pisni sestavek
  • Vsebina: ali si odgovoril na vse iztočnice (alineje) iz navodila in ali je vsaka dovolj razvita (ne le omenjena v pol povedi). Manjkajoča iztočnica je največja izguba točk.
  • Zgradba in oblika: odstavki, logično zaporedje, povezovalci (linking words), oblika, ki ustreza besedilni vrsti (nagovor in pozdrav pri e-pismu, glava in podnaslovi pri poročilu).
  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.

  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Zgradba poročila
To: ScreenCraft Short Film Production Fund / From: Ana Kovač / Subject: Report on 'The Last Mill'
Glava, uvod z namenom (This report summarises …).
The film and the budget
The film tells the story of the last working mill in our valley; the grant covered camera hire, editing software and travel.
Iztočnica 1: vsebina + kako je bil porabljen denar (konkretni postavki).
Success

Iztočnica 2: merljivi dosežki in ocena.
Difficulty

Iztočnica 3: težava + rešitev (As a result, we decided to …).
Conclusion: We are grateful for the support and would recommend the fund to other young filmmakers.
Sklep v formalnem slogu.
Višja raven: 150–180 besed; pasivne zgradbe in neosebni izrazi so zaželeni.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
To: ScreenCraft Short Film Production Fund
From: Ana Kovač, Gimnazija Kranj
Subject: Report on our documentary The Last Mill

Introduction

This report summarises the documentary that our film club produced with the help of your grant.

The film and the budget

The Last Mill tells the story of the last working water mill in our valley and of the family who have run it for five generations. The grant covered camera and microphone hire, editing software and transport.

Success

The film was screened at two regional festivals, where it received an award for the best student documentary. It has also been viewed over 3,000 times online, and a regional television channel has expressed interest in broadcasting it.

Difficulties

During the second week of filming, heavy rain flooded the mill, so we were unable to film outdoors. As a result, we rescheduled the shooting and recorded the interviews in the family's kitchen, which made the film more personal.

Conclusion

We are extremely grateful for your support and would strongly recommend the fund to other young filmmakers.

Kako napišeš esej o književnem delu

Analiza namesto obnove

  • Zgradba odstavka PEA: Point (trditev) → Evidence (prizor, navedek) → Analysis (kaj to pomeni za temo).
  • Uporabljaj sedanjik za dogajanje v delu (Will lies to the single mothers …).

  • Besedišče: pestro, natančno in primerno slogu; isto besedo ne ponavljaj, uporabi sopomenke.
  • Slovnica in pravopis: pravilni časi, ujemanje osebka in glagola (he goes), členi (a/an/the), predlogi, velika začetnica in ločila.
  • Dolžina: drži se razpona besed iz navodila. Prekratko besedilo navadno ne pokrije vseh iztočnic, predolgo pa izgubi točke za obliko.
Postopek v petih korakih
  • 1. Preberi navodilo dvakrat in podčrtaj: komu pišeš, zakaj pišeš (pritožba, prijava, poročilo …) in vse iztočnice.
  • 2. Naredi načrt: ob vsako iztočnico napiši dve do tri ključne besede in konkreten podatek (številko, datum, primer).
  • 3. Piši po odstavkih: praviloma ena iztočnica = en odstavek. Vsak odstavek začni s povedjo, ki pove, o čem govori.
  • 4. Preveri slog: formalno besedilo nima skrajšanih oblik (I'm → I am), pogovornih izrazov (stuff, a lot of → a great deal of) in klicajev.
  • 5. Preštej besede in popravi: preveri čase, -s v 3. osebi ednine, člene in črkovanje.
Načrt po korakih
Načrt eseja
Uvod: teza – the conch is the symbol of order and democracy; the boys' society lasts exactly as long as they respect it.
Teza v uvodu, brez obnove in avtorjevega življenjepisa.
Jedro 1 – Ralph and Piggy find the conch; Ralph blows it and is elected chief because he holds it.
Konkreten prizor s prve strani dogajanja.
Jedro 2 – the rule 'whoever holds the conch speaks'; Jack increasingly ignores it ('Bollocks to the rules!').
Pokaži upadanje avtoritete školjke.
Jedro 3 – the conch is smashed when Piggy is killed at Castle Rock; order is gone and the hunt for Ralph begins.
Simbolni konec: uničenje školjke in Piggyja hkrati.
Sklep: the conch shows how fragile civilisation is when it depends only on agreement.
Sklep razširi tezo.
Merila: vsebina in interpretacija, zgradba, jezik. 250–300 besed.
Zgledno besedilo (eden od mogočih odgovorov)
The importance of the conch in Lord of the Flies

In William Golding's Lord of the Flies, a group of boys stranded on a desert island try to build a society of their own. At the centre of this society is a simple object: a pink and cream conch shell. In my opinion, the conch symbolises order and democracy, and the boys' civilisation survives exactly as long as they respect it.

The conch appears at the very beginning of the novel. Ralph and Piggy find it in a lagoon, and Piggy explains how to blow it. When Ralph produces a loud, deep sound, boys come from all over the island. Because he is the one holding the conch, they elect him chief, even though Jack seems a more natural leader.

The boys soon agree on a rule: whoever holds the conch has the right to speak. For a while this works. Even the shy littluns are listened to when they hold the shell. However, the rule is only as strong as the boys' willingness to obey it. Jack increasingly interrupts others and finally shouts, "Bollocks to the rules!", showing that power, not discussion, now matters to him.

The final destruction of the conch is one of the most shocking moments in the novel. When Piggy goes to Castle Rock holding the shell and asks the boys whether it is better to have rules or to hunt and kill, Roger releases a huge rock. Piggy is killed and the conch "exploded into a thousand white fragments". Immediately afterwards, Jack declares himself chief, and the hunt for Ralph begins.

In conclusion, the conch shows how fragile civilisation is when it depends only on agreement. Once the boys stop respecting it, nothing remains to protect the weak.

The Village That Saved a Language

When Ana Rojas was a child, she spoke two languages: Spanish at school and Kallawaya at home. Kallawaya was the language of her grandparents, traditional healers in the mountains of Bolivia who travelled from village to village treating the sick with medicinal plants. By the time Ana was twenty, however, she realised that almost nobody of her age could understand it.

Kallawaya was never spoken by many people. For centuries it was a secret language, used mainly by healers to talk about plants and remedies without being understood by their patients. Children learned it from their fathers, and only men were traditionally allowed to use it. When young people began moving to the cities in search of work, the chain was broken. By the year 2000, fewer than a hundred people could speak it fluently.

Ana decided to do something. She was studying to become a teacher, and she spent her holidays visiting elderly speakers with a notebook and a small tape recorder. Many of them were suspicious at first. They had been taught that the language must never be shared with outsiders, and Ana, as a woman, was not supposed to know it at all. It took her two years to persuade the oldest healer in her village to record a single conversation.

Slowly, the situation changed. The healers began to understand that if they did not share their knowledge, it would die with them. They agreed to work with Ana on a dictionary, which now contains more than three thousand words, most of them names of plants. Ana also wrote a series of picture books for children, in which a young girl learns the names of healing herbs from her grandfather.

In 2003, UNESCO recognised the Kallawaya culture as part of the world's heritage. The decision brought money and attention. A small school now offers lessons in the language every Saturday, and about forty children attend. Some of them are girls, which would have been impossible a generation ago.

Ana admits that the future is still uncertain. Most of her pupils use Kallawaya only in class, and they speak Spanish with their friends. "A language is not saved by a dictionary," she says. "It is saved when children argue in it."

Still, there are signs of hope. Last year, two of her former pupils, now university students, created a website where young people can practise the language and share recordings. It has more visitors from abroad than from Bolivia. "My grandmother would laugh," Ana says. "For centuries we kept this language secret. Now we want the whole world to hear it."

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

  7. 6.What did Ana take with her when visiting elderly speakers?
  8. 7.Why was Ana not supposed to know the language?
  9. 8.What made the healers change their minds?
  10. 9.What are most of the words in the dictionary?
  11. 10.When are lessons in Kallawaya held?
  12. 11.According to Ana, when is a language really saved?

  • Postopek: 1) preberi vprašanje in podčrtaj vprašalnico (why, how long, what, where); 2) poišči v besedilu del, ki se nanaša nanj (vprašanja si sledijo v istem vrstnem redu kot besedilo); 3) odgovori natančno na vprašanje: why → razlog, how long → čas, where → kraj.

Sleep somewhere different

Five guests describe a night in an unusual hotel.

A The Ice Hotel, Sweden

Everything here is made of ice and snow, including the beds, which are covered with reindeer skins. The temperature inside is minus five degrees, and you sleep in a special sleeping bag. I was afraid I would freeze, but I was surprisingly warm. The worst part was getting up in the night to go to the toilet, which is in a heated building outside. The hotel melts every spring and is built again by artists each winter, so no two years are the same.

B The Treehouse Hotel, Costa Rica

Our room was eight metres above the ground in the rainforest, reached by a rope bridge. At night we heard monkeys and frogs, and in the morning a toucan landed on our balcony. It is not for people who are afraid of heights or insects – a large spider shared our shower. The owners use solar energy and collect rainwater, and they plant a tree for every guest who stays.

C The Underwater Room, Tanzania

We spent a night in a room four metres below the surface of the Indian Ocean. The bedroom has glass walls, and fish swim past all night. We hardly slept, because we didn't want to miss anything. A small boat takes you there from the island, so you are completely alone. It was the most expensive night of my life, but it was a present for our wedding anniversary, and I don't regret a penny.

D The Capsule Hotel, Tokyo

I stayed in a capsule hotel during a business trip. Each guest has a plastic box just big enough to lie down in, with a light, a small TV and a curtain instead of a door. It sounds terrible, but it was clean, quiet and very cheap for central Tokyo. Bags are kept in lockers, and there are shared bathrooms. I wouldn't stay there for a week, but for one night it was perfect.

E The Prison Hotel, Slovenia

This hostel in Ljubljana used to be a military prison. The cells have been decorated by different artists, so each one is unique, but the bars on the windows are still there. The hostel is in a creative area full of galleries and clubs, so it can be noisy at night. Breakfast is served in what was once the prisoners' dining room.

Which paragraph …

  1. 0.Which hotel can only be reached across a bridge? (B)
  2. 1.Where was the guest's fear not confirmed?
  3. 2.Which hotel is rebuilt every year?
  4. 3.Which hotel takes action to protect the environment?
  5. 4.Where did the guests choose not to sleep?
  6. 5.Which stay was a celebration?
  7. 6.Which hotel is good value for its location?
  8. 7.Where does the guest suggest that a short stay is best?
  9. 8.Which hotel has a different design in every room?
  10. 9.Which hotel may disturb guests' sleep because of its surroundings?

1. A
2. A
3. B
4. C
5. C
6. D
7. D
8. E
9. E

Can insects help us fight plastic pollution?

Every year, the world produces more than four hundred million tonnes of plastic, and only a small part of it is recycled. Most ends (0) in landfills or in the sea, where it can take hundreds of years to break down. Scientists have been searching for a solution for decades, and some of them now believe the answer may be surprisingly small.

In 2017, a Spanish scientist named Federica Bertocchini was looking after her bees (1) she noticed something strange. She had removed some wax moth larvae from her hives and put them in a plastic shopping bag. After a short time, the bag was full (2) holes. The larvae, which normally feed on beeswax, had been eating the plastic.

Bertocchini and her colleagues began to investigate. They discovered that the larvae produce a substance in their saliva (3) breaks down polyethylene, one of the most common and most difficult plastics to destroy. In laboratory tests, the substance changed the plastic in just (4) hour, a process that would normally take years.

Since then, other researchers have made similar discoveries. In Australia, scientists found that a type of beetle larva, sometimes called the "superworm", can survive (5) a diet of polystyrene, the white material used in packaging. In Japan, a team discovered bacteria that can digest the plastic used to make drinks bottles.

Does this mean that the problem of plastic will soon be solved? Unfortunately, it is not (6) simple. Nobody suggests releasing millions of insects into rubbish dumps. (7), scientists hope to identify the chemicals that the insects and bacteria use and then produce them in large quantities in factories. These could one day be used in recycling plants (8) turn waste plastic back into raw materials.

There are still many questions to answer. Researchers need to make (9) that the process does not produce any harmful substances, and it must be cheap enough (10) compete with making new plastic. "We are at the very beginning," says Bertocchini. "It could take ten years (11) more before this technology is used on a large scale."

Many environmentalists also warn (12) relying too much on such discoveries. If people believe that science will clean up the mess, they may be less willing to change their habits. The best solution, they say, is still to use (13) plastic in the first place.

Bertocchini agrees. "Nature has given us an interesting tool," she says, "but it (14) not a magic wand. We have to stop producing so much waste." Still, she admits that she looks at her bees differently now. "Science often begins with an accident," she says, "(15) you are curious enough to notice it."

Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: v vsako vrzel napisati eno besedo. Navadno manjkajo slovnične besede: členi (a, the), predlogi (in, on, at), vezniki (although, because), oziralni zaimki (who, which, that), pomožni glagoli (have, is, did), primerjave (as, than).
  • Postopek: preberi celo poved; ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka. Nato preveri ustaljene zveze (depend on, used to, as … as).
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove slovnično pravilo ali ustaljeno zvezo, ki zahteva prav to besedo. Kjer je več pravilnih rešitev, so navedene vse (ločene s poševnico).
  • Pasti: dve besedi v eni vrzeli; beseda, ki se pomensko ujema, a slovnično ne (who za stvari, that za vejico).

2. of

Oziralni zaimek za stvar (a substance) v vlogi osebka.
4. an / one
»in just an hour« – nedoločni člen pred samoglasniškim glasom (hour se izgovori brez h).
5. on
»survive on a diet of« = preživeti ob prehrani s.
6. that / so
»it is not that simple« = ni tako preprosto.
7. Instead
Prislov na začetku povedi za nasprotno možnost: Instead, scientists hope …
8. to
Namen: used in recycling plants to turn waste … (da bi spremenili).
9. sure
Stalna zveza »make sure« = poskrbeti, prepričati se.
10. to
»cheap enough to compete« – za enough stoji to + nedoločnik.
11. or
»ten years or more« = deset let ali več.
12. against
»warn against + -ing« = svariti pred.
13. less
Primernik pri neštevnem samostalniku (plastic): use less plastic.
14. is
Osebek je »it« (tool): it is not a magic wand.
15. if
Pogoj: Science begins with an accident if you are curious enough to notice it.

Read the text below and change the words in brackets so that they fit in the gaps. Write your answers in the spaces provided. There is an example at the beginning: Gap 0.

Harriet Quimby: the woman who flew across the Channel

In 1911, flying was still a new and dangerous adventure, and almost all pilots were men. That year, an American journalist called Harriet Quimby became the first woman in the United States to earn a pilot's (0) (LICENSE).

Harriet was a (1) (SUCCESS) writer before she ever saw an aeroplane. She worked for a popular magazine in New York, where she wrote theatre reviews, travel stories and articles about women's (2) (INDEPENDENT). In 1910 she attended an air show and decided (3) (IMMEDIATE) that she wanted to fly.

At that time, many people believed that women were too (4) (EMOTION) to control a machine. Harriet ignored them. She took lessons at a flying school on Long Island, often at dawn, when the air was calm. She also designed her own flying suit, made of purple satin, which was both practical and (5) (FASHION).

Her greatest (6) (ACHIEVE) came on 16 April 1912, when she became the first woman to fly across the English Channel. The weather was foggy, and she had to rely completely on her compass, which she had only learned to use the day before. After about an hour, she landed on a beach in France, where fishermen carried her on their shoulders in (7) (CELEBRATE).

Unfortunately, her success received little (8) (ATTEND). The day before her flight, the Titanic had sunk in the Atlantic, and the newspapers were full of the disaster. Her story appeared only on the inside pages.

Just three months later, Harriet died in a tragic accident at an air show near Boston. Her plane suddenly tipped forward, and she and her (9) (PASS) fell into the water. Neither of them was wearing a seat belt, which was not yet (10) (COMPULSION).

Harriet was only thirty-seven, but her short career was (11) (INCREDIBLE) important. She showed that women could be pilots, and she wrote articles encouraging them to see flying as a possible (12) (CAREERS). Many female pilots of the next generation, including Amelia Earhart, described her as an (13) (INSPIRE).

Today, she is remembered in museums and on a US postage stamp. Her life proves that (14) (COURAGEOUS) and curiosity can change history, even when the world is not ready to (15) (NOTICEABLE).

(Vadbeno besedilo Učilnica.com)

Example: 0. licence / license
naloge.rezultat:
1. successful
2. independence
3. immediately
4. emotional
5. fashionable
6. achievement
7. celebration
8. attention
9. passenger
10. compulsory
11. incredibly
12. career

14. courage

naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: besedo v oklepaju spremeniti tako, da se slovnično in pomensko prilega vrzeli (besedotvorje).
  • Postopek: 1) ugotovi, katera besedna vrsta manjka: za členom ali svojilnim zaimkom (the, its) samostalnik; pred samostalnikom pridevnik; ob glagolu ali pridevniku prislov; 2) preveri, ali je potrebna nikalna predpona (un-, in-, ir-, dis-) ali množina.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga pove, katera besedna vrsta mora biti na tem mestu in katera pripona (-tion, -ness, -ful, -ly …) ali predpona jo tvori.
  • Pasti: pravilna besedna vrsta, a napačen pomen (nikalnica); pozabljena množina; napačno črkovanje (begin → beginning).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. successful
Pred samostalnikom »writer« pridevnik: success → successful.
2. independence
Za »women's« samostalnik: independent → independence.
3. immediately
Prislov ob glagolu »decided«: immediate → immediately.
4. emotional
Za »too« stoji pridevnik: emotion → emotional.
5. fashionable
Vzporedno s »practical«: pridevnik fashion → fashionable.
6. achievement
Za »Her greatest« samostalnik: achieve → achievement.
7. celebration
Za »in« samostalnik: celebrate → celebration.
8. attention
»receive attention« = biti deležen pozornosti; attend → attention.
9. passenger
Za »her« samostalnik, oseba: pass → passenger.
10. compulsory
Za »was not yet« pridevnik: compulsion → compulsory (obvezen).
11. incredibly
Prislov pred pridevnikom »important«: incredible → incredibly.
12. career
Za »a possible« samostalnik v ednini: careers → career.
13. inspiration
Za »an« samostalnik: inspire → inspiration.
14. courage
Vzporedno s samostalnikom »curiosity«: courageous → courage.
15. notice
Za »ready to« stoji nedoločnik: noticeable → notice.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to an interview with Megan Lloyd, a volunteer with a lifeboat crew on the coast of Wales. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Interviewer: Megan, how long have you been a lifeboat volunteer?

Megan: Eleven years now. I joined when I was seventeen, which is the youngest age you're allowed to start. My uncle was a member of the crew, and I used to sit in the lifeboat station after school, listening to his stories.

Interviewer: What do you do when you're not on the lifeboat?

Megan: I'm a hairdresser. I have my own small salon in the town, and my customers are used to me running out in the middle of a haircut. When the pager goes off, I have about seven minutes to get to the station. Usually I leave a colleague to finish the job, but once I had to leave a woman with only half her hair cut!

Interviewer: What kind of calls do you get?

Megan: All sorts. In summer, it's mostly tourists – people on inflatable boats who get carried out to sea by the wind, or walkers who are cut off by the tide. In winter, it's more often fishing boats with engine problems. We go out about sixty times a year.

Interviewer: Is it dangerous?

Megan: It can be, but our training is very good. Every Tuesday evening we practise, whatever the weather. We learn first aid, navigation and how to work with a helicopter. The most important thing is that you trust the people next to you completely.

Interviewer: Can you remember your most difficult rescue?

Megan: Yes. Three years ago, a father and his two sons were sailing when their boat turned over in a storm. The waves were five metres high, and it was dark. We found the boys holding on to the boat, but the father had drifted away. We searched for almost two hours and finally saw the light on his life jacket. He was extremely cold, but he survived.

Interviewer: Do you get paid?

Megan: No, none of the crew is paid. The charity that runs the lifeboats is funded by donations from the public. People sometimes don't realise that – they think we're part of the coastguard.

Interviewer: What would you say to someone who wants to join?

Megan: You don't need to be a sailor or super fit. You need to be reliable, calm and willing to get up at three in the morning. And you need an understanding boss!

A lifeboat volunteer

  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem podčrtaj vprašalnice; med poslušanjem zapiši samo bistvo. Vprašanja si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Sprejmejo se tudi drugačne besede z enakim pomenom.

naloge.besedilo:
You will listen to two speakers, a writer and a scientist, talking about Mary Shelley's novel Frankenstein. You will hear the recording twice. Now read the task.

Posnetek prebere bralnik v brskalniku (angleški glas). Poslušaj ga dvakrat.
Besedilo posnetka (odpri šele po reševanju)

Presenter: Today we're discussing Frankenstein, which was first published more than two hundred years ago. Clare, as a writer, what do you find most surprising about the book?

Clare: That Mary Shelley was only eighteen when she started writing it. She was on holiday near Lake Geneva in 1816, a summer when it hardly stopped raining because of a volcanic eruption on the other side of the world. The guests were stuck indoors, so the poet Lord Byron suggested that everyone should write a ghost story. Most of them gave up, but Mary didn't.

Presenter: Tom, you're a biologist. Does the science in the novel make any sense?

Tom: Surprisingly, it was based on real experiments. At that time, scientists were using electricity to make the muscles of dead animals move. Some even tried it on the bodies of executed criminals, and audiences watched in horror as the faces twitched. Mary Shelley had heard about these experiments, so the idea of bringing a body back to life was not pure fantasy for her readers.

Presenter: Most people imagine the monster as a large green creature with bolts in his neck.

Clare: Yes, but that comes from the films of the 1930s, not from the book. In the novel, the creature is intelligent and sensitive. He teaches himself to read by secretly listening to a family through a hole in a wall, and he reads poetry and history. He only becomes violent after everyone rejects him because of his appearance.

Tom: And people often forget that the creature has no name. Frankenstein is the scientist, not the monster.

Presenter: Why is the book still relevant today?

Tom: Because it asks a question that we face all the time in science: just because we can do something, should we? Victor Frankenstein creates life, but he refuses to take responsibility for what he has made. When I teach students about genetic engineering or artificial intelligence, I often start with this book.

Clare: For me, it's a book about loneliness. The creature says that he is wicked because he is miserable. I think every teenager who has felt like an outsider can understand that.

Presenter: If you could ask Mary Shelley one question, what would it be?

Clare: I'd ask her whether she felt sorry for the creature or for Victor. I've read it five times, and I still can't decide.

Talking about Frankenstein

As you listen to the recording, decide whether the following statements are true (T) or false (F).

  1. 0.Frankenstein was published over two hundred years ago. (T)
  2. 1.Mary Shelley began the novel when she was a teenager. T / F
  3. 2.The summer of 1816 was unusually sunny. T / F
  4. 3.Lord Byron suggested a writing competition. T / F
  5. 4.The science in the novel had no connection with real experiments. T / F
  6. 5.The green monster with bolts comes from the book. T / F
  7. 6.In the novel, the creature learns to read on his own. T / F
  8. 7.The creature is called Frankenstein in the book. T / F
  9. 8.Tom uses the book when he teaches students. T / F
  10. 9.Clare has decided who she feels more sorry for. T / F
naloge.rezultat:
1. T
2. F
3. T
4. F
5. F
6. T
7. F
8. T
9. F
naloge.razlaga:
Kako rešiš to nalogo in zakaj so rešitve take
  • Kaj zahteva naloga: med poslušanjem odločiti, ali je trditev pravilna (T) ali napačna (F).
  • Postopek: pred poslušanjem preberi trditve in podčrtaj ključne besede (števila, imena, nikalnice, always/never). Trditve si sledijo v vrstnem redu posnetka.
  • Zakaj je odgovor pravilen: razlaga navede, kaj je govorec rekel. Trditev je F, če se v eni podrobnosti razlikuje od posnetka (drug čas, druga oseba, drug razlog).

Spodaj je pri vsaki postavki rešitev in razlaga, ki pokaže, kje v besedilu ali posnetku je odgovor in katero pravilo velja.

1. T
Ko jo je začela pisati, je imela osemnajst let.
2. F
Skoraj neprestano je deževalo zaradi izbruha vulkana.
3. T
Predlagal je, naj vsak napiše zgodbo o duhovih.
4. F
»it was based on real experiments« z elektriko.
5. F
Podoba izhaja iz filmov iz tridesetih let.
6. T
Sam se je naučil brati, ko je skrivaj poslušal družino.
7. F
Bitje nima imena; Frankenstein je znanstvenik.
8. T
Pri genskem inženirstvu ali umetni inteligenci pogosto začne s to knjigo.
9. F
»I still can't decide.«
